item.title: 円が158円台前半に下落－強い指標でドル全面高、利上げ継続との見方
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 23日のニューヨーク外国為替市場で、ドルが主要通貨に対して全面高となり、円は対ドルで9月3日以来の安値をつけた。米総合購買担当者指数（PMI）が2021年以来およそ5年ぶりの高水準となり、連邦準備制度（FRB）が利上げを継続するとの見方が強まった。

円は一時、0.6%安の1ドル＝158円40銭まで売られ、200日移動平均線の158円45銭に接近した。先週18日に、日本銀行がレートチェックを実施したとの報道が伝わる前につけていた158円05銭の安値水準を超えて円安・ドル高が進んだ。

一方、ブルームバーグ・ドル・スポット指数は0.6%上昇し、7月30日以来の高水準を付けた。今月に入ってからは1.4%上昇している。

この日は金利が急上昇した。強いPMI統計に加え、原油高や低調な入札を受けて国債売りが加速。大半の年限で利回りが約20年ぶりの高水準に上昇した。

バンク・オブ・アメリカ（BofA）の為替ストラテジスト、アレックス・コーエン氏は「ファンダメンタルズは一段のドル高を示唆している」と指摘。「PMIの上振れで米経済の底堅さが改めて意識された。夏場に見られた米経済指標の弱含み傾向は後退し、FRBの利上げ観測は他国・地域よりも根強い」と述べた。

ドルを巡るセンチメントは改善が続いており、先高観が根強い。FRBが3年ぶりの利上げに踏み切った後も、当局者はインフレに対するタカ派姿勢を維持している。原油高と底堅い経済指標を背景に、短期金融市場は年内に少なくとも0.25ポイントの追加利上げを織り込んだ。10月の利上げ確率は50%を上回っている。

INGのストラテジスト、フランチェスコ・ペソレ氏は「相場を支配しているのはFRBだ。FRB高官のタカ派発言だけでも、ドル需要を維持するには十分だ」と指摘した。

過去10年の傾向では、9月最終週はドルが最も上昇しやすい。ブルームバーグの集計によると、この期間の週間騰落率（中央値）は、1年を通じて最も高かった。最終週に当たる21日から始まる今週も、ドルはこれまで0.8%上昇しており、今年も過去と同じ傾向をたどっている。

item.title: GCash owner Mynt secures over 20 cornerstone investors for potentially biggest Philippine IPO
item.description: Mynt, the parent of Philippine mobile wallet GCash, has lined up more than 20 cornerstone investors including BlackRock and T. Rowe Price for its planned initial public offering, according to a preliminary prospectus seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Karen Lema
item.content:encoded: Mynt, the parent of Philippine mobile wallet GCash, has lined up more than 20 cornerstone investors including BlackRock (BLK.N) and T. Rowe Price (TROW.O) for its planned initial public offering, according to a preliminary prospectus seen by Reuters. The IPO could raise up to 80.3 billion pesos ($1.3 billion), making it the largest share sale on record in the Philippines if priced at the top end of the range. It would surpass Monde Nissin's 55.89 billion peso IPO in 2021. The offering would provide a much-needed boost to the Philippine equity market, where companies have raised just $227.1 million through equity capital markets deals so far this year, according to LSEG data. Cornerstone investors have agreed to buy 36.5 billion pesos of shares in the offering, the preliminary prospectus dated September 22 showed. They include Capital Research and Management Company, Citadel Multi-Strategy Equities Master Fund Ltd, FIL Investment Management (Hong Kong), HSBC Global Asset Management, International Finance Corporation, Lazard Asset Management, among others. Domestic cornerstone investors include ATRAM Trust Corporation, BPI Asset Management and Trust Corporation, China Bank Capital Corporation, among others, the preliminary prospectus showed. Cornerstone investors are large institutions that commit to buying shares before an IPO opens to the public. Their commitments would account for nearly 68.8% of the shares on offer, excluding any shares sold under an overallotment option. Mynt plans to sell up to 8.03 billion shares at up to 10 pesos each. An overallotment option covering up to 1.2 billion additional shares could increase the deal size to about 92.3 billion pesos, according to the preliminary prospectus. At the top of the price range, Mynt would be valued at about 669 billion pesos. The company said proceeds from the sale of new shares would be used to expand its digital financial services business, develop products and for general corporate purposes. The offer period is scheduled to run from October 6 to October 12, according to the preliminary prospectus. The final price will be set after the close of the offer, with trading on the Philippine Stock Exchange expected to begin on October 20. ($1 = 62.6650 Philippine pesos)

item.title: Trump, Venezuela's Rodriguez discuss debt overhaul, Rubio says
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez discussed restructuring the South American nation's billions of dollars in sovereign debt, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump and Venezuela's interim [USN:L6N3Y508S TEXT:"President Delcy Rodriguez"] discussed restructuring the South American nation's [USN:L8N41R217 TEXT:"billions of dollars in sovereign debt"], US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday. The brief meeting at a reception Trump hosted late on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly came during Rodriguez's [USN:L6N45E138 TEXT:"first trip to the US"] since American forces captured then-President Nicolas Maduro in a January raid. The meeting is the latest sign of a rapid thaw in US-Venezuela ties since Maduro's removal. Washington is backing efforts to reconnect Venezuela with international lenders and support an economic recovery after years of default, sanctions and isolation. "There's a lot that needs to be fixed in order for Venezuela to be successful," Rubio told reporters. "Debt restructuring is key to that." Rubio said Venezuela likely faces one of the world's biggest sovereign debt workouts. He said Washington wanted to help, but that the process "has to be done in the right way." Venezuela announced in May it would begin [USN:S0N4040KU TEXT:"restructuring its external debt"], which has been in default since 2017. The government and state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela together have about $60 billion in defaulted bonds outstanding. Analysts estimate total liabilities, including arbitration awards and accrued interest, could reach $150 billion to $200 billion. Venezuela has not published full debt data for years, while US sanctions imposed in 2017 largely shut it out of Western financial markets. POLITICAL CHANGE Rubio said Washington also pressed for political change. Critics say Washington has sidelined the Venezuelan opposition, dropping demands for free elections in favor of oil and investment deals with the interim government. "We made that point that in the end, for this project to be successful, it culminates in a free and fair election," Rubio said. Some [USN:L1N4411IQ TEXT:"US lawmakers"] have also called for elections, amid criticism that the Trump administration has failed to extract meaningful democratic concessions from Rodriguez's government. Rodriguez arrived in New York on Monday with a delegation [USN:L1N45D0KY TEXT:"holding talks"] with US officials, multilateral lenders and companies on energy, mining and debt, sources said. The head of the [USN:L6N45E117 TEXT:"Inter-American Development Bank"] has been working to secure approval for a $2.5 billion loan for Venezuela, Reuters reported on Tuesday, despite resistance from some board members. Though small relative to Venezuela's overall obligations, such a loan would mark a major step toward restoring international lending.

item.title: Four US Republicans call for Trump to release Taiwan security funds
item.description: Four of US President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans called on his administration on Wednesday to release more than $15 billion in stalled national security assistance for Taiwan, as he prepared to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping for a three-day visit to Washington.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Four of US President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans called on his administration on Wednesday to release more than $15 billion in stalled national security assistance for Taiwan, as he prepared to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping for a [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"three-day visit"] to Washington. Xi [USN:L4N45D00S TEXT:"is expected"] to press Trump to halt Taiwan arms sales altogether during his visit to Washington, sources briefed on the matter told Reuters. US Senators Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, the former Senate majority leader, John Cornyn of Texas, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Thom Tillis of North Carolina wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth expressing concern about the funds. The letter cites the State Department's failure to move ahead with $300 million in foreign military financing Congress appropriated for Taiwan, the Defense Department's failure to obligate $1 billion and the administration's decision to withhold approval for a $14 billion package of foreign military sales to the island. "We are concerned by President Trump's description of Taiwan as 'a very good negotiating chip' in engagements with Xi Jinping and the Chinese Communist Party," the letter said. "It is difficult to imagine how the United States might credibly project influence deterrence in the Indo-Pacific if the price of keeping up diplomatic appearances is denying our partners key deterrent capabilities," the letter said. The State and Defense departments did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the letter. Rubio, speaking to reporters in New York and asked about Taiwan arms sales, said the administration had to balance broader needs. "I know everyone's focused on Taiwan, but I want you to focus globally for a moment. If we sell you something, we don't have it anymore. Now, we may be able to make it in the future, but we don't have it right now," he said. CHINA VIEWS TAIWAN AS TOP PRIORITY China regularly describes the issue of Taiwan, which Beijing views as its own territory, as its most sensitive and important diplomatic issue, and has repeatedly called for arms sales to stop. The US is bound by law to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself. The Trump administration in December approved an $11 billion arms package to Taiwan, the largest ever. However, a second package, worth some $14 billion, has been on hold for months. After a [USN:P8N3ZT02P TEXT:"May summit in Beijing"] with Xi, Trump said he was holding it in abeyance and described it as a "very good negotiating chip." Trump's fellow Republicans in Congress rarely question his administration's actions publicly. Three of the senators who signed Wednesday's letter — McConnell, Cornyn and Tillis — are leaving the Senate at the end of this year, with only Murkowski remaining.

FAST

Sept 22 - A rise in Japanese bond yields is creating a "reverse carry" opportunity for overseas investors as Bank of Japan interest-rate hikes make the traditional yen-funded carry trade less compelling, Rong Ren Goh, fixed income portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments, said on Wednesday. Japanese asset prices have swung sharply since the US Federal Reserve and BOJ raised rates within two days of each other last week, with a decades-long era of ultra-cheap yen funding potentially giving way to a new dynamic where Japan's own bonds become the more attractive trade. Buying ultra-long Japanese government bonds and hedging yen exposure back into dollars or another developed-market currency could potentially give investors higher yields versus comparable bonds in their home markets, Goh told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. "The 30-year Japanese government bond above 4 per cent, when swapped in any developed-market currency in the world, including the dollar, gives you an FX-hedged yield 100 to 200 basis points higher than the base currency equivalent," he said.

Goh said the traditional yen-funded carry trade - in which investors borrow cheaply in the Japanese currency to buy higher-yielding foreign assets - is no longer a "no-brainer", as markets expect Japan's policy rate to eventually reach around 2 per cent from 1.25 per cent currently. He expects the reverse carry trade to gain broader appeal as investors become more confident of a stabilisation in Japanese bond prices following a selloff that started in 2022. Positioning data showed the net yen long position in the week to September 15 jumped to its highest since July 2025. A sharp move lower for the yen after Friday's 25-bp BOJ rate hike that came with two dissents, which investors interpreted as a dovish tilt at the Japanese central bank, was contained by a report that authorities conducted rate checks in the currency market. The yen is currently up 1.2 per cent versus the dollar month-to-date. Pointing to Japan's steepening yield curve - where the gap between 2- and 30-year JGB yields is more than 200 bps compared with an average of around 80 bps in other core developed markets where curves are flattening - Goh said buying dollar bonds no longer offered "any compelling carry play", even if the differential between U.S. and Japanese interest rates remained wide. Goh said Eastspring - which manages $291 billion in assets - is adding shorter-dated dollar-denominated bonds, while favouring the ultra-long end of the Japanese curve where the firm is gradually building exposure through high-quality corporate and Samurai bonds as it seeks "additional credit spread over and above JGBs to enhance carry further". Samurai bonds are yen-denominated debt issued by foreign governments or companies. Eastspring began 2026 with a relatively "underweight" position on the yen due to uncertainty over Japan's fiscal and monetary policies, but moved to a more neutral stance around August as currency intervention risk became more meaningful, Goh said. item.title: イラン、外交再開へ米に条件提示 ホルムズ海峡航路や制裁停止など
item.description: [国連／ドバイ ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[国連／ドバイ ２３日 ロイター] - イラン外務省の報道官は２３日、米国に対し外交再開の条件を伝えたと明らかにした。

報道官によると、イランは２２日、国連総会の合間に仲介役のカタールを通じ、２時間にわたり米国とメッセージを交換し、条件を提示した。条件には、ホルムズ海峡の沿岸国であるイランとオマーンが合意した同海峡の安全航路の受け入れ、経済「テロ」や海上封鎖を含む米国による対イラン措置の停止、凍結資産の解除、あらゆる戦線での戦闘終結が含まれるという。

これに先立ち、イラン高官は、敵対行為の終結に向けたイランの提案に対する米国の対応を精査していると明らかにした。また、両国の立場には依然多くの隔たりがあるものの、外交交渉は続いていると述べた。同高官によると、２２日の米・イラン間接協議では、ホルムズ海峡の再開や米国による対イラン海上封鎖の解除などが議題となった。

item.title: US, China agree to extend trade truce by two months, work on bigger deal, Bessent says
item.description: The United States and China have agreed to extend by two months a trade truce that was due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The United States and China have agreed to extend by two months a trade truce that was due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday. Bessent made the remarks on Fox News hours after his second meeting in four days with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to prepare for [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"a summit"] between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. "We met today to see if we could do a bigger deal as opposed to just a series of smaller things," the Treasury chief said, noting that the two-month extension of the trade truce agreed in Busan, South Korea in May would give the two sides "more time to see what we can do on the economic front." Bessent told reporters earlier that Beijing had raised the prospect of a more expansive US-China trade deal during 12 hours of talks on Sunday, but gave no details of its potential scope. Wednesday's meeting lasted about 90 minutes, Treasury said. Asked if a deal could be negotiated by January 10, Bessent told Fox News that was not yet clear, adding Washington was also pressing China to "be a bit more fulsome" in meeting its commitments under the existing deal in coming months. He said Beijing was meeting its requirement to buy 25 million tons of soybeans, but was lagging on its pledge to buy $17 billion in other agricultural goods. US officials last week said the delivery of rare earths by China was also lagging. Thursday's summit - the second of potentially four meetings between Trump and Xi this year - could see some announcements on the two countries goal of taking tariffs off $30 billion in non-critical goods, on financial services and agricultural purchases, Bessent said. "Given that this could be a historic year where the leaders meet up to four times -- this being the second meeting, in Shenzhen and then in Miami -- we're open to the idea of just continuing the Busan arrangement or examining the bigger deal," Bessent told reporters earlier. "We're fine with both, and we're going to do what's best for the American people." In a post on X, Bessent called the discussions substantive and said Treasury was focused on securing meaningful commitments that protected American workers, farmers and businesses while advancing US economic and national security interests. Bessent said he met He at the World Bank headquarters in Washington to clear up some "unfinished business" ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, adding that the Trump administration wanted strategic stability based on "reciprocity and fairness." Bessent, He and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer [USN:L1N45B04Y TEXT:"met in New York on Sunday"] in an effort to tee up potential trade and artificial intelligence agreements for the two leaders to consider. Bessent called those talks successful, saying both sides had agreed to launch a communications "hotline" for notifying each other about AI safety incidents. China's response to the AI hotline plan was unclear, with state news agency Xinhua acknowledging only that the two sides discussed AI. US-China analysts say expectations on AI cooperation are low due to a lack of mutual trust on the technology and because neither side has expressed serious interest in slowing down development. In fact, Trump has said the opposite, that he would not "stifle" AI growth and would maintain the US lead over China in what he now calls "super intelligence." The Busan "economic detente" dramatically lowered bilateral tariff rates that had escalated to triple digits after tit-for-tat retaliation over Trump's tariff hikes last year. China also had agreed to restore the flow of rare earth magnets and other critical minerals that it had severely restricted.

FAST

NEW YORK, Sept 23 : The US dollar rallied to its highest level in nearly two months on Wednesday as investors' expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike grew, while oil prices jumped after Iran cast doubt on progress in peace talks. Since the central bank's rate hike of 25 basis points last week to the 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent range, several Federal Reserve officials have flagged the possibility of more rate increases if inflation does not cool. On Wednesday, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said the US central bank took an important step last week to "recalibrate" short-term borrowing costs to bring down inflation, and will likely need to deliver further interest rate hikes. "It's a rate story right now," said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman in London.

"What's driving the dollar higher is a follow through from the hawkish Fed hike that we got last week and that's just given the dollar some renewed momentum. This week there hasn't been much data, or policy relevant data, but what was interesting is the comments from Fed officials, they're basically all toeing the same line that more tightening is in the pipeline." The dollar extended gains after S&P Global said its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month, its highest since July 2021, after a 56.0 reading in August, powered by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.51 per cent to 101.06 after hitting 101.23, its highest since July 29. Expectations the Fed will hike rates by at least 25 basis points at its October meeting climbed after the data and were last at about 70 per cent, according to LSEG data, up from roughly 53 per cent before the release. MIDDLE EAST TENSIONS LIFT OIL Further fueling gains in the greenback was a rise in oil prices, after Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said in an interview with state TV that as long as Iran's conditions are not met, the Strait of Hormuz would not be reopened and there would be no negotiations. In addition, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran and the United States remain far apart on how to end their war but diplomacy must continue, after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure. Hopes that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly could lead to a resolution to the seven-month-long Iran war had helped push oil prices lower since reaching a four-month high in mid-September, but have since reversed course this week. Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank needs to "be careful" and may need to treat the current energy shock as a source of persistent inflation rather than expect it to dissipate on its own. EURO WEAKENS, YEN UNDER PRESSURE The euro was down 0.51 per cent at $1.1389 and on pace for its third straight daily decline and biggest drop in a week. Earlier S&P Global Flash Euro Zone Composite PMI Output Index data showed the region's economy is showing unexpected signs of health even as conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine drive up energy costs for firms and households. Investors are also waiting for a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with the superpowers at odds over trade, technology and the Iran war. The dollar strengthened 0.17 per cent to 6.71 versus the offshore Chinese yuan. The Japanese yen weakened 0.52 per cent against the greenback to 158.19 per dollar as traders gird for any signs of intervention after the Bank of Japan's rate hike to a 31-year high last week fell short of reassuring investors that more increases may be on the way. Japanese markets are closed for a holiday and this period of lower liquidity makes it more likely that authorities intervene, according to analysts.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 米ロ外相が会談、ルビオ氏「双方が限定停戦に関心」 ロシア慎重姿勢
item.description:
Tom Balmforth Antoni Slodkowski Simon Lewis
[ニューヨーク／モスクワ／国連 ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Tom Balmforth　Antoni Slodkowski　Simon Lewis

[ニューヨーク／モスクワ／国連　２３日　ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は２３日、ロシアのラブロフ外相と国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで会談した。会談後、ロシアとウクライナの双方が穀物関連施設やエネルギー関連施設を対象とする限定的な停戦に関心を示していると述べたほか、ロシアのプーチン大統領が２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）首脳会議への招待を受け入れることを期待するとし、プーチン氏が出席すればトランプ米大統領と会談する機会になるとの認識を示した。

ウクライナは、ロシアが今冬も発電施設や暖房施設を標的にする可能性を懸念しており、エネルギーインフラへの攻撃停止や黒海の海上輸送に関する安全保障を求めている。ルビオ氏はラブロフ氏との会談後に記者団に対し「ロシアとウクライナの双方が穀物とエネルギーを巡る限定的な停戦に関心を示している」と述べた。ただ「実現は容易ではない」とも指摘。エネルギー関連施設への攻撃が双方の戦術上の中核になっていることで停戦実現が難しくなっているとの認識を示した。

ロシアはエネルギー施設などに限定した停戦などを巡る取り決めに応じる用意があるとの考えを公に示しておらず、ルビオ氏の発言がラブロフ氏との会談で何らかの進展があったことを意味するのか、現時点では明らかになっていない。

＜ラブロフ氏、「特別軍事作戦」目標達成継続と表明＞

ロシア外務省もラブロフ氏がルビオ氏と会談したと発表。ウクライナと中東の情勢や、米ロ関係の改善など幅広い課題について「詳細な意見交換」を行ったとした。

また、ラブロフ氏はウクライナと「欧州の支援国」との連携のほか、ウクライナによる国境を越えた攻撃について言及。「ウクライナによる破壊的な行動や民間人、国境を越えるインフラ施設への意図的な攻撃について言及した」とし、こうした攻撃が「世界のエネルギー市場の不安定化につながっている」と伝えた。

同時に、ロシアはウクライナでの「特別軍事作戦」の目標達成に引き続き取り組む姿勢を表明。これには、ロシアがウクライナ全面侵攻の「根本的な原因」と位置付ける問題を考慮した形での解決も含まれるという。

ラブロフ氏はこのほか、米ロ関係の「早期改善」の必要性を強調し、将来的な経済協力拡大の可能性にも言及。「そのためには『懸案事項』の解消と両国の在外公館の正常な運営回復に向けた率直な対話が必要だ」とし、「事実上没収された米国内のロシア資産」の返還が必要になるとの認識を示した。

ラブロフ氏はこの日、ロシア・ウクライナ戦争を討議する国連安全保障理事会の会合に出席。会合で行った演説で、「欧州は停戦による時間稼ぎを望んでいるに過ぎない。目的はウクライナに武器供与を続けることにある」と述べ、ロシアには一時停戦を受け入れる考えがない可能性を示唆した。

＜ゼレンスキー氏、黒海海上停戦案を支持＞

ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領はこの日、国連総会に合わせて開催された「クリミア・プラットフォーム」首脳会合で行った演説で、エジプト、インド、トルコが提案した黒海の海上停戦案を受け入れる用意があると表明。対応はロシア次第になるとの認識を示した。

ゼレンスキー氏によると、会合でエジプト、インド、トルコが黒海での商船の安全な航行を回復するための選択肢を提示。「ロシアの回答を待っている」とし、「ロシアも緊張緩和に向けた真剣な措置を取れば、ウクライナは黒海の安全な航行と食料安全保障の確保に向けて準備ができている。どこかから始めなければならない」と語った。

黒海ではロシアとウクライナの双方による船舶や港湾インフラへの激しい攻撃を受け、貨物輸送がほぼ停止している。

[ニューヨーク　２３日　ロイター] - ライト米エネルギー長官は２３日、気候問題で足並みが揃わない場合、米国は国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）からの離脱を検討する可能性があるとの考えを示した。

Octave Klaba, founder and Chairman of French web-hosting and server provider OVH Group, attends a debate during the MEDEF summer forum "La Rencontre des Entrepreneurs de France, La REF" in Paris, France, August 27, 2026. REUTERS/Stephanie Lecocq

FAST

Sept 23 : OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba on Tuesday estimated operators of Europe's proposed AI gigafactories would need annual sales of 300 million euros to 400 million euros just to break even on facilities built around fast-depreciating graphics chips.  Klaba said a proposed 200-million-euro public commitment to buy AI services over five years was too small to underpin the scale of private investment required and said focus on national markets prevented OVHcloud from joining existing French consortia.  The EuroHPC program is seeking industry consortia to build and operate up to seven AI gigafactories: large computing facilities for training, fine-tuning and running AI models. "Any national strategy is doomed to failure: there are simply not enough customers to make investments of this size profitable. In our view, national demand is too weak and we must operate on a European scale," he said.

Klaba said the public sector would buy 40 million euros of computing services a year, while an operator would spend at least 600 million euros for chips alone. "The numbers don't add up," he said.  He estimated a gigafactory would need 300 million euros to 400 million euros in annual revenue to break even, making the public order worth only 10 per cent-15 per cent of required turnover.

item.title: 米総合ＰＭＩ、9月は5年ぶり高水準 新規受注急増も供給網圧迫
item.description:
Lucia Mutikani
[ワシントン ２３日 ロイター] - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表した９月の米総合購買担...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米総合ＰＭＩ、9月は5年ぶり高水準　新規受注急増も供給網圧迫 0:03 配信

2025年12月、ニュージャージー州ロビンズビルにのアマゾン施設で撮影。REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

Lucia Mutikani

[ワシントン ２３日 ロイター] - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表した９月の米総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は５８．４と、前月の５６．０から上昇し、２０２１年７月以来の高水準となった。新規受注の急増が押し上げ要因となった。一方で、堅調な需要がサプライチェーン（供給網）を圧迫し、物価上昇につながっている実態も浮き彫りとなった。

指数はサービス業、製造業ともに上昇した。ＰＭＩは５０が景況拡大・縮小の分岐点。Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルは、今回の結果について年率換算で約５％の経済成長率と整合的との見方を示した。同時に、未処理の受注残高やサプライチェーンの遅延が急増しているとし、「操業能力の不足を示しており、それが価格上昇につながっている」と指摘した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフビジネスエコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は「製造業とサービス業の両方で活況を呈している」と指摘。その上で、「この成長には、新型コロナのパンデミック（世界的大流行）を除けば、調査開始以来約２０年で最も深刻なサプライチェーンのボトルネックが伴っている」と述べた。

新規受注指数は５８．２と、８月の５５．２から上昇し、２２年３月以来の高水準を記録した。サービス業、製造業の双方で上昇した。設備稼働率や将来の事業成長を示す重要な指標である受注残も２２年５月以来の高水準に達した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルによると、各企業は受注残の増加に対応するため採用を拡大しているものの、適切な人材の確保に苦慮しているとの報告が増えている。

ウィリアムソン氏は「未完了受注の積み上がりは、今後数カ月間の生産高と生産能力の一段の拡大につながる可能性を示している。一方で、企業の価格決定力が高まっていることも示しており、インフレ見通しにとっては懸念材料だ」と述べた。

投入物価指数は６６．４と、前月の５９．９から急上昇し、２２年１０月以来の高水準となった。支払価格指数も上昇し、とりわけサービス部門での上昇が目立った。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 コラム：ＡＩ相場はドットコム・バブルの再来か、強気派に分がある理由 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 最終更新: 9/24(木) 0:03 ロイター

item.title: Bangladesh to buy 11 more Boeing jets as it seeks closer US trade ties
item.description: Bangladesh will buy a further 11 aircraft from Boeing , officials said on Wednesday, expanding national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines' planned orders to 25 jets as Dhaka seeks closer trade ties with the US amid concerns over tariffs on its exports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bangladesh will buy a further 11 aircraft from Boeing (BA.N) , officials said on Wednesday, expanding national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines' planned orders to 25 jets as Dhaka seeks closer trade ties with the US amid concerns over tariffs on its exports. The agreement, scheduled to be signed in New York on Wednesday, is part of Bangladesh's efforts to boost imports from the United States, ease pressure from a roughly $6 billion trade imbalance and reduce the risk of tariff increases that could hurt its export-driven economy, particularly the garment sector. The US ambassador to Bangladesh, Brent Christensen, confirmed the Boeing purchase in a Facebook post, calling it another "win-win" for US-Bangladesh relations. Boeing said Biman ordered 11 787 Dreamliner and 737 MAX airplanes. The order includes five 787-10 and six 737-8 jets, Boeing said in a statement. Biman is renewing its fleet, aiming to expand capacity and improve connectivity. The latest order follows a $3.7 billion [USN:L4N41D0TD TEXT:"deal"] signed in April for 14 Boeing aircraft, including 10 Dreamliners and four 737 MAX 8 jets, with deliveries scheduled between 2031 and 2035. European rival Airbus remains in contention, with a government-appointed technical committee reviewing a proposal to acquire 10 aircraft.

item.title: Trump y presidenta encargada de Venezuela discuten reestructuración de la deuda, dice Rubio
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, discutieron la reestructuración de la deuda soberana de la nación sudamericana, dijo el miércoles el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, discutieron la reestructuración de la deuda soberana de la nación sudamericana, dijo el miércoles el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio. La reunión informal, celebrada durante una recepción organizada por Trump a última hora del martes al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU, tuvo lugar durante el primer viaje de Rodríguez a Estados Unidos desde que las fuerzas estadounidenses capturaron al entonces presidente Nicolás Maduro en una incursión en enero. Las conversaciones marcaron un paso más en la rápida mejora de las relaciones entre Estados Unidos y Venezuela desde la salida de Maduro; Washington respalda los esfuerzos para reconectar a la nación sudamericana con los prestamistas internacionales y apoyar una recuperación económica tras años de impago, sanciones y aislamiento. "Hay mucho que arreglar para que Venezuela tenga éxito", dijo Rubio a periodistas. "La reestructuración de la deuda es clave para ello". El secretario estadounidense señaló que Venezuela tenía "probablemente la mayor deuda soberana del mundo pendiente de reestructuración" y afirmó que Estados Unidos quería ayudar, pero que "debe hacerse de la manera correcta". En mayo, [USN:L6N41R17A TEXT:"Venezuela anunció que iniciaría"] la reestructuración de su deuda externa, que está en situación de impago desde 2017. El monto total de los bonos en mora —correspondientes tanto a la deuda soberana como a la de la estatal Petróleos de Venezuela (PDVSA)— asciende a unos 60.000 millones de dólares. Los analistas estiman que el pasivo total, incluidos los laudos arbitrales y los intereses acumulados, podría oscilar entre los 150.000 y los 200.000 millones de dólares. Venezuela lleva años sin publicar estadísticas exhaustivas sobre su deuda, y las sanciones impuestas en 2017 la aislaron en gran medida del sistema financiero occidental. CAMBIO POLÍTICO Rubio afirmó que Washington también presionó por un cambio político. Los críticos dicen que Washington ha marginado a la oposición venezolana, dejando de lado las demandas de elecciones libres en favor de acuerdos petroleros y de inversión con el gobierno encargado. "Hicimos hincapié en que, al final, para que este proyecto tenga éxito, debe culminar en unas elecciones libres y justas", dijo Rubio. Algunos legisladores estadounidenses también han pedido elecciones, en medio de críticas de que la administración Trump no ha logrado obtener concesiones democráticas significativas del Gobierno de Rodríguez. [USN:L6N45D0SR TEXT:"Rodríguez llegó a Nueva York"] el lunes con una delegación que ha estado manteniendo conversaciones sobre energía, minería y deuda con funcionarios estadounidenses, prestamistas multilaterales y empresas, dijeron las fuentes. El director del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo, Ilan Goldfajn, dijo esta semana que está trabajando para lograr la aprobación de un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela, pero se ha enfrentado al rechazo de algunos miembros de la junta del prestamista. Una operación del BID por 2.500 millones de dólares, aunque eclipsada por la sustancial deuda general de Venezuela, marcaría un hito en el financiamiento de la recuperación en las primeras etapas.

item.title: Zelenskiy warns of painful winter for Russia if energy truce talks fail
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy warned Moscow at the United Nations on Wednesday that Ukraine would strike back and make the coming winter deeply painful for Russia, if the two sides cannot agree a truce on energy attacks before the cold sets in.
item.dc:creator: Tom Balmforth, Antoni Slodkowski, Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy warned Moscow at the United Nations on Wednesday that Ukraine would strike back and make the coming winter deeply painful for Russia, if the two sides cannot agree a truce on energy attacks before the cold sets in. Ukraine and its allies are racing to secure limited agreements on energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping before winter, fearing renewed Russian strikes on power and heating facilities, while Moscow continues to show little interest in wider negotiations to end the war. "Ukrainians understand that this winter could be very harsh for us. But in response, we will have no choice but to make it painful for Russia too," Zelenskiy told the UN General Assembly during the annual gathering of world leaders in New York. Though Russia has a far bigger arsenal of missiles which it has used to pound its enemy throughout the war, Ukraine has developed and used thousands of long-range drones to strike back at Russian warehouses, port infrastructure and oil refineries. "That’s exactly why we say that de-escalation steps are needed before winter," Zelenskiy said, calling for more robust diplomacy and noting the potential sway that Chinese President Xi Jinping could have on Russian President Vladimir Putin. China's Xi, who did not attend the United Nations gathering, was due on Thursday to hold White House talks with US President Donald Trump, with whom Zelenskiy met on Tuesday to discuss a ceasefire on energy-related targets. NO SIGN OF CHANGING RUSSIAN POSITION Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov held talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday, after which Rubio said Ukraine and Russia had both voiced an interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy-related targets. There was no immediate sign of any movement in the Russian position, however. A Russian Foreign Ministry statement said that at the meeting it had "reaffirmed its unconditional commitment to achieving the objectives of its special military operation," the phrase that Moscow uses to describe its war in Ukraine. Addressing the 15-member Security Council on the sidelines of the annual UN gathering of world leaders, Lavrov indicated that Moscow would not countenance any temporary cessation of hostilities. "Europe, whatever it thinks, just wants to get a pause, and it wants to use it to pump the Kyiv regime with weapons," he told a council session focused on the war in Ukraine. Britain, France and Denmark's top diplomats used their speeches to deliver strong condemnations of Russia's war, warning variously of dangerous escalation and the spike in civilian deaths this summer. 'WE ARE WAITING FOR RUSSIA'S RESPONSE' Zelenskiy used his address to the General Assembly to single out Putin's role in driving the war, repeatedly describing him derisively as "patient zero" and "the one from whom this idea of war keeps spreading further". "That is why 'patient zero' must be stopped. He must be denied the space to act – and the space to spread this evil further," he said. Zelenskiy told leaders at a "Crimean Platform" summit on the sidelines of the UN that Kyiv was ready for a maritime truce in the Black Sea based on proposals such as those put forward by Egypt, India and Turkey. "We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere," he said. Top wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa that count on the Black Sea region for wheat have been finding it hard to secure supplies. Global wheat prices have soared.

item.title: 習氏訪米、中国企業代表団は同行しない見通し＝関係筋
item.description: [北京 ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２３日 ロイター] - 中国の習近平国家主席による今週の訪米に、中国企業の代表団が同行しない見通しであることが分かった。関係筋２人が明らかにした。理由は明らかになっていない。

関係筋の１人は、米政権には他の優先事項があると述べた。一方、別の関係筋によると、米当局者は中国軍と関係があるとみられる中国企業の代表が訪問に参加することを望んでいないという。

中国外務省報道官は定例記者会見で、中国企業代表団の同行に関する質問に対し、「その件に関する情報は持ち合わせていない」と述べた。

ロイターは先週、関係筋の話として、習氏の訪米に同行する中国の経済界トップの人選が進められており、米規制当局の厳しい審査や規制措置の対象となっている企業が、市場アクセス拡大を求めて代表団に加わる可能性があると報じていた。

item.description: [ニューヨーク ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ニューヨーク　２３日　ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は２３日、イランとの合意には一定期間にわたる多大な取り組みが必要になるとの見方を示した。また、トランプ大統領には軍事的な選択肢もあると記者団に語った。

ルビオ氏は、イラン問題について「われわれは（ホルムズ）海峡が問題であることを理解している」とした上で、「われわれは、引き続き海峡の防衛と開放を維持する」と述べた。

また、「イランとの合意が成立するなら、一定期間にわたる多大な取り組みが必要になるだろう」とした上で、トランプ大統領には軍事的選択肢を含め、多くの選択肢があると述べた。

item.title: First US-Iran talks in months raise hopes for progress despite no concessions
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated through mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

First US-Iran talks in months raise hopes for progress despite no concessions

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated through mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and other delegates attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, on Sep 23, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Mike Segar)

FAST

UNITED NATIONS/DUBAI: The first shuttle talks between the United States and Iran in months raised hopes on Wednesday (Sep 23) that the adversaries could make progress towards ending the Middle East war, although neither side spelled out any change in its position. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated through mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, the first such contacts since an interim ceasefire agreement collapsed in July. "Steve and Jared had a very productive meeting today with mediators of Iran," US President Donald Trump said. "I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal. It's what we're hearing from everybody." Earlier, Trump had told the UN General Assembly in a speech that he had to decide whether to make a deal with Iran or " annihilate " it. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was due to address the gathering on Wednesday. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Tehran had engaged with the United States through a Qatari mediator in New York and conveyed conditions, including an end to the war on all fronts and a halt to US "acts of aggression". Some Iranian state media had earlier reported that Araghchi and Witkoff had met, but Iranian officials clarified to Reuters that it was not face-to-face. Araghchi met the prime minister of Qatar, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, one of the main mediators at previous talks. The contacts offered the first diplomatic opening in months after negotiations broke down in July and fighting resumed across the region. Since then, the two sides have repeatedly exchanged fire , although Trump has stopped short of a full-scale resumption of US strikes after military commanders warned munitions stocks were running low. IRAN HARDLINERS RESIST DIPLOMATIC MOVES The diplomatic contact in New York caused backlash in Iranian media associated with hardliners. An opinion piece run by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, associated with the Revolutionary Guards, said Araghchi was wrong to have contacts with Witkoff and Kushner, "a major gift to Trump", as Iran had already conveyed its terms. Iranian sources told Reuters the delegation had been ordered not to meet the Americans face-to-face by the Supreme National Security Council, a body that includes figures selected by Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, the supreme leader, who has yet to appear in public since replacing his father killed on the war's first day. One Iranian journalist covering the visit told Reuters that some hardliners viewed the trip to New York itself as an insult to the memory of the slain leader, Ali Khamenei.

Related:

Iran 'toughened' conditions for ending war after US deal collapse: Guards spokesman

Iran attacks US targets despite Trump threats

OIL PRICES HOLD NEAR TWO-WEEK LOW Still, the diplomatic opening helped keep oil prices near two-week lows. Brent crude hovered around US$100 a barrel after surging earlier this month when Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched a major offensive, threatening traffic through the Red Sea, an alternative Saudi export route. The war, launched by Trump in February alongside Israel as "Operation Epic Fury", has lasted nearly seven months, killing thousands of people, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region - particularly to Lebanon and more recently to Yemen. Trump repeated previous assertions that the war could end around the time of November's US midterm elections, though he has not explained why. An interim agreement reached in June, signed by Trump and Pezeshkian, would have given Iran its main demands: lifting financial sanctions and unfreezing assets in return for talks on limiting its nuclear programme. But that deal unravelled within weeks over shipping rules in the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas before the war. Iran wants to exert control and collect fees from ships that use it, which Washington rejects. In the latest reported attack in the strait, Britain's UKMTO maritime security agency said a cargo ship had been hit by projectiles, causing two casualties among the crew. The crew had been evacuated, and the ship was on fire and adrift. Despite near-daily attacks, traffic through the strait has picked up in recent weeks. Oil producers pay shipping companies fees of as much as a quarter of a cargo's value to take the wartime risk of sailing through the strait with transponders switched off, before transferring crude to other vessels on the far side. Exports from the United Arab Emirates have already recovered to pre-war levels, and Saudi Arabia has sold 60 million barrels of Gulf oil for both this month and next, to be delivered beyond the strait off the coast of Oman. Nevertheless, a third of Gulf oil is estimated to be missing from global supplies. Shortages have particularly hit refined products such as diesel, causing inflation, pushing up interest rates and hurting Trump's Republicans ahead of the elections.

Source: Reuters/rk

item.title: Florida fund sues New York Times over alleged anti-Israel bias, demands records
item.description: Florida's state-run public pension fund and a conservative think tank sued the New York Times on Wednesday, seeking materials to determine whether the company's board is letting the newspaper promote biased editorial coverage against Israel.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Stempel
item.content:encoded: Florida's state-run public pension fund and a conservative think tank sued the New York Times (NYT.N) on Wednesday, seeking materials to determine whether the company's board is letting the newspaper promote biased editorial coverage against Israel. According to a petition filed in a New York state court in Manhattan, a series of factual errors in Times reporting on various subjects supports a reasonable inference that the board has allowed journalistic standards to be "weaponized within the company to serve the personal agendas of unchecked editors." The State Board of Administration of Florida (SBA), which oversees the Florida Retirement System Trust Fund, and the National Center for Public Policy Research said they are not second-guessing the newspaper's editorial judgment, but want assurances the board is making sure the Times follows its editorial standards and avoids "biased and unreliable" reporting. Both petitioners are Times shareholders, and said New York state law entitled them to inspect its records but the newspaper refused. "This lawsuit has no merit and was brought for an improper purpose," Times spokesperson Charlie Stadtlander said. "Although it is positioned as a corporate governance petition to inspect the company’s books and records, it is a transparent attempt to exert agenda-driven pressure against an independent media organization, level false allegations of bias and chill journalism protected by the First Amendment," he added. "We will defend against the suit vigorously.” BATTLES OVER ISRAEL COVERAGE, INDEPENDENCE Many media, including the Times, have faced accusations they have skewed coverage against Israel following the October 2023 outbreak of war in Gaza . Wednesday's petition also escalates a growing battle nationwide over journalistic independence, including US President Donald Trump's decision last week to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. Those [USN:FWN45C04L TEXT:"outlets sued Trump"], saying the ban was unconstitutional and violated their First Amendment rights. The Florida pension fund serves more than 1.2 million retirees, and had about $235.7 billion of assets under management as of August 31, according to its website. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis and Attorney General James Uthmeier, both Republicans, are SBA trustees. “The Times says unreliable journalism is a material risk," Uthmeier said in a post on X. "We asked if the board oversees its standards, and they refused to produce a single page." WHISTLEBLOWER CLAIMS Wednesday's petition is based in part on claims by an unnamed former Times newsroom employee who worked there for a decade, and began complaining as early as 2019 about its alleged widespread culture of anti-Israel bias. The petition said the Times repeatedly brushed off the whistleblower's complaints, including when a supervisor told her "it's not your job to be the ombudsman" and a human resources representative suggested she "go find a place whose values align with yours." It also said the Times appears to have not followed through on Times publisher and board chair A.G. Sulzberger's commitment in 2019 to update its "unconscious bias training" to include a direct focus on antisemitism. “We’re not trying to censor anyone," Steve Milloy, executive director of the think tank's Free Enterprise Project, said in an interview. "But if they want to go down as the paper of record, then there must be records backing up what they’re claiming.”

item.title: ＢｏｆＡ、英中銀利上げ予想に転換 半年で2回実施の見方
item.description: [２３日 ロイター] - バンク・オブ・アメリカ（ＢｏｆＡ）・グローバル・リサーチは、イングランド銀行（英中銀）が今...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＢｏｆＡ、英中銀利上げ予想に転換　半年で2回実施の見方 9/23 23:38 配信

2026年9月16日、英国ロンドンのイングランド銀行の建物。 REUTERS/Corey Rudy

[２３日 ロイター] - バンク・オブ・アメリカ（ＢｏｆＡ）・グローバル・リサーチは、イングランド銀行（英中銀）が今後半年間で２回の利上げに踏み切るとの見方を示した。エネルギー価格の上昇でインフレが長期化するリスクが高まっていることを踏まえたもので、同様の予想を打ち出す他社に続いた。

同社は、英中銀が１１月と２月にそれぞれ０．２５％ポイントの利上げを実施すると予想。従来は金利据え置きが続いた後、２０２７年１１月に利下げに転じるとの見通しを示していたが、これを撤回した。

見通し変更の背景には、先週の英中銀会合で政策当局者が、特に足元の原油・天然ガス価格の急騰に起因するリスクについて、より強い調子で言及したことがある。これを受けバークレイズ、ＵＢＳグローバル・リサーチ、Ｊ．Ｐ．モルガンも利上げを予想している。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場は英中銀が１１月に利上げする確率を６７％織り込んでおり、１２月にもさらなる利上げが予想されている。

ただ、ＢｏｆＡは見通しを修正したものの、市場は引き締めを過大に織り込んでいる可能性があると指摘。英中銀が２０２８年に利下げを開始するまでに利上げは２回にとどまり、最終的に政策金利は３．５％に戻るとの見方を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 9/23(水) 23:38 ロイター

Sept 23 : Alphabet-owned YouTube unveiled a slate of artificial intelligence tools, shopping updates and personalized viewer features on Wednesday at its annual Made on YouTube event in New York City. Here are some details: • The new creator tools include additions to YouTube Studio for feedback on video drafts, channel-matched thumbnails and testing up to three video cuts. • A Gemini-powered assistant in Shorts and YouTube Create will also help edit clips, trim pauses and sync music.

• The video platform is testing opt-in AI comment moderation that adapts to creators' preferences. It will also combine voice and facial detection in its likeness-protection tools. • The company will expand its YouTube Shopping affiliate program to 35 countries by year-end, with more than 1.3 million creators already enrolled. • Creators in India and Brazil will soon be able to tag Amazon products, while product tags will show localized offers to viewers in different markets. • YouTube will introduce Custom Feeds for U.S. users on web, mobile and TV, allowing them to save homepage tabs tailored to interests such as documentaries or DIY videos. • Its Ask YouTube feature will add shopping queries and follow-up questions, including product-comparison tables and voice commands for TV users.

item.title: アポロのプライベートクレジット、解約5%に再び制限－3四半期連続
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米オルタナティブ資産運用会社アポロ・グローバル・マネジメントは、プライベートクレジット・ファンドからの資金引き出しを3四半期連続で制限している。同社の投資家も、1兆8000億ドル（約285兆円）規模のダイレクトレンディング市場から資金を引き揚げる動きに加わっているもようだ。

約260億ドルの資産を運用するファンド「アポロ・デット・ソリューションズ」は22日、発行済み株式の14.7%相当の払い戻し請求を受け、償還を同5%に再び制限すると投資家に通知した。株主向け書簡で明らかにした。前期も16.8%の償還要求があった。

ブラックロックやクリフウォーターなど同業他社も、自社のプライベートクレジット・ファンドからの資金引き出しを引き続き制限している。融資の質や従来型ソフトウエア企業へのエクスポージャーを巡る懸念から、投資家が資金を引き揚げようとする中、今年は過去最大規模の解約の動きがプライベートクレジット市場を揺るがしている。

アポロ・デット・ソリューションズは7－9月期、総資金流入が約2億ドルだった。投資家が現金で受け取らず、新たな株式の購入に充てた配当金も含まれる。一方、株式の買い戻しに7億ドルを支払ったため、純流出額は約5億ドルと、純資産価値（NAV）の3%に上る見込みだ。同ファンドは、2022年の運用開始以来、年率8.2%のリターンを上げているとしている。

アポロによると、償還請求の大半は、以前の請求が全額満たされなかった投資家による再請求だった。書簡では、今年償還を求めた投資家は、今回の払い戻しにより、請求した資金の約75%を回収することになると説明した。

同ファンドは、未処理の買い戻し請求への対応を引き続き進めるとしたうえで、十分な流動性確保の手段を有しており、「必要に応じてレバレッジを若干高める」ことも可能だとしている。また、「より良好な市場環境の下で、運用会社が行った選択が、運用成績に表れ始めている」とも強調した。

item.description: [２３日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のバー理事は２３日、ＦＲＢが先週の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
バーＦＲＢ理事、追加利上げ必要との見方　「インフレ目標達成にリスク」 9/23 23:31 配信

2026年4月14日、バーFRB理事。REUTERS/Evan Vucci

[２３日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のバー理事は２３日、ＦＲＢが先週の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げを決めたことについて、インフレ抑制に向けて金利を「再調整」する重要な一歩を踏み出したと評価した。その上で、さらなる利上げが必要になる公算が大きいと述べた。

バー理事はシカゴ連銀の住宅取得能力に関する会合で行う予定の講演原稿で「われわれのインフレ目標達成に対するリスクは高まった一方、労働市場のリスクは後退した」と指摘した。

さらに、米経済成長は力強く、労働市場は堅調だが、インフレはＦＲＢの目標である２％を上回る水準にとどまり、明確に低下する方向には向かっていないと述べた。「私のメインシナリオでは、インフレを適時に目標まで押し下げるため、追加の政策調整が必要になる公算が大きい」と語った。

バー理事は年内に少なくともあと２回の利上げが必要と考えている可能性がある。

バー理事は先週の利上げに言及し、「経済の変化を踏まえると、われわれは適切な位置になく、正しい方向に調整を行ったと思う。ＦＲＢは最大限の雇用を支える持続可能で息の長い成長を支援したいと考えており、物価の安定はそのために極めて重要だ」とした。

バー理事の金融政策に関する発言は短く、講演の大半は住宅取得能力問題に充てられた。住宅取得能力は供給不足と住宅ローン金利の高止まりで一段と悪化している。

item.description: 米企業、インフレ見通しを引き上げ 金利上昇を懸念＝ＦＲＢのＣＦＯ調査 Reuters

item.title: 米企業、インフレ見通しを引き上げ 金利上昇を懸念＝ＦＲＢのＣＦＯ調査
item.description:
Howard Schneider
[ワシントン ２３日 ロイター] - 米国の企業財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は、今年と来年の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米企業、インフレ見通しを引き上げ　金利上昇を懸念＝ＦＲＢのＣＦＯ調査 9/23 23:18 配信

米ニューヨークで2025年11月撮影。REUTERS/Angelina Katsanis

Howard Schneider

[ワシントン　２３日　ロイター] - 米国の企業財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は、今年と来年のインフレ率が一段と高まると予想しており、金利上昇を最大の懸念材料の一つに挙げ始めている。連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が２３日公表した四半期調査から明らかになった。

財務幹部らは今年、価格を平均で５．３％引き上げる見通しを示した。第２・四半期時点の４．６％、年初時点の３．６％から上昇した。来年の価格引き上げ幅は平均４．５％と、第２・四半期時点の４．１％、年初の３．６％から上振れした。

最大の懸念事項としてインフレへの言及が少なくなった一方、「金融政策」に関する言及が最も多く、約２０％の企業が最大の懸念材料として挙げた。前回調査では１５％未満だった。

リッチモンド地区連銀のワデル副総裁は、財務幹部の景気全般に対する楽観的な見方は依然として強いものの、資金調達を巡る懸念が中小企業の見通しに影を落とし始めているとの見方を示唆。「課題がある場合、それは中小企業や資金繰りに制約のある企業で最も顕著だ」と述べた。

中小企業の約５分の１が、事業拡大計画の妨げになったり、コスト吸収を困難にしたりしていると回答した。企業全体では、今後６カ月間の設備投資は、半年前の見通しに比べ減少すると予想している。

設備投資を計画していない企業のうち、約４２％がその理由として「資金調達環境の悪化」や「現金確保の必要性」を挙げており、６カ月前の３２％から上昇した。

調査は８月１７日から９月４日にかけ、約５００社を対象にアトランタ地区連銀とリッチモンド地区連銀がデューク大学フクア経営大学院と共同で実施。これはＦＲＢによる先週の利上げ決定前、ＦＲＢの政策論議が利上げの可能性に傾き、投資家が借り入れコストの上昇に備え始めていた時期に当たる。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：出遅れ気味の米不動産株、持ち直し期待高まる 焦点：後退する米企業役員の多様性、トランプ米大統領の政策反映 コラム：「米国例外主義」なお健在、外国投資家のテック株流入持続が示唆 アングル：米株、下半期の上昇基調維持に多くの試練　ＡＩ投資から金融政策まで 最終更新: 9/23(水) 23:22 ロイター

[ドバイ ２３日 ロイター] - イラン国家安全保障最高評議会のモフセン・レザイ書記は２３日、国営テレビとのインタビューで、周辺国が米国に協力してイラン便の運航を停止させれば、イランはそれらの国の空港が機能しないようにすると述べた。

ベセント米財務長官は２１日、航空サービス提供業者に対する二次制裁を発動すると警告し、これによりイランの全航空会社が９月２３日に運航停止を余儀なくされるとの見通しを示していた。

レザイ氏はまた、イランの条件が満たされない限り、ホルムズ海峡は再開されず、交渉も行われないと述べた。

item.title: 米総合PMI、9月速報値は21年以来の高水準－新規受注や雇用が増加
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 9月の米企業活動は過去5年余りで最も速いペースで拡大した。堅調な需要を背景に、製造業とサービス業で新規受注や雇用が増加した。

雇用は4年余りで最も速いペースで増加した一方、投入価格の伸びは2022年以来の高水準となった。回答企業は主に燃料費や輸送費の上昇を要因に挙げ、多くの企業が賃金の伸び加速も指摘した。

S&Pグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフ・ビジネス・エコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は発表文で、「製造業、サービス業ともに企業活動は明らかに活況を呈している」と指摘。「ただ、こうした成長に伴い、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック（世界的大流行）期を除けば約20年に及ぶ調査の歴史でも特に深刻な部類に入るサプライチェーンの目詰まりが生じている。企業からは適切な人材の確保が一段と難しくなっているとの報告も増えている」と述べた。

サービス業の企業活動指数は58.7へ上昇し、2021年以来の高水準となった。雇用指数は2022年6月以来の高水準だった。

製造業の指数は57に上昇し、2022年以来の高水準。需要の指標となる新規受注は2022年4月以来の速いペースで拡大し、雇用の伸びも2021年2月以来の高水準となった。

一方、サプライヤーの納期は2022年半ば以来最も長期化し、原材料コストも高止まりしており、サプライチェーンへの圧力が続いていることを示した。

今年の米企業活動は、堅調な個人消費やAIを背景とした企業投資、国防支出に支えられている。S&Pグローバルの最新データは、イランとの戦争に伴うエネルギーコストの上昇やサプライチェーンの混乱にもかかわらず、力強い需要が企業活動を支えている状況を示している。

ウィリアムソン氏は、パンデミック後の経済再開局面を除けば、9月の企業活動の改善は「2015年初め以降で最大だ」と述べた。

原題：US Business Activity Expands at the Fastest Pace Since 2021 (1)（抜粋）

item.title: 原油は急反発、ディーゼル燃料は米輸出禁止措置の観測で大幅下落
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ニューヨーク原油相場は大幅反発。国際指標の北海ブレント原油先物は、1バレル＝100ドル台を回復した。前日までは5営業日続落していた。世界の燃料市場の混乱と、ホルムズ海峡で新たに発生した攻撃が材料視された。原油先物は依然、戦争前の水準を上回ってはいるものの、中東からの原油輸送を背景に、燃料相場に比べれば値動きは抑えられている。

米ディーゼル燃料先物は急落した。世界各地で主要な製油インフラがなお停止している。ホワイトハウスが輸出禁止を検討しているとの観測が広がり、市場を揺さぶった。

共和党議員の一部から今週、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止を求める声が上がり、トランプ米大統領も前向きな姿勢を見せていた。政治メディアサイトのポリティコは23日、ホワイトハウスがこうした措置を準備していると報じ、先物は一時7.5%下落して日中安値を付けた。ホワイトハウス当局者はこの報道は不正確だと述べたと、ロイター通信は報じた。

ディーゼルは今年に入り80%余り上昇している。米国の小売価格は過去最高水準に達しており、11月の中間選挙を前に消費者は不満を強めている。エネルギー価格の高騰は、インフレ抑制を目指す連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）をはじめとする中央銀行にとっても、頭痛の種となっている。

ディーゼル市場では中東とロシアからの供給が急減し、米国が主要な供給国となっている。原油市場では米国からの輸出が停止されるとの懸念が、サウジアラビアの原油輸出が回復するとの楽観を相殺した。

サウジは26日までに東西パイプラインの再稼働を目指すとしている。同国はペルシャ湾岸からの輸出についても、高いペースを維持しているもようだ。

米エネルギー情報局（EIA）によると、国内のディーゼル在庫は42万8,000バレル減少した。一方、オクラホマ州クッシングの在庫は200万バレル余り増え、5月以来の高水準となった。ただ、留出油の輸出は約3カ月ぶりの低水準に減少。この落ち込みを受け、輸出禁止が回避される可能性があるとの期待につながった。

item.title: 原油反発、ブレントは100ドル台－ディーゼル燃料の急騰が影響
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ニューヨーク原油相場は反発。中東からの原油輸送が回復するとの見方が広がる一方で、トレーダーは燃料価格の急騰を意識している。

国際指標の北海ブレント原油先物は1バレル当たり100ドル台を回復した。前日までは5営業日続落していた。トランプ米大統領が前日、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止案に前向きな姿勢を示したため、この日は欧州のディーゼル先物が急騰した。これが原油価格の上昇に弾みを付けていると、サクソバンクの商品戦略責任者、オーレ・ハンセン氏は指摘した。

ディーゼル市場では中東とロシアからの供給が急減し、米国が主要な供給国となっている。原油市場では米国からの輸出が停止される懸念が、サウジアラビアの原油輸出が回復するとの楽観を相殺した。

サウジは26日までに東西パイプラインの再稼働を目指すとしている。同国はペルシャ湾岸からの輸出についても、高いペースを維持しているもようだ。

それでもホルムズ海峡を巡るリスクは続いている。英国海運貿易オペレーション（UKMTO）によれば、同海峡を航行中に飛翔体の攻撃を受けた貨物船で火災が発生し、漂流している。

トランプ米大統領は前日、米・イラン代表が3時間にわたって協議したと明らかにし、「非常にうまくいった」と成果を強調したが、市場の反応は冷ややかだったと、サクソバンクのハンセン氏は指摘した。「解決につながる具体的な行動が双方から求められている」と同氏は述べた。

キャピタル・エコノミクスのエコノミスト、ハマド・フセイン氏によれば、ディーゼル燃料の輸出が禁止されれば、米国内のディーゼル価格はいったんは下落する可能性があるものの、国内で石油を輸送する能力に制約があるため、いずれ在庫が積み上がり、製油業者は生産削減を余儀なくされる。

ニューヨーク時間午前10時現在、北海ブレント11月限は前日比2.2%高の101.41ドル。ウェスト・テキサス・インターミディエート（WTI）11月限は同2.7%高い91.97ドル。

item.title: US business activity at more than five-year high; inflation pressures building
item.description: US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in September, fueled by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in September, fueled by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher. S&P Global said on Wednesday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month. That was the highest level since July 2021 and followed a reading of 56.0 in August. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. The rise in the PMI reflected strong gains in both the services and manufacturing sectors. The PMI was consistent with the economy growing at around a 5% annualized rate, S&P Global said. It also noted a sharp rise in work backlogs and supply chain delays, "pointing to a lack of operating capacity which fed through to higher prices." The Atlanta Federal Reserve's gross domestic product tracking estimate is running at a 5.1% rate. The economy grew at a 1.5% pace in the April-June quarter. "Business is clearly booming now in both manufacturing and services," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "However, this growth is being accompanied by some of the most severe supply chain bottlenecks seen in the near-two-decade survey history if the pandemic is excluded." The supply constraints mostly stem from the US-Israeli war with Iran, now in its seventh month. STRONG DEMAND ADDING TO INFLATION Chicago Fed President [USN:L6N45C08M TEXT:"Austan "][USN:L6N45D0L7 TEXT:"Goolsbee"] said on Monday supply shocks were proving more persistent, adding there was evidence that strong demand was now adding to the problem. That view was supported by the findings of the S&P Global survey. The survey's measure of new orders received by businesses raced to 58.2, the highest reading since March 2022, from 55.2 in August. The increase was across both services and manufacturing industries. Incomplete orders, a key indicator of capacity utilization and future business growth, increased to the highest level since May 2022. Though companies across manufacturing and services sectors boosted hiring to tackle the order backlog, S&P Global also noted increasing reports of problems finding suitable staff. "While this accumulation of uncompleted orders bodes well for the further expansion of output and capacity in the coming months, it also indicates that companies are developing more pricing power, and hence is a worry for the inflation outlook," said Williamson. The survey's gauge of prices paid by businesses for inputs jumped to 66.4, the highest reading since October 2022, from 59.9 in August. Both services and manufacturing businesses reported higher input prices. S&P Global noted that high raw materials prices in manufacturing were also often linked to supply shortages. It said suppliers' delivery times lengthened considerably on average, "with the incidence of supply chain delays the most widespread since July 2022." A measure of prices paid increased, with the sharpest gain in the services sector. Further gains are likely as [USN:L6N4580TA TEXT:"record high"] diesel prices will, among other things, boost the cost of transporting goods. The Federal Reserve last week raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"benchmark overnight"] interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range and flagged more hikes in the coming months.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Sept 23 : The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said Wednesday it is investigating startup Comma.ai after reports of five crashes of vehicles using its aftermarket driver-assistance devices involving three reported deaths and 11 serious injuries.  NHTSA said vehicles with Comma devices reportedly struck five stopped or slow-moving vehicles. Comma.ai says the devices that use open source software can allow for hands-free driving and reports more than 30,000 vehicles have logged 402 million miles with the devices. The system "can accelerate, brake automatically for other vehicles, and steer to follow the road/lane," Comma.ai says. The company could not immediately be reached for comment but says on its website that it requires "the driver to be alert, pay attention, and be ready to take over at all times."

NHTSA said it will review any other incidents involving the Comma.ai devices and obtain data to verify system status for each incident and evaluate system performance and safeguards. In 2016, NHTSA demanded that Comma.ai provide proof to regulators that its proposed device for self-driving cars would be safe, or risk having its sale blocked. The company at the time said in response it was redirecting its efforts to "other products and markets." The California Department of Motor Vehicles had also in 2016 sent Comma.ai a cease-and-desist letter. NHTSA and the National Transportation Safety Board have repeatedly investigated serious crashes involving failures of vehicles with advanced driver assistance systems to identify stopped or slow vehicles on highways. In March, the NTSB criticized Ford Motor's hands-free advanced driver assistance system BlueCruise for failing to ensure drivers were not distracted before they were involved in two fatal collisions. The Ford SUVs struck stationary vehicles at highway speeds in San Antonio and Philadelphia, killing three people in total, and there was no attempt to brake by either Ford driver. In 2023, Tesla recalled over 2 million vehicles in the US to better ensure drivers pay attention when using its Autopilot driver assistance system after NHTSA opened a probe after identifying more than a dozen crashes in which Tesla vehicles hit stationary emergency vehicles.

ＥＣＢ、エネルギー高波及なら追加利上げも＝アイルランド中銀総裁 9/23 22:41 配信

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのマクルーフ・アイルランド中銀総裁。米ワシントンで4月撮影。REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

[ダブリン ２３日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのマクルーフ・アイルランド中銀総裁は２３日、エネルギー価格の高騰が他の分野に波及すれば、ＥＣＢは再び利上げを迫られるとの見方を示した。ただ現時点では、こうした「２次的な」インフレ効果の兆候は見られないとの認識を示した。

同総裁は公共放送ＲＴＥとのインタビューで、「インフレ率は目標を上回っているが、価格に波及し始めるような２次的効果は見られない」と指摘。「もしそのような（エネルギー価格が高止まりし、他の分野に波及する）事態になれば、目標を達成するために再び行動を起こさなければならない」と述べた。

マクルーフ氏は今月、ＥＣＢが年内２回目となる利上げを決定した後、「大幅な」追加利上げは経済成長に打撃を与える恐れもあるとの見方を示していた。

item.title: US Energy Secretary Wright says diesel export ban won't work
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Wednesday said a US ban on diesel exports would not work and could push up gasoline and jet fuel prices, a stance at odds with President Donald Trump, who is backing the idea.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Wednesday said a US ban on diesel exports would not work and could push up gasoline and jet fuel prices, a stance at odds with President Donald Trump , who is [USN:L6N45E0WU TEXT:"backing"] the idea. Diesel prices have surged to record highs due to the US-Israeli war with Iran and the conflict in Ukraine , angering farmers and other users of the fuel ahead of the midterm elections in November that will decide control of Congress. "The blunt tool of banning diesel exports definitely doesn't work," Wright said at an event hosted by the Economist in New York. Average US diesel prices were $6.52 a gallon on Wednesday, up 76% from a year ago, according to AAA, a motorist advocacy group. "If you can't export the diesel that comes out of our refineries, you run out of places to store it, and you have to reduce US refining, which would put upward pressure on gasoline prices and jet fuel prices," Wright said. The Trump administration is open to any ideas on lowering fuel prices and will make policy announcements in coming days, he said. Wright said the administration was working with the refining industry to increase the supply of US diesel in a "simpler, voluntary, cooperative fashion, without using blunt instruments that would reduce refining throughput." He did not detail that plan and said no decisions have been made. "The Secretary remains fully aligned with the President in exploring all available options to lower energy prices," the Department of Energy said in a statement. Record fuel prices are a risk for Trump as his fellow Republicans seek to maintain narrow control of both chambers of Congress in the November 3 elections. With global diesel supplies tight and few obvious ways to quickly bring prices down, the administration is [USN:L1N45F0YF TEXT:"facing calls"] from Republicans in competitive races for action, putting fuel costs at the center of a broader political challenge for the party. The US oil and refining industry on Wednesday urged Trump to reject calls for a diesel export ban, saying restrictions would reduce refinery output and raise prices for gasoline and jet fuel. A letter signed by 36 industry and business groups, including the American Petroleum Institute, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers, Business Roundtable and US Chamber of Commerce, said US refiners are running at full capacity and producing more diesel than the country consumes. “Export bans would lead to less fuel production, tighter supplies, and rising costs for American families, farmers, and truckers," the letter states. RUN RATES While US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins has also raised the issue of high diesel prices with the president, other top US officials have opposed an export ban. US Interior Secretary [USN:L1N4560TC TEXT:"Doug Burgum"] said last week such a ban could lead to retaliatory action from countries that export fuel to the US, which could hurt states like California. Many energy analysts agree that a ban would risk boosting fuel prices. "The loss of export abilities would force many plants to cut run rates, and reduce their output of gasoline (and numerous other products) as well, which becomes counterproductive," analysts for TACenergy wrote in a note on Wednesday. US refineries were running at about 94% of capacity last week, according to the Energy Information Administration. A White House official said Trump "wants to see gas prices at the pump fall and is evaluating all the options on the table." Wright praised Trump's policy in Venezuela where the US is urging companies to expand production and return to operations there after US special forces in January captured the South American country's leader, Nicolas Maduro, and left his deputy Delcy Rodriguez in charge. Many companies are interested in investing in Venezuela to fix oil operations that have suffered over the last 20 years from neglect, corruption and US sanctions, Wright said. "Some of them will strike deals, and tens of billions of dollars are flowing." For other companies, "it won't work, and they'll invest elsewhere."

(Corrects to say Blockchain.com is a brokerage not an exchange, in first paragraph and third bullet point) By Elizabeth Howcroft Sept 23 : The New York Stock Exchange and crypto brokerage Blockchain.com will together explore creating crypto versions of US-listed stocks, Blockchain.com said in a press release on Wednesday. The partnership is the latest example of a mainstream stock exchange looking to cash in on tokenisation, which is the idea of creating blockchain-based tokens which represent or are pegged to assets such as stocks and bonds.

• Blockchain.com and NYSE announced a "strategic collaboration" to explore selling tokens representing NYSE-listed stocks and ETFs on blockchain, the technology behind cryptocurrencies. • The companies have not yet announced which countries the products will be sold in. • The companies also signed a data agreement, with NYSE's parent company Intercontinental Exchange distributing Blockchain.com's crypto market data and analytics, while the crypto brokerage will use NYSE data in its app. • "It’s a bet by both parties on where capital markets are heading," Blockchain.com said. • Blockchain-based stock tokens rarely offer buyers the same rights as traditional equities, and the buyer typically does not become a shareholder in the underlying company, raising concerns about investor protection. • Proponents say they enable more people to buy stocks and trade them outside of standard market hours. • Blockchain.com, based in London and Dallas, has already started selling tokenised stocks to customers in Europe, but a spokesperson for the company declined to comment on how many customers had bought them. • The US Securities and Exchange Commission unveiled an exemption that will allow platforms to sell blockchain-based versions of stocks and other securities, without having to follow many of the rules that apply to stock exchanges.

item.title: AI-based drug developer Basecamp valued at $800 million after $140 million funding round
item.description: Basecamp Research said on Wednesday it has raised $140 million in a Series C funding round that valued the AI-based drug developer at $800 million.
item.dc:creator: Puyaan Singh
item.content:encoded: Basecamp Research said on Wednesday it has raised $140 million in a Series C funding round that valued the AI-based drug developer at $800 million. The oversubscribed round was led by S32, with participation from Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio Capital Management, the NATO Innovation Fund, the Rockefeller Foundation and Singular, among other investors. Basecamp raised $60 million in its Series B round in October 2024, led by Singular. The company said it would use the latest funding to train a new generation of its EDEN biological foundation models and move a pipeline of AI-designed therapies toward clinical development. The London-based company will initially focus on therapies that reprogram patients' cells inside the body. The company said its EDEN technology could make cell therapies more customizable and easier to administer for cancer and autoimmune diseases, compared to current treatments that it said cost "hundreds of thousands of dollars per patient". Basecamp added it had demonstrated strong preclinical results across several types of therapies and diseases, but did not provide a timeline for starting clinical trials. EDEN is trained on Basecamp's proprietary genomic dataset, assembled through partnerships in more than 30 countries, and can generate potential drug candidates based on information about a disease, the company said. The company also appointed former Biogen (BIIB.O) executive Richard Pearce as chief business officer to expand its pharmaceutical partnerships.

Sept 23 : Private investment in space companies globally more than doubled to $23 billion in the year through June as the sector shifts toward proven businesses, according to British investment firm Seraphim and Relm Insurance on Wednesday. SpaceX's June IPO has reshaped the funding landscape for the sector, drawing in new investors as venture firms look for the next space company capable of a similar payoff. Investors are funneling capital toward companies that can show operational proof rather than early-stage promise, with the space economy moving from "hype to commercial reality", according to Relm Insurance. It said the companies attracting capital include Earth observation (EO), in-orbit manufacturing and satellite supply chains.

"EO is already an established category — the tech is well established, if still improving," said Andrew Bonwick, Relm's VP of Product Development. "The real value is in the analytics. Customers buying these services don't think of them as space services — they're sold on what they actually want: where are my ships, when should I plant my crops, is that refinery switched on, where's at risk of wildfire." Capital grew more selective toward Earth observation companies with visible revenue and experienced leadership, the report said. In-orbit manufacturing is still in its early days, held back by limited ways to launch and bring products back to Earth, with some companies merging while others struggle to grow beyond small pilot projects. Satellite supply chains have grown more complicated as production increases, pushing companies to bring more of their manufacturing in-house to control costs and reduce reliance on outside suppliers. Traditional insurance policies often don't fit these smaller, experimental space projects, creating demand for new types of coverage, the report said.

item.title: Passive investing? That S&P 500 index fund is basically a tech fund
item.description: Passive investors may be far more exposed to the AI trade than they realize. New data brings into sharp relief the risk that investors are, perhaps unknowingly, putting all of their eggs into the US technology basket.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: Passive investors may be far more exposed to the AI trade than they realize. New data brings into sharp relief the risk that investors are, perhaps unknowingly, putting all of their eggs into the US technology basket. Warnings about [USN:L1N45011B TEXT:"tech-sector concentration"] are nothing new, but the problem is intensifying just as the risks surrounding the artificial intelligence boom are multiplying. If you take into account the tech sector’s share of the S&P 500 (.SPX) market cap – which is within a whisker of June's record high – as well as the communications services sector and other big tech-centric companies, the broader tech universe now makes up more than half of the index's entire $70 trillion market value. The US stock market has rarely been this concentrated and narrow. Investors buying an index-tracking fund may think they're gaining exposure to the top US banks, retailers, energy firms and healthcare giants, as well as the famed tech and AI behemoths. But tech is now so dominant in the index that what they're buying increasingly resembles a tech fund with a few other sectors added on for appearance's sake. PASSIVE PUSH Passive investing itself arguably exacerbates the problem by pushing more money into already crowded trades – and passive investment flows have long dwarfed their active counterparts. US equity funds currently hold over $16 trillion in assets under management, based on funds that report at least weekly, according to Société Générale, and roughly 70% of that is now passively managed. These passive funds have attracted cumulative inflows of almost $3 trillion since 2019, while investors have pulled around $1 trillion from actively managed funds, SocGen analysts note. Even the concentration within the passive fund universe is rising rapidly. The three largest listed passive S&P 500 index exchange-traded funds (ETFs) – State Street SPDR (SPY.P) , iShares Core (IVV.P) , and Vanguard's VOO (VOO.P) – have nearly $2.7 trillion in assets under combined management. It's a near-constant, one-way flow. 'TOO CONCENTRATED FOR COMFORT' This concentrated bet is fine when tech is on the up, as has been the case for much of the past few years. The rising tide has – for the most part – lifted all boats. But it's [USN:L6N45C084 TEXT:"not all plain sailing"] for the AI revolution right now, with safety concerns and doubts over the technology's long-term economic viability recently bubbling to the surface. If these waters suddenly turn choppy, the pain will be felt far and wide. And [USN:L6N45716B TEXT:"more Americans than ever"] are in this boat. According to Federal Reserve figures released earlier this month, equities now account for almost 47% of US households' financial assets and 34% of total assets. Both are record-high levels. "We are not calling time on the AI cycle, but positioning has grown too concentrated for comfort, and the reward for looking beyond the crowded trade has rarely been clearer," WisdomTree's Aneeka Gupta argued last week. Ameriprise's Anthony Saglimbene echoed this on Monday, stressing the importance of "understanding the concentration of technology in your portfolio and diversifying inside and outside of that tech exposure." But diversifying out of tech is easier said than done. AI's footprint in all markets is expanding, whether that be in investment-grade credit, emerging markets or private markets. What should investors do? Everyone likes to think they will get to the exit in time, but history has proven that not everyone does. The stampede, if and when it comes, could be fierce. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. item.description: エチオピア北部で戦闘再燃、反政府勢力が空港掌握 Reuters

item.title: エチオピア北部で戦闘再燃、反政府勢力が空港掌握
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - アフリカのエチオピア北部ティグレ州の指導部は２３日、連邦政府との新たな戦争に入ったと表明した。ティグレ州と隣接するアファール州、アムハラ州で戦闘が発生し、４年前に結ばれた和平合意は崩壊した。

アビー首相の顧問は、反政府勢力のティグレ人民解放戦線（ＴＰＬＦ）がティグレ州内で連邦政府の管理下にあった空港を掌握し、隣接するアファール州とアムハラ州の政府軍拠点に対して「全面攻勢」を開始したとＸに投稿。エチオピア航空はティグレ州向けの運航を停止した。

エチオピアでは、２０２０─２２年にＴＰＬＦと連邦政府軍の間で内戦が起き、数十万人が死亡した。２２年１１月にプレトリア合意が締結されたが、数カ月前から対立が強まり、ＴＰＬＦは２１日、アビー政権打倒を目指し、エチオピア各地の武装組織６団体と同盟を結成したと発表していた。

ＴＰＬＦ主導のティグレ州政府は声明で「アビー・アハメドの独裁的かつジェノサイド的な政権が、ティグレの人々に対してさまざまな手段による侵攻を激化させたことを受け、ティグレ州政府はティグレ軍に反撃を指示し、防衛戦争に入ったと発表した」と述べた。
