item.title: 米企業業績、アナリストの見通しが弱気に－インフレと金利上昇懸念
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米企業の業績見通しを巡り、株式アナリストは数カ月ぶりに全体として弱気に転じた。インフレと金利上昇が利益に及ぼす影響への懸念が背景にある。

シティグループの指数によると、利益予想を引き下げたアナリストの数が23週間ぶりに、引き上げたアナリストを上回った。2021年9月以来最長となっていた上方修正優勢の流れが途切れた。

BNPパリバ・ウェルス・マネジメント・ドイツのシュテファン・ケンパー最高投資責任者（CIO）は「弱さの主な要因は、生活必需品と一般消費財の両方を含む消費関連、素材、金融だ。生活費の上昇とエネルギー価格の上昇が重なったことに直接関係しているとみられる」と分析した。

ウォール街のアナリストは、米企業の利益が今年大幅に伸びるとの見方におおむね自信を示しているものの、一部は目先の株式市場の見通しに懸念を示している。

モルガン・スタンレーのストラテジスト、マイケル・ウィルソン氏は今週、株式のバリュエーションがさらに低下し続け、エネルギー価格の一段の上昇によって金融政策が引き締められれば、S&P500種株価指数が最大7%下落するリスクがあると警告した。

経済協力開発機構（OECD）は23日のリポートで、2027年の世界のインフレ率は予想を上回るペースとなり、金融政策のさらなる引き締めが必要になるとの見通しを示した。米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）は物価上昇圧力に対応するため、今月、3年ぶりに政策金利を引き上げた。

原題：Analysts Snap Longest Run of US Earnings Upgrades in Five Years（抜粋）

item.title: Dramatic eviction of 87-year-old Madrid tenant spotlights Spain's housing crisis
item.description: Police evicted an 87-year-old woman on Wednesday from her Madrid home of more than seven decades despite hundreds of people protesting outside and the government criticising the eviction order, in a dramatic new flashpoint of Spain's housing crisis.
item.dc:creator: Corina Pons
item.content:encoded: Police evicted an 87-year-old woman on Wednesday from her Madrid home of more than seven decades despite hundreds of people protesting outside and the government criticising the eviction order, in a dramatic new flashpoint of Spain's housing crisis. After being given just 30 minutes to leave with only essential belongings, Maricarmen Abascal was eventually removed from the building on a stretcher accompanied by social services officials and driven away in an ambulance as supporters chanted "Maricarmen, you're not alone!" and "Murderers!" The case highlights mounting pressure on long-term tenants in major Spanish cities, where soaring rents, gentrification and a shortage of affordable housing have fuelled social and political tensions. The apartment in the capital's affluent Retiro neighbourhood had been acquired by an investment fund that sought a steep increase in her rent. Maricarmen's lawyer, Beatriz Duro, said court officials and representatives of the investment fund, Urbagestion, had refused to suspend the eviction despite a pending court filing, humanitarian appeals and evidence that public authorities were working to secure alternative accommodation. Urbagestion did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Duro said an anonymous individual had offered to cover the rent payments, but the landlord declined to sign a new lease. "I've lived here for 71 years and I don't want to leave," Maricarmen told reporters on the eve of the eviction. The eviction sparked tense scenes outside the building, where police forcibly removed protesters blocking the entrance. Reuters witnesses saw officers dragging and pushing demonstrators, lifting some by their arms and legs as they cleared the doorway. Spain remains divided over how to tackle a worsening housing affordability crisis. The left-wing coalition government has pushed for stronger tenant protections and wider rent controls, but has struggled to secure backing in a divided parliament, while the conservative-led Madrid regional government has favoured a more market-oriented approach. Madrid's regional leader, Isabel Diaz Ayuso, is embroiled in a scandal regarding her government's purchase, via a public real estate agency, of a €6.3 million ($7.2 million) luxury penthouse. The opposition accuses Ayuso of seeking to use the property as her personal residence while bypassing public spending and transparency rules, which she denies. Referring to that scandal, activists at Wednesday's eviction shouted: "Ayuso's penthouse for Maricarmen!" ($1 = 0.8763 euros)

item.title: トルコ、ファンド不正渦中の投資会社会長ら逮捕－元外務省高官も
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 巨額の投資家資金を消失させた株式ファンドの破綻を捜査しているトルコ当局は、渦中にある証券会社の創業者を逮捕した。

トルコのNTVが報じたところによると、同国投資会社テラ・ヤティリム・メンクル・デエルエルのエムレ・テズメン会長および同社取締役会メンバーのケレム・アルキン、エムレ・アルキン両氏、別の企業幹部1人を当局が23日朝方にそれぞれ逮捕した。テズメン氏は19日から身柄を拘束されていた。

ケレム・アルキン氏はトルコ外務省を昨年退職したばかりで、2021－24年にはトルコの経済協力開発機構（OECD）常駐代表を務めた。同氏の弟であるエムレ氏は著名なエコノミストで、全国放送のテレビ局に定期的に出演するなどコメンテーターとしても活動していた。

NTVによると、テラと並び混乱の震源地となっているプスラ・フィナンス・ホールディングのセルダル・トゥルハン会長も同じ捜査の一環で逮捕された。

当局はこれまでに複数の金融会社の幹部に関連する資産を凍結し、その幹部の一部およびその配偶者、近親者について、資産を減らすような取引に制限を課したと、国営アナドル通信は報道。資産の国外移転の有無を見極めるため、2024年以降の国外送金と暗号資産に関するデータも要請したという。

問題のファンドは浮動株が少なく株価をつり上げやすい銘柄に集中投資して好パフォーマンスであるかのように見せかけ、数十万人に上る個人投資家の資金を引きつけていた。だが、投資先の銘柄は流動性に乏しいため、集中的な解約請求に応じられず行き詰まった。

このファンドの取引を検証した金融専門家によると、保有株を担保に短期資金を借り入れ、同じ銘柄に再び投資しているケースもあった。トルコの法相はこの手法を「ねずみ講詐欺のようなもの」と断じた。

23日の取引では、トルコ株の代表的な指標であるイスタンブール100指数は一時1%上昇。より幅広い全株指数はほぼ横ばいで推移しているが、テラを含む40以上の銘柄は依然として値幅制限いっぱいの10%安に沈んでいる。

Sept 23 : India government-backed 48.50 billion rupees ($506.58 million) line of credit to the Maldives became effective on August 27, 2026, the Reserve Bank of India said on Wednesday, paving the way for individual project-level credit agreements under the facility. Here are some details: • The RBI said that the facility will be deployed through individual credit agreements with minimum value of 5 billion rupees each • Under the agreement, at least 75 per cent of the value of goods, works and services under contracts financed through the facility must be supplied by sellers from India, while the remaining 25 per cent may be sourced from outside India.

item.title: 米住宅ローン金利が急上昇、節目の7%を上回る－2年超ぶり高水準
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国の住宅ローン金利が、この2年余りで最も高い水準に上昇した。米住宅市場は物件価格の高止まりと販売低迷で既に不振にあえいでいるが、ローン金利上昇がさらなる重しとなる。

全米抵当貸付銀行協会（MBA）が23日に発表したデータによれば、30年物固定住宅ローン金利は18日終了週に、前週比15ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）上昇して7.12%となった。2024年5月以来の高水準だ。

当初5年間は固定金利でその後変動金利となるタイプの住宅ローン金利は、13bp低下して6.10%となった。

住宅ローン金利は2月以降、上昇基調にある。2月末にイラン戦争が勃発したことを受けてエネルギー価格が押し上げられ、インフレ懸念が再燃した。米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）は先週、物価上昇圧力を抑えるため、2023年以来となる利上げを実施した。

住宅ローン金利の上昇を受け、ローン申請をする人の数も減っている。MBAによれば、住宅購入のための申請指数は前週比0.8%低下して、4週間ぶりの低水準。借り換えのための申請指数は2.6％低下し、2025年2月以来の低い水準となった。

不動産仲介レッドフィンのチーフエコノミスト、ダリル・フェアウェザー氏は「7%という数字は重要だ。目にする最初の数字が7%では、心理的な影響を及ぼす」と述べた。

同氏は金利上昇によって住宅価格の伸びは抑えられる一方、販売の低迷は続くとみている。

米中古住宅販売件数は8月に減少し、25年6月以来の低い水準となった。米住宅建設業者の業況感は9月に1年ぶりの低水準となり、22年12月以来の最低に並んだ。金利上昇が住宅購入をためらわせているほか、建設資材や燃料の値上がりでコストも膨らんでいる。

原題：US Mortgage Rates Surge Above 7% to a More Than Two-Year High（抜粋）

item.title: McDonald's expects inflation to keep traffic flat, shares dip after $8.5 bln capex plan
item.description: McDonald's warned on Wednesday that industrywide customer traffic in key markets would likely remain flat as long as inflation remained elevated, sending its shares down as much as 6.5% even as it unveiled an $8.5 billion franchisee support plan and a slate of long-term growth initiatives.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Mistry, Waylon Cunningham
item.content:encoded: McDonald's (MCD.N) warned on Wednesday that industrywide customer traffic in key markets would likely remain flat as long as inflation remained elevated, sending its shares down as much as 6.5% even as it unveiled an $8.5 billion franchisee support plan and a slate of long-term growth initiatives. The warning reinforced investor concerns that McDonald's turnaround could take longer than expected, even as it rolls out its "NEXT" strategy to reignite growth after several quarters of slowing sales and intensifying competition from value-focused rivals. "Look at Starbucks, these changes don't happen overnight," said Jake Dollarhide, a McDonald's investor as CEO of Longbow Asset Management, referring to the [USN:L6N44V1E6 TEXT:"turnaround effort at Starbucks"] that took close to a year for investments to translate into boosted sales. Last month, McDonald's [USN:L6N44017R TEXT:"missed "]estimates for second-quarter US sales growth, citing execution missteps that hindered efforts to win back lower-income consumers who had cut back on dining out. Its shares, which are now down about 22% so far this year, dropped to a near four-year low of $234.03 on Wednesday. Newly appointed US business head [USN:L6N441161 TEXT:"Skye Anderson"] acknowledged those shortcomings on Wednesday, saying McDonald's had fallen short on "consistent execution" and needed to improve restaurant operations. The chain on Wednesday outlined an $8.5 billion, decade-long support package for franchisees, who bear hefty costs under the "NEXT" plan, and set new targets for restaurant productivity and operating margins in the low- to mid-50% range by 2030. "We expect industry traffic growth in our wholly owned markets will be flat while inflation remains elevated," CEO Chris Kempczinski said during an investor meeting. "The winners will be the companies that create more demand and deliver it more efficiently." Announced in June, McDonald's "NEXT" strategy focuses on improving food quality, hospitality, value and innovation, with executives on Wednesday providing the first detailed roadmap. The initiative includes simplifying operations, modernizing restaurant designs, investing in employee training and expanding the use of ArchIQ, an AI-powered restaurant operating system that automates tasks such as drive-thru ordering. Anderson, who was named as president of its US business last month to steer the company's turnaround strategy, said on Wednesday that McDonald's was also adapting to changing consumer preferences, including higher-protein options and greater portion flexibility for GLP-1 users. Anderson added that the company is exploring bowls, grilled chicken and egg bites to expand protein-centered options across breakfast, lunch and dinner. "Consumers are making choices based on more than price, and McDonald's needs to give them reasons to visit beyond a deal," eMarketer analyst Suzy Davidkhanian said. McDonald's has seen greater tensions with franchisees who have complained about eroding control and rising costs. McDonald's executives in August said execution of its under-$3 menu was hurt by a third of franchisees that did not participate. Dollarhide, the investor, said he has watched strains in McDonald's franchisee relations closely because a lack of franchisee buy-in can hurt execution of the company's strategies. US restaurant remodeling required by McDonald's and upgrades under the "NEXT" plan could cost at least $1.2 million for the average location. McDonald's will offer some assistance including rent relief, but the support does not extend to the cost of the remodels. "It's a big commitment for franchisees," said Dollarhide. Of the $8.5 billion investment, roughly $5 billion will be deployed by 2030 through rent relief and capital support for franchisees. The company expects the strategy to improve restaurant-level efficiency by 250 basis points, generating about $100,000 in additional annual cash flow for the average US restaurant. The burger chain expects restaurant expansion to contribute about 2.5% of systemwide sales growth in 2027 and around 2% by 2030. US foot traffic at McDonald's has declined year-over-year for every complete month since March, according to estimates from data analytics firm Placer.ai.

item.title: ガザ「平和評議会」、24.5億ドルの復興計画発表 停戦なお不透明
item.description:
Nidal al-Mughrabi
［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Nidal al-Mughrabi

［２３日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領が設置したパレスチナ自治区ガザの暫定統治機関「平和評議会」は２３日、総額２４億５０００万ドルの復興計画を発表した。計画はイスラエルとイスラム組織ハマスの約２年間に及ぶ戦闘で破壊されたガザ地区のインフラと経済の再建を目指す６６の事業で構成。ただ、米国が仲介する停戦を巡るイスラエルとハマスの隔たりは依然大きく、復興の先行きに不透明感が残っていることを当局者も認めた。

復興計画はニューヨークで開催されている国連総会に合わせて開かれたイベントで平和評議会が発表した。ガザ地区の物的被害額を３５２億ドルと見積もり、向こう１０年で完全な復旧・復興に約７１４億ドルが必要になると試算した。国境検問所の修復や電力・水道インフラの復旧のほか、２万５０００基の携帯型太陽光発電キットの配備、優先的な復興事業に必要な用地の地下にあるトンネルの恒久的な埋め戻しなどが盛り込まれた。

ルビオ米国務長官は記者団に対し「これは明らかに長期的な事業で、６カ月で実現できるものではない。ただ、少なくとも人々に希望を与えることができる。誰もが自らの役割を果たせば、このような未来が待っている」と語った。

トランプ大統領の娘婿でガザ復興計画の策定に関わったジャレッド・クシュナー氏は、復興計画がさまざまな理由で遅延していることを認めた上で、「計画をさらに練り上げ、行動に移すときに備えている」と述べた。

平和評議会のガザ地区担当首席特使、ニコライ・ムラデノフ氏は、ガザ地区を戦闘前の状態に戻すことを目指しているのではないとし、「ガザ地区のパレスチナ人と、国境を挟んで暮らすイスラエルの地域社会の双方が、長年にわたり生活を支配してきた暴力への恐怖を乗り越える機会を得られるようにしたい」と語った。

item.title: Huracán Polo azota costa oeste de México con copiosas lluvias y fuertes vientos
item.description: El huracán Polo disminuyó ligeramente su intensidad el miércoles en aguas del océano Pacífico, pero seguía descargando copiosas lluvias en los estados de la costa occidental de México, mientras sus fuertes vientos y oleaje anómalo obligaron a cerrar algunos puertos y ultimar precauciones en centros turísticos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Polo disminuyó ligeramente su intensidad el miércoles en aguas del océano Pacífico, pero seguía descargando copiosas lluvias en los estados de la costa occidental de México, mientras sus fuertes vientos y oleaje anómalo obligaron a cerrar algunos puertos y ultimar precauciones en centros turísticos. Por la tarde del miércoles, Polo se ubicaba a 240 kilómetros al sur-suroeste de Zihuatanejo, un conocido destino de playa en la costa del estado Guerrero, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 230 kilómetros por hora (km/h), con rachas más fuertes, mientras se desplazaba hacia el noroeste a 11 km/h, según datos del Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). "Según la trayectoria prevista, se espera que el centro de Polo permanezca cerca de la costa del suroeste de México hasta la mañana del jueves, antes de adentrarse más en el mar", dijo el NHC. "Polo es un huracán de categoría 4 en la escala Saffir-Simpson. Es posible que se fortalezca lentamente durante el próximo día", agregó. Un huracán mayor se considera a partir de que alcanza la categoría 3 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson. En lunes, Polo llegó a[USN:L1N45D0ST TEXT:" categoría 5"]. Los vientos y lluvias de Polo golpearán hasta la tarde del jueves una franja costera desde el turístico Puerto Vallarta hasta Acapulco. En previsión, la Secretaría de Marina cerró algunos puertos a la navegación de todo tipo de embarcaciones. En las principales terminales portuarias del país, Lázaro Cárdenas y Manzanillo, la navegación fue suspendida para embarcaciones menores. La Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil (CNPC) instó a la población que habita en la franja costera de los estados afectados a suspender actividades recreativas y marítimas y a mantenerse informada a través de los canales oficiales. En Acapulco, el fuerte oleaje azotaba la costa, la lluvia caía sobre la bahía y los vientos huracanados doblaban las palmeras. Los comerciantes reforzaban los techos de sus puestos mientras los botes permanecían anclados en la bahía. "Cuando nos avisaron ayer (martes), empecé a poner mis documentos en orden y a empacar mis cosas por si acaso", dijo Andrea Tenorio, una residente local. Ella comentó que una escuela primaria cercana había sido habilitada como refugio temporal. "Con Otis nos quedó un trauma", agregó. "No hemos podido superarlo". En 2023, Acapulco sufrió la furia de Otis, un huracán de extraordinaria potencia y capacidad destructiva, considerado el ciclón tropical más fuerte que ha tocado tierra en las costas del Pacífico mexicano. La tormenta, que golpeó a fines de octubre, dejó 68 fallecidos confirmados y unos 16,000 millones de dólares en daños. Desde el jueves, Polo se irá alejando de la costa mexicana, pero el lunes podría pegar como un huracán de categoría 2 en la península de Baja California Sur, donde se ubican La Paz y Los Cabos, los dos principales centros turísticos de playa de la región.

item.title: UK says will revisit Chagos deal after latest Trump criticism
item.description: LONDON: Britain will rework its deal to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, a minister confirmed on Wednesday (Sep 23), after US President Donald Trump branded the agreement "terrible" during his first meeting with UK leader Andy Burnham.London's decision to hand back the Indian Ocean archipelago to its f
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

UK says will revisit Chagos deal after latest Trump criticism

Members of the Chagossian community and supporters protest outside the High Court in London on May 22, 2025, as a hearing into the fate of the Chagos Islands, goes on inside. (Photo: AFP/Henry Nicholls)

23 Sep 2026 07:32PM (Updated: 23 Sep 2026 09:01PM)

FAST

LONDON: Britain will rework its deal to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, a minister confirmed on Wednesday (Sep 23), after US President Donald Trump branded the agreement "terrible" during his first meeting with UK leader Andy Burnham. London's decision to hand back the Indian Ocean archipelago to its former colony and pay to lease a strategic US-UK military base on Diego Garcia has been a bone of contention with Trump's administration for months. The UK confirmed in April that it was pausing the plans agreed last year between the Mauritian government and Britain's then-prime minister Keir Starmer. It faced vocal opposition from Trump, who had initially supported the pact, but then later branded it "an act of great stupidity".

The unpredictable American leader railed against the deal again on Tuesday in his first face-to-face with Burnham, who replaced Starmer in July. Meeting on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Trump said he believed Burnham would be reconsidering the "terrible deal", as the UK leader sat beside him, nodded and said "yep". Burnham later told broadcasters Britain would "work hard" to find a resolution on the thorny issue and that he was "confident we can find it working with our US partners". Hours later, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said Trump's opposition was "not news to us" but that his latest comments "provide absolute clarity that his position on this Chagos deal as currently drafted is not changing". "So we have to do more work with our American allies, with President Trump and his administration, to get the deal to a place where we can support it," he told the BBC on Wednesday. Streeting confirmed that annual payments worth at least £120 million (US$159 million) to lease back the military base from Mauritius would not be made "at this stage". Starmer struck the deal after insisting that international legal rulings have put Britain's ownership of the Chagos in doubt and only a deal with Mauritius would guarantee continued US and UK use of the base. "MILLSTONE?" Britain kept control of the Chagos Islands after Mauritius gained independence in the 1960s. It evicted thousands of Chagos islanders who have since mounted a series of legal claims for compensation in British courts. In 2019, the International Court of Justice recommended that Britain hand the archipelago to Mauritius. The deal would have given Britain a 99-year lease of the base, with the option to extend. James Cartlidge, defence spokesman for the main opposition Conservative party, said the agreement "should be binned entirely". But Streeting told Times Radio: "The ostrich strategy of sticking our heads in the sand and hoping it (will) go away ... is not a wise strategy when it concerns one of the most sensitive national security assets we have anywhere in the world." Jack Pannell, a senior researcher at the British Foreign Policy Group think-tank, said Burnham's priorities with Trump would be on "the big international issues" like AI regulation, Ukraine and the Middle East. "Success for Burnham means avoiding this issue becoming a millstone around his neck while he pursues his other foreign policy priorities and focuses on his domestic agenda," Pannell told AFP. "The chances of a breakthrough on this issue are slim, and that may suit the prime minister just fine." On Tuesday, Trump signed a security deal with the leaders of Greenland and Denmark that will allow the US to build two military bases in southern and eastern Greenland.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: Meta expected to unveil new smart glasses at Connect developer event
item.description: Meta is expected to show off AI-powered smart glasses at its Connect developer conference as CEO Mark Zuckerberg continues to evangelise the glasses as the next step in human-computer interactions.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Meta expected to unveil new smart glasses at Connect developer event

Meta expected to unveil new smart glasses at Connect developer event Meta is expected to show off AI-powered smart glasses at its Connect developer conference as CEO Mark Zuckerberg continues to evangelise the glasses as the next step in human-computer interactions.

Meta logo (Photo: Reuters)

AP Washington 2 min read Last Updated : Sep 23 2026 | 11:58 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Meta is expected to show off artificial intelligence-powered smart glasses at its Connect developer conference Wednesday as CEO Mark Zuckerberg continues to evangelise the glasses as the next step in human-computer interactions. Last year's Meta Connect was far less metaverse and far more AI. Expect this year's event to be virtually dominated by AI, specifically AI glasses and superintelligence, said Forrester research director Mike Proulx. While Meta has the head start on AI glasses, competition is chomping at the bit with new entrants. The Menlo Park, California-based company teased a prototype for Orion, which Zuckerberg called the most advanced glasses the world has ever seen, last year but these holographic augmented reality glasses are still years away from being on the market.

Instead, analysts expect Meta to show off new smart glasses, likely with a small display controlled by a wristband the user wears. While more of an experimentation platform, they should enable consumers to access time, weather, notifications, frame and preview pictures, show captions and translate speeches, allow early integration of Meta's assets (WhatsApp and Instagram), and display Meta AI responses, said Forrester's Thomas Husson. Also Read

Zuckerberg says AI labs can self-regulate, rejects industry slowdown calls

Meta tried to turn employee activity into AI data. The plan backfired

Apple's new CEO may bet big on Siri-powered smart glasses by 2027: Report

Meta's new teen safety rules: What changes on Instagram and Facebook

Zuckerberg wanted to cut Meta workforce by 60%; here's why he didn't

Meta is also expected to show off updates to its Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, which are likely to have enhanced AI capabilities interpreting the user's surroundings and context," the analyst added. While the company has not disclosed sales figures of the glasses, it said they've been more popular than expected, helped by social media creators.

Zuckerberg said he believes AI glasses are going to be the main way we integrate superintelligence.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: 英保険・資産運用のL&G、従業員約10%を削減へ－来年半ばまでに
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英国の保険・資産運用大手リーガル・アンド・ジェネラル・グループ（L&G）は、組織簡素化の一環として、従業員数を約1割削減する方針だ。

ブルームバーグ・ニュースが確認した23日付の従業員向け電子メールによると、同社は、来年半ばまでに約1000人のポストを削減する計画に着手した。この計画に詳しい関係者によると、英国では当初、希望退職を募るが、状況に応じて会社都合による人員削減も検討する。

1兆2000億ポンド（約250兆円）の資産を運用する投資運用部門は、すでに独自の再編計画を進めているため、希望退職プログラムの対象外となる。内部情報だとして匿名を条件に関係者が明らかにした。

L&Gの約1万人の従業員の大半は英国に勤務している。同社の広報担当者は電子メールで、これらの変更は変革の「次の段階」に当たり、「組織体制や働き方を、現在構築している事業と、事業を展開する急速に変化する環境に即したものにする」と説明。「長期的な成長機会が最も大きいとみている分野に、リソースと投資を集中させることにもつながる」と述べた。

原題：L&G Seeks to Cut About 10% of Workforce by Middle of 2027 (1)

--取材協力：Will Standring、Michael Msika.

item.title: After Trump's annihilation threat, Pezeshkian says Iran won't surrender
item.description: In a potential new flashpoint, Iran also threatened to act against its neighbours if they abide by new US sanctions intended to ground Iranian civilian aircraft worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / After Trump's annihilation threat, Pezeshkian says Iran won't surrender

After Trump's annihilation threat, Pezeshkian says Iran won't surrender In a potential new flashpoint, Iran also threatened to act against its neighbours if they abide by new US sanctions intended to ground Iranian civilian aircraft worldwide.

Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian (Photo: PTI)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Sep 23 2026 | 11:56 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in a speech at the UN on Wednesday that Tehran would never surrender to the US but still believes in diplomacy, a day after President Donald Trump used the same forum to threaten to "annihilate" Iran.   The duelling speeches at the annual UN General Assembly in New York bookended the first shuttle talks between the United States and Iran for months, which appeared to have yielded no concessions in the public stance of either side towards ending the Middle East war.   In his speech, Pezeshkian defended Iran's military actions as defensive, and insisted Iran was not seeking nuclear weapons.

In a potential new flashpoint, Iran also threatened to act against its neighbours if they abide by new US sanctions intended to ground Iranian civilian aircraft worldwide.   Washington has said it will impose so-called secondary sanctions against any country that allows Iranian flights after Wednesday.   Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state TV Iran would ensure neighbouring countries' airports could not function if they stop Iranian flights. Also Read

Cargo ship MV Cape Dao hit in Strait of Hormuz, 1 Indian on board killed

Dolly Parton's estate in turmoil after accusations of extortion

Fact check: A look at what Donald Trump got wrong in UN address

Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 yrs in prison for 2006 sex crime in NY

US, Iran officials held 'very good' meeting on sidelines of UNGA: Trump

The annual UN gathering in New York provided the occasion on Tuesday for Iranian and U.S. officials to hold their first known indirect talks since a ceasefire collapsed in July, with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicating through mediators on the sidelines.

"Steve and Jared had a very productive meeting today with mediators of Iran," Trump said on Tuesday after his own speech. "I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal. It's what we're hearing from everybody."   Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Tehran had engaged with Washington through a Qatari mediator and conveyed conditions, including an end to the war on all fronts and a halt to US "acts of aggression".     Some Iranian state media initially reported that Araqchi and Witkoff had met, but Iranian officials clarified to Reuters that it was not face-to-face.   Iran hardliners resist diplomatic moves The diplomatic contact in New York caused a backlash in Iranian media associated with hardliners.

An opinion piece run by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, associated with the Revolutionary Guards, said Araqchi was wrong to have contacts with Witkoff and Kushner, "a major gift to Trump", as Iran had already conveyed its terms.   Iranian sources told Reuters the delegation had been ordered not to meet the Americans face-to-face by the Supreme National Security Council, a body that includes figures selected by Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, the supreme leader. Khamenei has yet to appear in public since replacing his father, who was killed on the war's first day.   One Iranian journalist covering the visit told Reuters that some hardliners viewed the trip to New York itself as an insult to the memory of the slain leader, Ali Khamenei.

Oil prices hold near two-week low Still, the diplomatic opening helped keep oil prices near two-week lows. Brent crude hovered around $100 a barrel after surging earlier this month when Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched a major offensive, ??threatening traffic through the Red Sea, an alternative Saudi export route.   The war, launched by Trump in February alongside Israel as "Operation Epic Fury", has lasted nearly seven months, killing thousands of people, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region - particularly to Lebanon and more recently to Yemen.   An interim agreement reached in June, signed by Trump and Pezeshkian, would have given Iran its main demands: lifting financial sanctions and unfreezing assets in return for talks on limiting its nuclear programme.

But that deal unravelled within weeks over shipping rules in the Strait of Hormuz, conduit for a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas before the war. Iran wants to exert control and collect fees from ships that use it, which Washington rejects.   In the latest reported attack in the strait, Britain's UKMTO maritime security agency said a cargo ship had been hit by projectiles, causing two casualties among the crew. The crew had been evacuated and the ship was on fire and adrift.   Despite near-daily attacks, traffic through the strait has picked up in recent weeks. Oil producers pay shipping companies fees of as much as a quarter of a cargo's value to take the wartime risk of sailing through the strait with transponders switched off, before transferring crude to other vessels on the far side.

Exports from the United Arab Emirates have already recovered to pre-war levels, and Saudi Arabia has sold 60 million barrels of Gulf oil for both this month and next, to be delivered beyond the strait off the coast of Oman.   Nevertheless, a third of Gulf oil is estimated to be missing from global supplies. Shortages have particularly hit refined products such as diesel, causing inflation, pushing up interest rates and hurting Trump's Republicans.

More From This Section

Iran Prez Pezeshkian defends country's right to civil nuclear enrichment

item.title: 米30年物住宅ローン金利7.12％、2年超ぶり高水準＝米抵当銀行協会
item.description:
Ann Saphir
［２３日 ロイター］ - 米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が２３日発表した３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米30年物住宅ローン金利7.12％、2年超ぶり高水準＝米抵当銀行協会 9/23 20:11 配信

カリフォルニア州カールスバッドで16日撮影　REUTERS/Mike Blake

Ann Saphir

［２３日　ロイター］ - 米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が２３日発表した３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均金利（１８日までの週）は７．１２％で、前週から１５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇し２０２４年５月以来の高水準となった。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が利上げをし、住宅ローン金利の基準となる米国債利回りが上昇した。

ＭＢＡによると、借り換えと住宅購入向けのローン申請は減少した。借り手の間では変動金利型住宅ローン（ＡＲＭ）の利用が増え、住宅ローン申請に占めるＡＲＭの割合は９．８％だった。ＡＲＭは固定金利型より当初の借入コストが低い一方、数年後にはその時点の市場金利に応じて金利が見直される。

２月下旬に米国とイスラエルがイランを攻撃し、原油価格を押し上げて以降、住宅ローン金利は１％ポイント超上昇。住宅購入を検討する人をためらわせ、米住宅市場を冷え込ませている。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 コラム：ＡＩ相場はドットコム・バブルの再来か、強気派に分がある理由 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 最終更新: 9/23(水) 20:11 ロイター

item.title: ロシア「和平協議の用意ある」、前提条件なお整わず キーウ攻撃継続
item.description:
Daniel Flynn Pavel Polityuk
［モスクワ／キーウ ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Daniel Flynn　Pavel Polityuk

［モスクワ／キーウ　２３日　ロイター］ - ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官は２３日、ウクライナ和平協議を行う前提条件は依然として整っていないと述べる一方で、和平協議に応じる姿勢は維持していると述べた。ウクライナの首都キーウでは、ロシアによるドローン（小型無人機）攻撃で少なくとも２人が死亡した。

ペスコフ氏は記者団に対し、「現時点で平和的な交渉の軌道に移る前提条件はない。ただ、ロシア側としては和平協議に引き続き応じる用意がある」と述べた。

トランプ米大統領とウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２２日、ニューヨークで会談した。ゼレンスキー氏は、トランプ氏を交えた３者会談の方式でプーチン大統領と会談する用意があると表明した。

ペスコフ氏は、両首脳が必要と判断すれば、プーチン氏はトランプ氏と１対１の会談を行う用意があると述べたが、ゼレンスキー氏との直接会談を巡るロシアの立場に変化はないと明確にした。

ロシアはかねて、ゼレンスキー氏がロシア側の条件を満たした上で、モスクワで会談する必要があると主張。ウクライナ政府はこれを拒否し、協議は中立国で開催すべきとしている。

ペスコフ氏は首脳会談の構想についても慎重な見方を示した。「一般論として、専門家レベルで下準備が整う前に首脳会談を開くのは、他のいかなる状況でも不適切だ。時間の無駄になる」と語った。

＜ロシア、キーウを激しく攻撃＞

ロシアは２３日、キーウをドローンで激しく攻撃し、キーウ市当局によると、少なくとも２人が死亡、３０人以上が負傷した。鉄道インフラや倉庫、給油所が攻撃された。

市中心部では爆発音が聞かれ、煙が立ち上った。欧州連合（ＥＵ）のマテルノバ駐ウクライナ大使は交流サイトへの投稿で、「これはきょう、ＥＵ代表部の窓から見える光景だ。近くの建物が燃えている」と述べた。

攻撃は午前から午後早い時間にかけて数時間継続。ロシアが迎撃が困難な高速・高高度飛行のジェット推進型ドローンを用いた攻撃を開始して以降、最も激しい攻撃の一つとなった。

ゼレンスキー大統領は、ロシアがこの日の攻撃に投入した無人機の多くがジェット推進型だったとし、「ロシアは引き続き民間施設や重要インフラを標的にしている。製薬施設、ガソリンスタンド、鉄道、通信インフラ、ショッピングモールが攻撃対象となっている」と非難した。

＜ロシア国防省、データセンターと物流拠点標的と表明＞

ロシア国防省はその後、ウクライナ軍を支援するために使用されているとして、複数のデータセンターと物流・倉庫施設を攻撃したと表明。通信アプリ「テレグラム」への投稿で、首都キーウの２カ所のデータセンターのほか、黒海沿岸の港湾都市オデーサの２カ所の物流拠点を標的に攻撃したと明らかにした。

ウクライナのデジタル省によると、ロシアによる攻撃でキーウと周辺地域で約１０万世帯のインターネットが一時的に遮断された。

ウクライナ東部ドネツク州の前線地域にある集落に対してもロシア軍による攻撃があり、少なくとも４人が死亡、４人が負傷した。

item.title: Here’s a Crystal Ball Glimpse of the Global Economy in 30 Years

South Korea says Trump welcomes progress in US strategic investment projects

US President Donald Trump meets with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, on Oct 29, 2025. (Photo: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein)

SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and US President Donald Trump welcomed "significant progress" in discussions on strategic investment projects during a 30-minute meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Seoul's presidential office said on Wednesday (Sep 23). The meeting came after South Korea's Industry Ministry briefed lawmakers on Tuesday on implementation plans under the countries' US$350 billion investment package, including a Texas gas-fired power project identified as a potential first investment, as well as possible investments in nuclear energy and an Alaskan LNG project. "The two leaders welcomed the significant progress made in discussions on strategic investment projects between the two countries," National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac told a briefing. Based on the Joint Fact Sheet issued after their summit last November, Lee and Trump also agreed to deepen cooperation and continue discussions on issues including nuclear fuel enrichment and reprocessing, nuclear-powered submarines, shipbuilding and the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the US to South Korea, Wi said.

Trump also reaffirmed his willingness to engage in dialogue with North Korea, Wi said, with the two leaders agreeing to remain in close communication in pursuit of a peace process. Lee also said the US-China summit scheduled for Thursday would be important for regional developments, including South Korea-China relations, according to Wi. The White House did not immediately comment on the Trump-Lee meeting. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday called for the swift execution of South Korean investment commitments during a meeting with South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun, the State Department said. In a post on X, Lee said he had an in-depth discussion with Trump on the progress made on investment projects and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the alliance.

Related:

North Korea fires unidentified projectile into East Sea: Seoul

Court orders North Korea pay Seoul US$32.5 million for blowing up office

DISCUSSED NORTH KOREA, GOLF Earlier on Wednesday, Lee told the UN General Assembly that Seoul would support efforts to revive dialogue with North Korea and work toward a durable peace framework while seeking broader international backing for those efforts. A senior presidential official separately told South Korean media outlets that Lee had told Trump he hoped the US president would help advance engagement with North Korea, to which Trump replied that he would do so. The official said Trump also remarked that he maintained a good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though there was no indication of any specific contact currently taking place, the media reports said. The official said Lee and Trump also spent considerable time discussing OPCON transfer, with Trump gaining a better understanding of Seoul's position. The US side stressed the need to meet the required conditions and complete the process as soon as possible. The South Korean side outlined plans to increase defence spending, while expressing a desire to accelerate talks on developing nuclear-powered submarines, the official said. The official was also quoted as saying that progress in talks on investments in US projects helped pave the way for the summit, which had not initially been expected to take place. The two leaders had been briefed on the negotiations and welcomed the progress, but discussions were still under way on the details of the package and how it would be announced, the official said. "The bigger framework is almost complete," the official was quoted as saying. Lee later said on X that Trump had reminded him of their plan to play golf together, first discussed in France in June, and that he hoped they could continue their discussions at the G20 summit in Miami later this year.

item.title: Iran Prez Pezeshkian defends country's right to civil nuclear enrichment
item.description: Questions surrounding the Islamic Republic's nuclear program won't be "resolved on the battlefield," he said in an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday. "We say ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Iran Prez Pezeshkian defends country's right to civil nuclear enrichment

Iran Prez Pezeshkian defends country's right to civil nuclear enrichment "We say clearly: No to nuclear weapons, and no to deprivation of nuclear knowledge," Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian said.

Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian | Image: Bloomberg

Bloomberg 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 23 2026 | 10:56 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country has no interest in developing atomic weapons but won't give up the right to develop nuclear technology for economic development.    Questions surrounding the Islamic Republic's nuclear program won't be "resolved on the battlefield," he said in an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday.   "We say clearly: No to nuclear weapons, and no to deprivation of nuclear knowledge," Pezeshkian said.   The Iranian president delivered his address as tentative signs emerge of renewed diplomacy to end the nearly seven-month conflict with the US even as major differences remain between Tehran and Washington over the terms of a settlement and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

On the strait, Pezeshkian said Iran would not allow free passage through the waterway while being hampered by sanctions.  Also Read

NTPC, Adani Power get nod for nuclear plant feasibility studies in Odisha

US, Iran officials held 'very good' meeting on sidelines of UNGA: Trump

Iran war pushes diesel to record high prices, with no relief on the horizon

Iran rules out reopening Strait of Hormuz until US meets its demands

RAPP-8 begins fuel loading, commercial operations targeted this fiscal

During his speech to the General Assembly on Tuesday, President Donald Trump threatened to "annihilate" Iran unless it makes a deal to end the conflict.   He later said he thinks a settlement with Iran can be reached and that his officials had held "very good" talks with Tehran envoys earlier that day. He said the relationship with Tehran is "developing."   Iran was represented in those talks by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who laid out "firm positions" for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media. Tehran's conditions include the US immediately lifting a naval blockade, unfreezing Iranian assets and ending the war "on all fronts," IRIB News reported, an apparent reference to Israel's campaign against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon.

Before departing Iran for New York, Pezeshkian said the country would use the General Assembly to defend its position and convey the suffering of its people.   The appearance puts Pezeshkian in the unusual position of addressing foreign leaders in New York while the Islamic Republic is at war with the US, giving Tehran a high-profile platform on American soil to present its side of the conflict.   The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the biggest obstacles to a settlement. Traffic through the waterway, a critical route for global oil and gas supplies, has been severely disrupted during the war.   Iran has been talks with Oman on an arrangement for the strait. One sticking point is Tehran's push to charge ships fees for services it provides in the waterway, an idea opposed by the US.

Iran's nuclear program is another central issue in any potential negotiation. Tehran says its nuclear activities are peaceful, while Washington has sought restrictions on the program as part of a broader agreement.   Pezeshkian, who has said Iran is prepared for diplomacy but won't surrender to US pressure, is also due to hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders in New York.

item.description: [２２日 ロイター] - 中国の金融規制当局が、中国不動産大手の万科企業の延滞融資を不良債権に分類せず、返済期限を延...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国当局、不動産大手の延滞融資巡り銀行に窓口指導か　不良債権分類防ぐ 9/23 19:37 配信

北京で2025年12月撮影　REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

[２２日 ロイター] - 中国の金融規制当局が、中国不動産大手の万科企業の延滞融資を不良債権に分類せず、返済期限を延長するよう一部銀行に求めたことが、事情に詳しい複数の関係者の話で分かった。

関係者によると、当局は、万科の債務不履行回避に向けた非公式の「窓口指導」で、金融機関に同社を支援し、資金繰り悪化につながる行動を控えるようを行った。

一部銀行に、万科が支払うべき利息の回収を当面見合わせるよう求めたという。

ロイターは指導を受けた銀行数を確認できなかったが、関係者は、主に規模の大きい銀行が対象と述べた。

融資を不良債権に分類しない期間は定められておらず、不動産市場の動向や万科との今後の協議に左右されるという。

万科は長期化する不動産不況下で経営難に陥りながらも、国有企業の資金支援もあって債務不履行を回避してきた数少ない不動産開発会社の一つ。

万科は販売低迷で手元資金が減少し、２０２５年は過去最大の８８６億元の赤字となった。２６年上期は１４９億５０００万元の純損失、売上高は前年同期比３３％減の７０２億元だった。

関係者の１人は、金融当局が市場の信認に与える打撃を懸念し、国有株主との結び付きが強い不動産開発会社で「リスク事象」が起きるのを防ごうとしていると述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：中国の緩和シグナルに一抹の警戒心、経済再構築は待ったなし コラム：海外マネーの中国離れ、習主席はじっとやり過ごすのが得策か アングル：中国ユニツリー、上場後に株価急落　バブルやＩＰＯ制度に懸念 焦点：中国地方経済の二極化鮮明、ハイテク拠点が成長けん引　伝統産業依存は低迷 最終更新: 9/23(水) 19:37 ロイター

item.title: Iran, US still far apart in peace talks, Iranian official says; Pezeshkian vows no surrender
item.description: Iran and the United States remain far apart on how to end their war but diplomacy must continue, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.
item.dc:creator: Parisa Hafezi, Humeyra Pamuk, Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Iran and the United States remain far apart on how to end their war but diplomacy must continue, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday, after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in [USN:L6N45F0T5 TEXT:"his speech"] in New York, condemned what he called "signs of a bullying mentality" from US President Donald Trump, who had used the same forum on Tuesday to threaten to "annihilate" Iran. The duelling speeches at the annual UN gathering bookended the first shuttle talks between the US and Iran for months, though they appeared to have yielded no concessions in the public stance of either side towards ending the war . The senior Iranian official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals, which prioritise lifting a US naval blockade on Iranian ports and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. "There are still many differences between the Iranian and US positions, but diplomacy is continuing," the official said. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Wednesday that a deal with Iran would involve hard work over a period of time, adding that Trump also had military options. The US has also said it will impose so-called secondary sanctions against any country that allows Iranian flights after Wednesday. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state TV Iran would ensure neighbouring countries' airports could not function if they stop Iranian flights. IRAN 'WILL NOT BOW TO PRESSURE', PRESIDENT SAYS In his address to the 193-member General Assembly, Pezeshkian homed in on the US blockade of Iranian ports and on the Strait of Hormuz, conduit for a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before the war. "It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access to shipping through this waterway. The permanent deployment of hostile fleets and the expansion of the war will not lead to peace," he said. "The Iranian people will not bow to pressure," he added. Iran wants to exert control over the strait and collect fees from ships that use it. Washington rejects this and says the strait must remain fully open to international shipping. Oil prices were [USN:L1N45F01U TEXT:"up almost 2%"] on Wednesday in choppy trade as traders weighed the comments of Pezeshkian and Trump. Trump on Tuesday argued that he had prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end the conflict. Pezeshkian on Wednesday reiterated Iran's line that it is not seeking nuclear weapons. Iranian and US officials held their first known indirect talks on Tuesday since a ceasefire collapsed in July, with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicating through mediators. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Tehran had conveyed conditions during a two-hour exchange of messages with Washington via a Qatari mediator. These included an end to the war on all fronts, a halt to US "acts of aggression" and the release of frozen Iranian assets. IRAN HARDLINERS RESIST DIPLOMATIC MOVES The diplomatic contact in New York caused a backlash in Iranian media associated with hardliners. An opinion piece run by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, associated with the Revolutionary Guards, said Araqchi was wrong to have contacts with Witkoff and Kushner, "a major gift to Trump", as Iran had already conveyed its terms. Iranian sources told Reuters the delegation had been ordered not to meet the Americans face-to-face by the Supreme National Security Council, a body that includes figures selected by Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, the supreme leader. Khamenei has yet to appear in public since replacing his father, who was killed on the war's first day. One Iranian journalist covering the visit told Reuters that some hardliners viewed the trip to New York itself as an insult to the memory of the slain leader, Ali Khamenei. The war, launched by Trump in February alongside Israel as "Operation Epic Fury", has lasted nearly seven months, killing thousands of people, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region — particularly to Lebanon and more recently to Yemen. In the latest reported attack in the Strait of Hormuz, Britain's UKMTO maritime security agency said [USN:S8N44D002 TEXT:"a cargo ship had been hit by projectiles"], causing two casualties among the crew. The crew was evacuated and the ship was on fire and adrift. Despite near-daily attacks, traffic through the strait has picked up in recent weeks. Oil producers pay shipping companies fees of as much as a quarter of a cargo's value to take the wartime risk of sailing through the strait with [USN:L1N45A0KR TEXT:"transponders switched off"], before transferring crude to other vessels on the far side. Exports from the United Arab Emirates have already recovered to pre-war levels, and Saudi Arabia has sold 60 million barrels of Gulf oil for both this month and next, to be delivered beyond the strait off the coast of Oman. Nevertheless, [USN:L6N44U0L7 TEXT:"a third of Gulf oil is estimated to be missing"] from global supplies. Shortages have particularly hit refined products such as diesel, causing inflation, pushing up interest rates and hurting Trump's Republicans.

OpenAI’s Sam Altman, Anthropic’s Amodei to brief UNSC as France flags AI threat to kids, global security

Meeting called by Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot because AI's security implications had not received enough attention at the Security Council, says a French official.

Debdutta Chakraborty

23 September, 2026 03:54 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

France's President Emmanuel Macron addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, the US | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: France is convening a high-level meeting at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) on Wednesday in which OpenAI, Anthropic and Hugging Face CEOs will brief the 15-member council on the risks posed by artificial intelligence.

France holds the rotating presidency of the Security Council for September, coinciding with the opening of the 81st Session of the General Assembly in New York.

A French official said the meeting had been called by Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot because the security implications of artificial intelligence had not received enough attention at the Security Council.

Show Full Article

“We consider that artificial intelligence and the threat it could cause has not been sufficiently discussed, especially at the Security Council, and this is why Minister Barrault called for this meeting,” the official said at a media briefing.

French President Emmanuel Macron is expected to host an event focused on protecting children from potential harms associated with artificial intelligence. The initiative brings together governments, technology companies, civil society organisations and foundations, with the stated goal of ensuring that AI benefits children without harming their cognitive and social development.

About 20 countries are expected to participate at various levels, including heads of state and ministers, according to officials.

“The French president will have a major event on the protection of children with AI, which is a coalition bringing together governments, companies, civil society organisations, foundations, with a focus on ensuring that the development of AI benefits our children and do not harm their cognitive and social development, which is a key topic for the future of our society,” the French official added.

The Security Council meeting will address a different set of concerns. “AI has reached a level of development where it raises questions for global security,” the official said. “Now, on several fronts, the malicious use of models, but also the risk of losing control over advanced models, or autonomous weapons, for instance.”

The decision to invite the technology companies directly involved in developing advanced AI systems reflects the growing role of private companies in shaping the technology and its associated risks.

The official added that OpenAI was invited “in light of the recent security incident of this summer,” where independent AI test agents broke out of their sandboxes and accessed external systems, while Anthropic would appear “in light of its proposal on basing the development of advanced AI systems”.

According to the French officials, governments would ultimately have to establish the rules governing the technology and it will be discussed in the UNSC meeting.

The Security Council has previously addressed emerging technologies in the context of international peace and security, but the French initiative puts the rapidly evolving capabilities of generative and advanced AI systems directly before the council.

The first briefer will be Joshua Bengio, co-chair of the International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, who is expected to offer what the official described as “an independent academic perspective on the threats that AI causes to peace and security”.

He will be followed by Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Clément Delangue, the chief executive and co-founder of Hugging Face, the French artificial intelligence company.

Another French official said Paris believed the technology offered substantial benefits but also required international safeguards.

“First, by saying that France has put AI very firmly on the agenda of this UN General Assembly, and that was on purpose because AI is playing an increasingly important role around the world, no need to say about it,” the official added.

“We strongly believe in the immense benefits it could have, but it has to be done well.”

In the UN General Assembly’s 81st session Tuesday, France President Emmanuel Macron had also focused on the risks posed by AI, particularly the fact that most people and countries have little or no say in the debate over how the technology should be regulated.

He argued that decisions about AI should not be left solely to the US, China and a small group of private companies. The stakes, he said, were too high, given that the technology could threaten “the security of our States, of our hospitals, of our banks”.

“We must defend science. We have waited too long to protect our children and adolescents from social media. Everywhere in our societies, we see the consequences,” Macron said.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

item.title: Tigrayan leaders say new war with Ethiopian government has begun
item.description: Forces from the northern Ethiopian region of Tigray launched a major offensive against the federal government on Wednesday, a senior Ethiopian official said, shattering a four-year-old peace deal and threatening a wider regional conflict.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Forces from the northern Ethiopian region of Tigray launched a major offensive against the federal government on Wednesday, a senior Ethiopian official said, shattering a four-year-old peace deal and threatening a wider regional conflict. Tigray's leaders said in a statement they had entered a "defensive" war to counter aggression by the federal government. A civil war that began in 2020 between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and federal forces resulted in hundreds of thousands of deaths before the Pretoria Agreement, brokered by the African Union, was signed in November 2022. The new hostilities follow months of growing animosity between the two sides, capped by Sunday's announcement that the TPLF had [USN:L6N45D0K7 TEXT:"formed an alliance"] with six other armed groups from across Ethiopia aimed at overthrowing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. The TPLF-led regional administration said there had been an "intensification of the invasion conducted through various methods" by Abiy's government against the people of Tigray. "The Tigray Forces have been instructed to counter the attack and have entered a defensive war," it said in a statement. Getachew Reda, an adviser to Abiy and a former TPLF official, wrote on X that the TPLF had seized control of federally controlled airports in Tigray and launched an "all-out offensive" against government positions in the neighbouring regions of Afar and Amhara. "The TPLF politico-military leadership has obviously taken irresponsibility to new heights," he said. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to the region. FEARS OF A WIDER WAR Spokespeople for Abiy, the federal government and the TPLF did not respond to requests for comment on Wednesday. The chair of the African Union Commission, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, urged the warring parties to immediately de-escalate tensions and hold direct talks, and called on neighbouring countries not to contribute to further escalation. The US ambassador to Ethiopia, Ervin J. Massinga, accused the TPLF leadership, which had sanctions imposed on it by the US State Department in June, of "engaging in an unwinnable fight" and called for political dialogue. Regional diplomats and analysts have warned for months that a resumption of the conflict in Tigray could quickly escalate into a wider war, overlapping with fighting in neighbouring Sudan and further roiling the volatile Red Sea region. A [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"civil war"] that broke out in 2023 in Sudan has drawn in powerful states from outside the Horn of Africa and created what the UN describes as the world's largest humanitarian crisis. In the 2020-2022 Tigray war, Ethiopia's neighbour and historical adversary Eritrea backed the government militarily against the TPLF, but relations between the two countries have soured since then. Abiy's spokesperson, Billene Seyoum, said on Monday members of the newly announced alliance had been collaborating for a while with Eritrea's financial backing. Eritrea has denied accusations it supports Ethiopian armed groups. Its information minister declined comment on Wednesday about the latest developments. ARMED GROUPS SIDE WITH TPLF In Afar, Tigrayan forces were fighting alongside a local armed group, and in Amhara, they were fighting alongside the Fano militia, said a senior Ethiopian government official, a diplomatic source, a humanitarian source and another source with links to the TPLF and Fano. Fano sided with the federal government during the 2020-2022 war, but rose up against it in 2023 in an ongoing insurgency that has resulted in thousands of deaths. It is a member of the new alliance with the TPLF. The regional government in Afar accused the TPLF on Wednesday of launching an invasion and said Afari forces would defend themselves in coordination with their allies. In Amhara, federal forces were firing heavy weapons from a camp in the town of Lalibela, whose rock-hewn churches date back to the 12th and 13th centuries, two residents told Reuters. The firing targeted advancing Fano forces some 50 km (30 miles) outside the town, the residents said. The wider scale and intensity of the fighting were not clear. Jawar Mohammed, a political analyst and formerly a close ally of Abiy, said the federal government was limiting its engagement to try to prove to the international community that the TPLF was the instigator. The federal government is in a tactically stronger position than in 2020 because of its large stocks of drones and divisions within the TPLF, said Edward Bach, Senior Africa Analyst at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft. Tigray is yet to recover from the humanitarian toll of the 2020-2022 war, which pushed hundreds of thousands into famine conditions. Around 750,000 Tigrayans were still internally displaced as of February, according to the UN refugee agency, and the region faces drought linked to El Nino. The Ethiopian military has carried out several drone strikes against Tigrayan forces in recent months, according to data from the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project. The federal government has not commented on any of the reported strikes.

item.title: Mexico beach towns brace for storms as Polo churns off the coast
item.description: Residents of Mexico's Pacific beach towns were preparing for heavy rain and dangerous surf on Wednesday as Hurricane Polo, a powerful Category 4 storm, tracked northwestward just offshore, threatening flooding and mudslides along the country's southwestern coast.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Residents of Mexico's Pacific beach towns were preparing for heavy rain and dangerous surf on Wednesday as Hurricane Polo, a powerful Category 4 storm, tracked northwestward just offshore, threatening flooding and mudslides along the country's southwestern coast. The US National Hurricane Center said Polo is expected to continue moving slowly along the coast between the fishing town Zihuatanejo and port hub Manzanillo, with maximum sustained winds of 145 mph (230 kph) at 3 p.m. local time. The center of the hurricane was forecast to track along the edge of southwestern Mexico through Thursday morning before gradually turning farther out to sea. Meanwhile, the storm's outer rainbands were already affecting the coast, where tropical storm warnings and watches remained in place. In resort town Acapulco, rough surf pounded the shoreline, rain swept across the bay and strong winds bent palm trees. Merchants reinforced stall roofs as boats remained anchored in the bay. "As they gave us a warning yesterday, I started getting my documents in order and half-packed my things, just in case," local resident Andrea Tenorio said. She said a nearby elementary school had been opened as a temporary shelter. Asked whether she was afraid, Tenorio said memories of Hurricane Otis still haunted residents. "With Otis, we were left with trauma," she said. "We haven't been able to overcome it." Hurricane Otis slammed into Acapulco in October 2023 as a Category 5 storm, killing dozens and flattening the coastal town. Polo is expected to dump 4 to 6 inches (10 to 15 cm) of rain across coastal Guerrero state, with isolated totals of up to 8 inches (20 cm), the NHC said. That could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in mountainous areas. Lower but still significant rainfall was forecast for parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco states. "Fluctuations in intensity are expected, but Polo is expected to remain a very powerful major hurricane during the next few days," the NHC said.

item.title: Wall Street ends down as oil prices, Treasury yields rise
item.description: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday, pulled down by Alphabet and Amazon, as Treasury yields climbed and Iran's president said Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday, pulled down by Alphabet and Amazon, as Treasury yields climbed and Iran's president said Tehran would never surrender to US pressure. Oil prices rose almost 4% and the S&P 500 energy sector index (.SPNY) rallied after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's speech at the UN, a day after US President Donald Trump warned he could "annihilate" Iran. A survey showed [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"US business activity raced"] to a more than five-year high in September, pushing government bond yields higher and raising expectations the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates at its October meeting. Yields on 2-year Treasuries touched their highest since 2024, while 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007. "The stock market wants a resolution to the (Middle East) conflict, and if we don't get that, we will have higher rates for longer, and that's going to continue to weigh on the equity market," said Lauren Cassidy, chief investment officer at Founders 100 ETF in Dallas. Meta Platforms (META.O) rose 1%, bringing its gain this week to 12% following a strong reception of its "Muse" AI assistant, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online shopping platforms and other consumer businesses. Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) fell 3.8%. Amazon (AMZN.O) , which has blocked Muse from its shopping platform, dropped 2.2%. The PHLX chip index (.SOX) dropped 1.2%, with Nvidia (NVDA.O) down 1.5%. Expedia (EXPE.O) and Airbnb (ABNB.O) both fell more than 7%. The Nasdaq recorded record-high closes in the previous two sessions as Wall Street remained optimistic about AI-related companies. The S&P 500 is less than 2% below its record high close on August 13. US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit. The agenda includes extending the trade truce reached last year between the two superpowers, AI regulation and US [USN:L1N45F06T TEXT:"arms sales"] to Taiwan. The S&P 500 declined 0.75% to end the session at 7,706.05 points. The Nasdaq declined 1.13% to 26,936.04 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.68% to 51,511.59 points. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by utilities (.SPLRCU) , down 1.72%, followed by a 1.49% loss in communication services (.SPLRCL) . Volume on U.S. exchanges was relatively heavy, with 17.0 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 16.5 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions. The S&P 500 is trading just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations. Markets also parsed comments from Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr, who said the [USN:S0N4490DT TEXT:"central bank will likely"] need to deliver further interest rate hikes as inflation remains north of the Fed's 2% target. Traders are now pricing in a 71% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates at its policy meeting next month, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. Casual dining chain Cracker Barrel (CBRL.O) rallied 4.5% after beating fourth-quarter sales estimates. Paychex (PAYX.O) dropped 8.8% after the HR and payroll services provider said that its [USN:L4N45F0UQ TEXT:"largest segment"] missed first-quarter revenue estimates. Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.9-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 posted 14 new highs and 33 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 41 new highs and 186 new lows.
