item.title: Judge skeptical of Trump's White House media ban at hearing
item.description: A US judge appeared skeptical on Wednesday about the legality of Donald Trump's decision to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists from the White House, indicating he may grant their request to lift the ban they describe as unlawful retaliation for news coverage the president dislikes.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe, Jack Queen
item.content:encoded: A US judge appeared skeptical on Wednesday about the legality of Donald Trump 's decision to bar [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"CNN, MS NOW and Politico"] journalists from the White House, indicating he may grant their request to lift the ban they describe as unlawful retaliation for news coverage the president dislikes. US District Judge Timothy Kelly said at a hearing in Washington that Trump's ban did not appear to comply with past legal precedents by failing to give the news outlets an opportunity to respond. Kelly did not immediately rule on a bid by the three outlets for a temporary restraining order lifting the ban while their legal challenge plays out, but said he would do so soon. Trump announced the ban on Friday on his social media platform, [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"saying"] those news organizations "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." The Justice Department has emphasized Trump's contention that the ban is legally justified on national security grounds. The outlets [USN:FWN45C04L TEXT:"said in a lawsuit"] filed on Monday that the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for freedom of speech and a free press, as well as their rights to due process, meaning fair treatment from the government. The judge said it does not appear that Trump complied with two past rulings by the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit by failing to give the news outlets a meaningful opportunity to contest the revocation of their access. Kelly, who Trump appointed in 2017, noted that the government contends that those cases were wrongly decided. "Maybe they were wrongly decided, maybe they weren't," Kelly said. "But as a district court judge I have to apply them. I think it is fair to say the process the circuit laid out in those two cases wasn't followed here." Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer for the news outlets, told Kelly that the ban discriminated against them based on legally protected speech and violated their rights to due process. "The president said, 'I don't like what you're publishing. I'm taking away your press pass based on that,'" Boutrous said. 'A PIECE OF PAPER' Michael Velchik, a Justice Department lawyer, accused the news outlets of publishing classified information, and said they knew that doing so was illegal. He also said the government gave a sufficient explanation and opportunity to respond in letters sent to the news outlets on Tuesday, though Kelly was skeptical of this argument. "I don't know how a letter that they got after the pass was revoked could provide them with the notice of the kind of standards that they would have to conform their conduct to, since it's a piece of paper they got saying, 'You've already violated this,'" the judge said. Trump's ban is the most dramatic of his recent clashes with the media, which he has accused of trying to hurt his fellow Republicans ahead of the November midterm elections in which the party is fighting to retain control of Congress. In a filing on Tuesday, the Justice Department argued that access to the White House is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president has the power to suspend access by news organizations. It accused the outlets of threatening national security with their coverage, citing stories about US missile stockpiles, construction of Trump's White House ballroom and turnout at the recent Republican midterm convention. 'OUR LEAD WITNESS' Boutrous said Trump's social media posts made clear that the president took exception to adversarial reporting produced by the three outlets, and then latched onto national security as a "pretext" for revoking their access. "He keeps proving our point," Boutrous said of Trump. "He's really our lead witness here." In a 2018 case that raised similar legal issues, Kelly ordered the White House to restore CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press pass, which had been revoked after a contentious news conference with Trump. Kelly ruled in that case that the White House had not used fair and clear procedures to revoke Acosta's credential. In a social media post on Monday, Trump indicated regret over appointing Kelly and said he was bracing for a loss. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations filed a legal brief on Wednesday supporting the three news outlets targeted by Trump. They asserted that "stripping journalists and news outlets of their rights because of perceived editorial viewpoint violates decades of Supreme Court jurisprudence." The brief was signed by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, Reuters, the Washington Post and Fox News, among others.

item.title: AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful
item.description: The world's leading artificial intelligence companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the risks posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols, Courtney Rozen, John Irish
item.content:encoded: The world's leading artificial intelligence companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"risks"] posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told the 15-member council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, that if managed poorly, he believed "AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole." The meeting — convened by France during the annual UN General Assembly gathering of world leaders — comes amid [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"warnings"] that AI systems could soon improve themselves and slip beyond human control. "For all the differences of the people in this room, we must put aside those differences in order to confront this global opportunity and global threat that is being presented to us at the same time. No leader, no company and no nation can manage this alone," Amodei said. Governments around the world have struggled to keep pace with rapid advances in artificial intelligence. The United States and China, the two leading powers in AI development, have taken different approaches to oversight. President Donald Trump has argued that the US does not need new AI-specific regulations, while China has imposed rules governing AI algorithms and training data, including requirements that AI-generated content be clearly labeled. Hugging Face co-founder Clément Delangue highlighted the role of AI tools in defending against cyberattacks, citing an incident in which US giant OpenAI's AI agents breached Hugging Face's infrastructure after escaping their testing environment. "We were attacked by AI, but more importantly, we defended ourselves with AI," he told the council. Council members, including leading AI rivals the United States and China, were also set to speak. Delangue said Hugging Face relied on a Chinese AI model to help defend against the attack by OpenAI's AI agents because it faced fewer restrictions than comparable US tools. His remarks underscored the growing presence of Chinese AI products, which have gained users globally in part because they can offer lower-cost alternatives to American models. [USN:L6N45D0R6 TEXT:"OpenAI"] CEO Sam [USN:L6N45A15J TEXT:"Altman"] said international cooperation was needed. “If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people they serve," Altman told the council. As the council met, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told reporters in New York that an AI agent developed by OpenAI [USN:L4N45F1E8 TEXT:"infiltrated"] an Australian government website in June, accessing public and non-public files. US TO UN: YOU CANNOT GOVERN TECHNOLOGY YOU DON'T UNDERSTAND Yoshua Bengio, a Canadian considered one of the "Godfathers of AI" and co-chair of the Independent International Scientific Panel — created by the UN General Assembly last year — told the Security Council: "The dangers are real and imminent." "This council faces an unprecedented threat, one that none of its members would choose, that none can contain alone, and that does not respect the borders we defend," he said. Trump [USN:L6N45E0R5 TEXT:"told world leaders"] at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that he "rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control" AI, describing the technology as amazing but noting that the US would be careful. White House science and technology adviser Michael Kratsios echoed Trump in remarks to the UN Security Council on Wednesday. "You cannot govern technology you do not understand. This body and others like it should focus on sharing best practices to build domestic capacity, not establishing a global regulatory scheme," he said. China's UN Ambassador Fu Cong said continuous improvement of regulatory frameworks, emergency response, and cross-border cooperation on AI was needed. "It is incumbent upon the international community to work more closely together, attach equal importance to development and security, and steer AI development for the positive, for good, and for humanity," he told the Security Council. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who has long pushed for global governance of AI, has warned that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence poses risks that cannot be ignored, putting him at odds with Trump. The Security Council met for the first time on the risks of AI in 2023, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and the United States warned against its use to censor or repress people. Then-US Secretary of State Antony Blinken chaired a Security Council meeting on AI in 2024.

item.title: US Education Department panel deadlocks on ABA's law school oversight role
item.description: The American Bar Association's status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools remained in limbo on Wednesday after a US Department of Education committee failed to reach consensus on ending or renewing its role following seven hours of discussion and debate in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: The American Bar Association's status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools remained in limbo on Wednesday after a US Department of Education committee failed to reach consensus on ending or renewing its role following seven hours of discussion and debate in Washington. The 18-member committee opted to revisit the matter on Thursday after holding two deadlocked votes on whether or not to strip law school oversight functions from the attorney organization, which has been enmeshed in a series of clashes with President Donald Trump's administration. The ABA's legal education council appeared at Wednesday's hearing before the Education Department's bipartisan National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity and argued its status should be renewed. Several committee members said the accreditor was too intertwined with its parent trade organization, however, citing the ability of the larger ABA's policymaking body to weigh in on accreditation standards. Daniel Thies, the past chair of the legal education council, repeatedly countered that the council was in compliance with Education Department rules and that it has taken additional steps in recent months to become more independent. The ABA is the country's most-recognized attorney organization, with about 150,000 dues-paying members. Its legal education council, which became the government's recognized accreditor of law schools in 1952 and currently accredits 198 US schools, largely operates separately from the wider ABA. But it has drawn Trump administration criticism amid a federal crackdown on diversity, equity and inclusion policies in government, the private sector and academia. Trump signed an executive order in April 2025 [USN:L1N3R2130 TEXT:"directing"] Education Secretary Linda McMahon to assess whether to suspend or terminate the ABA as the government’s official law school accreditor, citing its “unlawful" DEI requirements. Under rules the ABA [USN:L6N4500VW TEXT:"repealed"] earlier this month, ABA-accredited schools were required to demonstrate their commitment to diversity in recruitment, admissions and student programming. Trump and the ABA have separately clashed over his [USN:L1N3SJ0SR TEXT:"executive orders"] targeting law firms and his officials’ statements criticizing judges. The US Department of Justice has [USN:L2N3QN1FS TEXT:"barred"] its attorneys from speaking at or attending ABA events and [USN:L2N3S10ZS TEXT:"curtailed"] the ABA’s longtime role in vetting judicial nominees. A White House spokesperson in 2025 [USN:L2N3PN0XV TEXT:"dismissed"] the organization as a “snooty” group of “leftist lawyers.” Even if the committee makes a recommendation Thursday, a final decision on the ABA legal education council's accreditor status is not expected for several months. The department reviews higher education accreditors every five years. AGENCY SAYS ACCREDITATION ARM NOT INDEPENDENT In an August report recommending against renewing the ABA’s accreditor status, Education Department staff concluded that the legal education council is not "separate and independent" from the larger ABA as required. The report also faulted the ABA for being too slow to revise its law school diversity rule. Melissa Hart, chair of the ABA’s legal education council, said in a statement that it has “consistently complied” with the Education Department’s requirements. The Education Department did not respond to a request for comment ahead of Wednesday's meeting. Revoking the ABA's accreditor status would disrupt federal student loan access for some law schools and could make it harder for law students to take the bar exam and become licensed attorneys in different states. Read more: [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"Trump administration moves to end attorney group's law school oversight"] [USN:L6N4500VW TEXT:"US lawyer group repeals DEI rule for law schools as accreditation decision looms"] [USN:L1N3R2130 TEXT:"Trump executive order says ABA's role as law school accreditor may be revoked"]

item.title: US Senate Democrats seek sanctions over Israeli settlements, bill says
item.description: A group of US Senate Democrats will introduce legislation on Wednesday to sanction individuals or groups that facilitate Israel's "E1 project," a widely condemned West Bank settlement plan cutting across land the Palestinians seek for a state, according to a copy of the legislation seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: A group of US Senate Democrats will introduce legislation on Wednesday to sanction individuals or groups that facilitate Israel's "E1 project," a [USN:L8N3UC0SM TEXT:"widely condemned West Bank settlement plan"] cutting across land the Palestinians seek for a state, according to a copy of the legislation seen by Reuters. The introduction of the bill is the latest sign of growing friction between Democrats in Congress and the Israeli government over its handling of the West Bank, with many in the party — and a few Republicans — calling for curbs on US military aid to Israel over its conduct of the war in Gaza. US Democratic lawmakers have also [USN:L1N44M0ZR TEXT:"recently urged"] Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to rein in violence by West Bank settlers and mass arrests of Palestinians by Israeli security forces in the occupied territory. The measure's lead sponsors are Chris Coons of Delaware, Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, Ron Wyden of Oregon and Ruben Gallego of Arizona. "As Palestinian civilians face a campaign of devastation and fear from violent extremist settlers, the United States must send a strong message that this behavior is unacceptable and that it remains committed to freedom, security, prosperity and self-determination for all Israelis and Palestinians," Coons said in a statement. The bill has at least 10 co-sponsors, all Democrats. MIDTERMS COULD SHIFT CONGRESS' ISRAEL STANCE Democrats currently control only 47 seats in the 100-member Senate, but [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"polls show they could "] win majorities in November 3 midterm elections from President Donald Trump's Republicans, who have aligned themselves closely with Netanyahu. The bill would impose sanctions on foreign companies, individuals or other entities that the Treasury Department determines to have been responsible for or complicit in the construction of any Israeli settlements or related structures in the E1 area of the West Bank, including by submitting a bid for E1 tenders. It also would sanction those who attempt to organize, direct, finance or facilitate the transfer of Israeli civilians into settlements in the E1 area. Approval of the E1 project, which would bisect the occupied West Bank and cut it off from East Jerusalem, was announced in August 2025 by Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. The two-state solution to the decades-old Israeli-Palestinian conflict envisages a Palestinian state in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza, existing side by side with Israel. Western capitals and campaign groups have opposed the E1 settlement project due to concerns that it could undermine a future peace deal with the Palestinians and diminish the chance for the two-state solution. Most of the international community considers Israeli settlements in the West Bank illegal under international law. Israel disputes this, citing historical and biblical ties to the area and saying the settlements provide strategic depth and security. Congress's lower chamber, the US House of Representatives, is currently not in session, so even in the unlikely chance of the bill's passage in the Senate, the House would not be expected to take it up before the midterms.

item.title: Meta opens Connect conference as camera-free smart glasses expected
item.description: Meta Platforms kicked off its annual Connect conference on Wednesday, where it is expected to unveil new smart glasses, including a camera-free model, amid growing privacy concerns over AI-powered devices that can record people without their consent.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) kicked off its annual Connect conference on Wednesday, where it is expected to unveil new smart glasses, including a camera-free model, amid growing privacy concerns over AI-powered devices that can record people without their consent. The social media giant is the early leader in the race to put AI devices in the hands of customers, with sales of the smart glasses it co-developed with EssilorLuxottica (ESLX.PA) surging last year to more than 7 million. That has given Meta a dominant share of a market where it mainly faces competition from Chinese companies such as RayNeo and Xiaomi (1810.HK) . But the devices' growing popularity has sparked concern globally about their ability to covertly record people, with several UK restaurants, pubs and theaters [USN:L8N44H109 TEXT:"restricting their use"]. The glasses have also drawn lawsuits, including a proposed class action in California alleging Meta misled users about privacy protections and that human annotators training its AI viewed and labeled footage of people's private moments, including changing clothes, after the recordings were uploaded to its servers. Meta, which contests the allegations and plans to defend itself, is expected to unveil the glasses without cameras in two styles, one called Clubmaster and another named Burbank, according to the Information. Analysts expect the company to also launch a new version of its Meta Ray-Ban glasses that come with cameras, as well as a thinner and lighter pair of augmented-reality glasses that reports say is code-named Phoenix. The potential Phoenix launch comes days after [USN:L4N45814C TEXT:"Snap unveiled new partnerships and software"] details about its $2,195 Specs augmented-reality glasses that launch later this year. Some analysts are, however, doubtful that removing cameras alone could allay the privacy concerns about AI devices that can still record audio. Losing the camera may also blunt demand as capturing photos and video ranks among the devices' most popular features. "Microphones and audio collection could trigger similar concerns, although likely to a lesser degree," said Linda Sui, founder of Smart Analytics Global, a market research firm. "More importantly, removing the camera from glasses that also lack a heads-up display will create a product differentiation challenge. Consumers may ask why they need smart glasses rather than Bluetooth earbuds if the primary experience is limited to voice interaction, microphones and speakers."

item.title: Trump plans grand spectacle for Xi as US says trade truce extended
item.description: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit where the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Tehran will play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit where the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Tehran will play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony. Trump and his wife greeted Xi and his wife on a 100-foot-long red carpet rolled out on the tarmac beside Xi's plane at the Maryland military base that hosts Air Force One. The greeting broke with normal protocol, marking the first time a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at Joint Base Andrews in 11 years, when President Barack Obama welcomed Pope Francis in 2015, according to C-SPAN, which tracks presidential events. The two leaders smiled, shook hands and spoke for a few minutes at the start of the Chinese leader's first trip to the US in nearly three years. A military band played, and cannons blasted ceremonial fire as they greeted each other. Trump winced as a loud B-1 military bomber flew overhead. The leaders then went their separate ways, ahead of meetings scheduled for Thursday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News that he and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng agreed to [USN:L1N45F114 TEXT:"extend a trade truce"] set to expire on November 10 by two months, through January 10. China's embassy in Washington had no immediate comment. EXPECTATIONS ARE LOW But expectations for a broader breakthrough during Xi's visit were slim. The two sides are at odds on issues ranging from Taiwan to narcotics and rare-earth minerals. People familiar with the plans said Xi was likely to forcefully raise Beijing's claim to Taiwan, a topic Washington would prefer to avoid, while Trump was likely to maintain firm US export controls despite Xi’s objections. But talks set for Thursday could nonetheless yield deals to lower tariffs in specific sectors, cooperate on drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue. Trump is expected to seek the release of some Americans and others detained in China, according to the people. The two countries could also agree to talk more on AI, where they are in fierce competition but mindful of growing dangers. The meeting comes at a difficult moment for Trump, who faces [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"falling approval numbers"] as public discontent with his war on Iran grows. Xi, while also facing challenges at home, arrives in a seemingly stronger position, with his country's trade engine [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"roaring"]. The leaders themselves may not feel they need to compromise, analysts said. "The president very much believes that over time the US economy is going to grow, the US will get stronger," said Edgard Kagan, a former White House official now with Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies. "I think when Xi Jinping sits down with Donald Trump, he very much believes the US is in hurtling decline, and that time is on China's side." STATE DINNER WITH AI CHIEFS Additional fanfare during the trip is due to include a state dinner with tech luminaries, a White House military ceremony including jet flyovers and a visit to the National Archives where the original Declaration of Independence and Constitution are housed. A state dinner on Thursday is expected to bring together chiefs of companies important in both markets like Apple's (AAPL.O) Tim Cook, Nvidia's (NVDA.O) Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman. Despite their deep disagreements, both sides pressed ahead with the summit, which analysts said seeks to project stability between the world’s biggest factory and its biggest consumer. As in their prior two meetings since 2025, the leaders are planning a highly scripted public spectacle. Instead of a joint press conference or statement at the end, the countries are expected to issue dueling announcements highlighting what each side hopes to convey to a domestic audience. For Trump, the trip caps a week of diplomacy that began with a two-day stay in New York for the [USN:L8N45C0C3 TEXT:"United Nations General Assembly"]. Nearly seven months of war with Iran have spiked energy prices in the US, and the president's Republican Party faces tough prospects in November’s congressional elections. Xi has overseen a surge in China's foreign trade but faces weak household spending and a property market downturn. Sweeping corruption and discipline crackdowns in the military have helped cement Xi’s power but also raised questions about the People's Liberation Army's readiness. Another meeting between Trump and Xi is seen as likely this year, potentially at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China in November or the Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

item.content:encoded:
中国、大型連休に大規模流動性供給　1日最大1兆元 9/23 18:57 配信

2022年9月撮影　REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

［上海　２３日　ロイター］ - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２３日、銀行システムの短期的な流動性需要に対応するため、９月２８日から１０月８日にかけて、翌日物リバースレポを通じ１日当たり最大１兆元（１４９０億ドル）供給すると発表した。

実施日や資金の借り入れコストは明らかにしなかった。中国では通常、連休前に資金需要が高まる。

中国の金融市場は国慶節で１０月１日から１０月７日まで休場。銀行間債券市場も１０月１日から７日まで休場となる。同市場のウェブサイトによると、中秋節に伴い９月２５日から２７日も休場となる。

item.title: ユーロ圏企業活動、サービスけん引し約3年ぶりの急拡大－英国は減速
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ユーロ圏の民間部門の9月の企業活動は、サービス業が予想外に改善したことを受け、約3年ぶりの大幅な拡大を示した。

S&Pグローバルが23日発表した9月のユーロ圏総合購買担当者指数（PMI）速報値は53.1と、前月の52から上昇。活動の拡大と縮小の境目を示す50を大きく上回った。ブルームバーグがまとめたエコノミスト予想では、51.7への小幅低下が見込まれていた。

域内の2大経済国であるドイツとフランスのPMIはいずれも予想を上回った。ドイツは2025年10月以来の速いペースで拡大、フランスも予想に反して拡大し、2年余りで最も高い水準となった。

S&Pグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフビジネスエコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は発表文で、「ドイツがけん引する製造業は、AIや防衛関連支出の増加に後押しされ、4年余りで最も好調な成長局面を迎えている」と指摘。「サービス業の成長にも勢いが出ており、経済成長が幅広く改善していることを示している」と述べた。

一方、英国のPMIは51.7と、前月の52.5から低下し、エコノミスト予想の52も若干下回った。

英国経済が夏場に見せた予想外に力強い成長が勢いを失い始めていることを示唆している。米国とイランの戦争が長期化する中、エネルギー市場と債券市場が新たな混乱に見舞われたことが背景にある。

バーナム英首相の下で初となる予算案の発表を控え、警戒感も強まっている。借り入れコストの上昇で、もともと乏しい政府の財政余力が一段と圧迫され、増税の可能性が高まっている。

item.description: China's state-run Global Times has laid out Beijing's case for a more predictable US-China relationship. Here's what China wants from the Xi-Trump meeting.
item.dc:creator: Raunaq Lekhi
item.content:encoded:

What China’s state media is saying ahead of Xi-Trump Summit

China's state-run Global Times has laid out Beijing's case for a more predictable US-China relationship. Here's what China wants from the Xi-Trump meeting.

Raunaq Lekhi

23 September, 2026 03:08 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Donald Trump greets Xi Jinping in Busan, South Korea, on Oct. 30, 2025. | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Chinese President Xi Jinping is in the US for a state visit that Beijing is portraying as an opportunity to put a more stable footing under its increasingly complicated relationship with Washington.

Xi, who is visiting the US from 23-25 September at the invitation of US President Donald Trump, will meet the American president just four months after Trump’s state visit to China in May. The two leaders had then agreed to work towards what they called a “constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability”.

In the past two days, China’s state-run Global Times has repeatedly returned to that phrase, describing the latest Xi-Trump meeting as an attempt to give greater predictability to ties between the world’s two largest economies.

Show Full Article

But what does Beijing appear to want from the meeting?

Stability, without ending competition The Global Times’ coverage in the run up to the meeting suggests China is not presenting stability as the end of rivalry between Beijing and Washington.

An editorial published ahead of Xi’s visit described the proposed relationship as one where cooperation remains possible alongside competition and differences. Another commentary broke the idea down into four principles: cooperation as the mainstay, competition within limits, managing differences through dialogue and maintaining peace.

That distinction is important because trade, technology and security remain major sources of friction between the two countries.

The message from Beijing, as reflected in the Global Times coverage, is therefore less about resolving every disagreement and more about preventing those disagreements from destabilising the wider relationship.

Read Here: World keeps pushing Russia, India, China together. Then RIC tears itself apart

Trade and technology are key Economic ties feature prominently in the coverage.

Chinese and US officials held economic and trade consultations ahead of Xi’s visit, discussing bilateral trade and investment as well as artificial intelligence. Global Times quoted Chinese experts as saying continued talks were necessary to implement earlier agreements and reduce trade friction

Veteran US diplomat Chas W. Freeman Jr, who served as an interpreter during former US president Richard Nixon’s 1972 China visit, told Global Times that both countries should concentrate on areas where their interests overlap.

He pointed to trade, climate change, nuclear non-proliferation and management of the global economy as areas where cooperation remains possible despite ideological and political differences. Freeman also argued that the two countries should stop trying to hold back each other’s development and instead compete by becoming more competitive themselves.

AI is another emerging area. Global Times reported that the two sides discussed AI during their latest economic consultations, while one US academic interviewed by the newspaper said cooperation on AI governance could be an area where Beijing and Washington work together.

Why keep talking when tensions remain? One argument running through the recent coverage is that regular contact itself has value.

Freeman told Global Times that losing contact could deepen mutual suspicion and eventually turn it into hostility. He argued that the two countries need to rediscover the logic behind the 1972 Shanghai Communiqué: China and the US have different political and socioeconomic systems, but can still cooperate where their interests overlap.

Global Times has also highlighted people-to-people exchanges, including American students travelling to China and Chinese and US businesses expanding into each other’s markets.

An editorial published Wednesday pointed to Chinese bubble-tea brands operating in the US and American fast-food chains expanding in China as examples of what it described as “everyday” connections between the two societies.

What could come out of the meeting? The recent Global Times coverage does not point to a single expected breakthrough. Instead, it stresses incremental progress: keeping trade relations stable, expanding practical cooperation, managing disputes and maintaining regular communication between the two governments.

That does not mean the major disagreements have disappeared. Global Times itself noted that stability does not remove the problems between Beijing and Washington, while another commentary identified Taiwan as a major underlying variable in the relationship.

The broader message from the coverage is therefore relatively straightforward: Beijing wants the Xi-Trump meeting to reinforce the framework agreed by the two leaders in May – competition without uncontrolled confrontation, cooperation where interests overlap, and dialogue when differences persist.

Whether that produces concrete agreements will depend on what Xi and Trump are able to achieve at the table.

item.title: OECD、来年の世界インフレ見通しを引き上げ－日米欧の追加利上げ予想
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 2027年のインフレ率は世界各地で予想を上回る見通しで、米国やオーストラリアなどで一段の金融引き締めが必要になるだろうと、経済協力開発機構（OECD）が予測した。

OECDは23日に発表した報告書で、中国とサウジアラビアを除く全ての20カ国・地域（Ｇ20）のインフレ率見通しについて6月の予測から引き上げ、これに金融政策で対応せざるを得なくなる可能性があると指摘した。

「エネルギー価格の新たなショックや予想以上に強い需要圧力を受け、インフレ率はすでに多くの国・地域で目標値を上回っている。基調的なインフレ圧力を持続的に抑えることが、中央銀行には求められる」とOECDは論じた。

この分析は、トランプ米大統領が引き起こした中東での戦争による経済的影響が、同氏の任期後半まで続く見通しとなったことを浮き彫りにする。

今月は既に、米連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）、欧州中央銀行（ECB）、日本銀行が相次ぎ利上げを決定した。OECD当局者はこうした引き締めが今後もあるだろうと見込む一方で、2022年のロシアによるウクライナ全面侵攻開始直後に見られたほどの積極的な政策対応には至らないとの見方を示した。

OECDは米国で年内にあと1回の利上げを予想し、ユーロ圏とオーストラリア、韓国について「さらに緩やかな利上げ」、日本は「追加利上げ」があると見込んだ。

対照的に、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）カナダ銀行は当面、金利を据え置くだろうとみている。

この見解は、市場の見方とやや食い違う。短期金融市場では、米国とユーロ圏、英国とも年内に1回の利上げが完全に織り込まれ、2回目の確率が50%前後とされている。日銀については年内1回の追加利上げにとどまり、カナダ銀行も年内1回の利上げがあるとの見方が有力だ。

OECDによると、世界経済の成長軌道は6月時点から概ね変わっていない。予測の小幅な修正が大半を占める中で、米国との貿易戦争に見舞われたカナダと、政治的に不安定となる時期が迫るフランスの見通し引き下げが目立った。

Greenland welcomes US military pact but trust still shaky

"You can't simply say: 'Okay, we’ve signed this, so now we trust you again.' Trust really needs to be rebuilt within that partnership," said a mayor in southern Greenland.

NUUK, Greenland: Greenland's government and residents expressed relief that a military pact with the United States and Denmark may end anxiety over President Donald Trump's threats to seize their Arctic island, but many remain distrustful of Washington. "I am incredibly relieved and think the outcome is very sensible. We can be satisfied," Naaja Nathanielsen, a Greenlandic MP in the Danish parliament, told Reuters. Parliament speaker Kim Kielsen urged households to raise the Greenlandic flag on Wednesday (Sep 23). Activist and influencer Orla Joelsen encouraged residents in the capital Nuuk to show up at the airport to welcome the prime minister and foreign minister back from New York, where they struck the deal. NEW US BASES The agreement allows the US to expand its military presence on Greenland, reopening Cold War-era bases in the settlements of Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, with a prospect of renewed spending and employment potential.

But it stopped short of Trump's unsettling previous demand that the US annex Greenland to head off the growing Arctic presence of Russia and China. "There has previously been a significant American presence in Greenland, so this is nothing new," added Nathanielsen. "However, in light of the unrest over the past few years, there is likely greater scepticism in Greenland, and consequently, work needs to be done to reassure the local population." The US first built military bases in Greenland during World War Two. During the Cold War, it maintained 17 military installations and more than 10,000 personnel to monitor Soviet forces. Today only Pituffik Space Base remains, with some 150 US military personnel.

Related:

Commentary: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust

CNA Explains: What does the US-Greenland security deal actually change?

RESIDENTS DIVIDED Pitanguaq Mikissen, 69, a retired ship assistant, said the potential reopening of some old US bases gave greater security to the territory's 57,000 people. But not all residents were happy. "I think that Trump is really good at creating a lot of worry and a lot of fear," said Jensia Dam-Davidsen, 40, a voice and choir teacher. "It (the deal) seems wrong in every way – especially now that Denmark has expanded their military presence here." Denmark has significantly increased its own military footprint in Greenland since Trump's threats peaked in January, deploying additional troops, boosting Arctic defence spending and hosting allies under military exercises.  Malene Vahl Rasmussen, mayor of Kujalleq municipality in southern Greenland, where the US is looking to reopen the Narsasuaq military base, said that under the agreement, US military expansion must respect the Greenlandic way of life to protect hunting and fishing. "You can't simply say, 'Okay, we’ve signed this, so now we trust you again'. Trust really needs to be rebuilt within that partnership," she told Reuters. Some Greenlanders worry that expanded military activity - including increased aircraft and vessel movement - could disrupt hunting and fishing grounds that communities rely on for a living, though the agreement states such activity must respect Greenlandic society and traditional ways of life.

Source: Reuters/rk

item.title: AI覇権争い「減速」せず、米中首脳の利害一致へ－双方に余裕なし
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領と中国の習近平国家主席は今週、貿易から台湾に至る数多くの難題について協議する。双方が一致している点が一つある。AI開発にブレーキをかける余裕は、どちらにもないということだ。

シリコンバレーではAIが人類を滅ぼす可能性を巡り論争が続いているが、米中両政府はいずれも、テクノロジー覇権争いをより懸念しているようだ。

トランプ政権も習指導部もAI開発を減速させる意向を示していない。この議論は、米アンソロピックの共同創業者ダリオ・アモデイ氏が3800語に及ぶ論考で、歯止めのない進歩の危険性を警告し、開発ペースの「減速」を求めたことで再燃した。

トランプ氏はAIの開発抑制を求める声をほぼ即座に「デマ」だと一蹴し、米国の主導的地位を維持すると表明した。中国側も開発を減速させる理由はほとんどないとみている。その一因は、差を縮めつつあるとはいえ、AI分野でなお米国に後れを取っていることに加え、米エヌビディア製先端半導体へのアクセスを巡る米国の規制に制約されているためだ。

習氏のワシントン訪問は23日に始まる。その直前、中国のアリババグループは最大10兆個のパラメーターを持つ巨大モデルを開発中だと発表した。また、中国で最も高性能だとするAI半導体を投入し、20ギガワット規模のデータセンターを建設する計画も明らかにした。ある試算によると、このデータセンター計画は1600億ドル（約25兆円）のクラウド収入につながる可能性がある。

中国のAI業界ではここ数日、動きが活発化。北京智譜華章科技（Z.AI）と小米（シャオミ）は自社のAIシステムが自ら能力を向上させる仕組みを披露し、華為技術（ファーウェイ）はエヌビディア製プロセッサーの代替を狙う高性能AI半導体の投入を前倒しした。

エージェント型AIのパイオニア、マナスは米メタ・プラットフォームズとの関係がようやく整理された後、次の事業展開に必要な資金を確保するため、評価額40億ドルで資金調達を目指した。中国当局は、いったん決まっていたメタによるマナス買収を阻止した。

KYIV: Russia pounded Kyiv with drone strikes on Wednesday (Sep 23), hitting railway infrastructure, warehouses and fuel stations, just hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met US President Donald Trump to discuss peace efforts. At least two people were killed and more than 30 were injured in the attack, which lasted for hours from the morning into early afternoon, officials said, in one of the heaviest strikes since Russia began hitting Kyiv and nearby areas with faster and high-flying jet drones that are harder to intercept. Several explosions were heard and smoke billowed above the centre of the Ukrainian capital and other areas. Zelenskyy said Russia had deployed many drones against the city, with a large number of them jet-powered.

"Russia continues to turn civilian and critical infrastructure into targets: pharmaceutical facilities, gas stations, railways, communications infrastructure, and shopping malls," he said on X. A separate Russian aerial bomb attack killed at least four people and injured four others in a village in the frontline Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, the regional governor said on the Telegram messaging app. Zelenskyy, who was due to address the UN General Assembly later on Wednesday, said it was important to keep up sanctions pressure on Moscow, including on Russian oligarchs. In his meeting with Trump on Tuesday, Zelenskiy discussed a potential bilateral ceasefire on energy-related targets and asked for increased supplies of US Patriot air defence missiles to defend against an expected Russian winter campaign against Ukraine's electricity infrastructure. No agreements were reached, he said. Zelenskiy said he was ready for "any format" of an energy ceasefire with Moscow, as long as Russia halted its own attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure. On Wednesday, the Kremlin said the grounds for future peace talks with Ukraine were still not in place and there were no plans for any high-level meetings.

A firefighter and police officers work at the site of a petrol station hit by a morning Russian drone strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Sep 23, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Valentyn Ogirenko)

PETROL STATIONS HIT "This is the view from the windows of the EU Delegation (in Kyiv) today. Buildings nearby are burning," Katarina Mathernova, the EU ambassador to Ukraine, said in a social media post. The attacks largely targeted the neighbourhood near the main railway station, which Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said had not been damaged. Ukrzaliznytsia's head Oleksandr Pertsovskyi said railway infrastructure came under attack and one of its workers had been injured. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a drone hit a nine-storey non-residential building, as well as a business centre and warehouses. Ukrainian oil company Ukrnafta said Russia hit one of its petrol stations in the capital, the sixth such facility attacked in recent weeks. In total, two petrol stations came under attack, authorities said. Reuters TV footage showed one of the heavily damaged stations on a busy highway. Energy worker Mykola Nechypurenko, one of a team repairing damage to the power network, was sceptical about the prospects for any energy ceasefire with Russia. "I don't think they'll agree on anything. As long as the war goes on, energy infrastructure remains under threat," said Nechypurenko, 55. "I don't believe it will work. Not until the war ends."

item.title: Turkey says nearly half a million investors affected by funds liquidation
item.description: Turkey's capital markets regulator said on Wednesday that almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds worth around $18 billion which authorities last week ordered to be liquidated during a market selloff.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey's capital markets regulator said on Wednesday that almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds worth around $18 billion which authorities last week [USN:L1N45907O TEXT:"ordered to be liquidated"] during a market selloff. Turkish authorities also took steps last week to support financial stability, including measures to boost lira liquidity and ease some capital and margin requirements after some funds struggled to meet withdrawals during a stock market selloff. Turkey's Capital Markets Board, or SPK, said in a statement that the number of individual investors in the funds affected was 455,758, citing central securities depository records. Meanwhile, authorities have widened an [USN:L6N45E09B TEXT:"investigation"] launched by prosecutors last week after the SPK filed criminal complaints over transactions in shares of Turkish companies Katilimevim, Gundogdu Gida and Destek Finans. Turkish media reported that five people who were detained in recent days had appeared in court on Wednesday and had been jailed pending trial. Turkey's justice ministry had no immediate comment. The ministry said in a statement on Tuesday that individuals faced charges including violating Turkey's capital markets law, membership of a criminal organisation and aggravated fraud committed by company executives or others acting on behalf of a company during commercial activities.

item.title: 英サービスＰＭＩ、9月51.7に低下 価格圧力高まる
item.description:
Andy Bruce
［２３日 ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルがまとめた９月の英国サービス部門購買担当者景気指数（Ｐ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英サービスＰＭＩ、9月51.7に低下　価格圧力高まる 9/23 17:53 配信

ロンドン中心部を6月ドローンで撮影　REUTERS/Yann Tessier

Andy Bruce

［２３日　ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルがまとめた９月の英国サービス部門購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は５１．７で、８月の５２．５から低下し、３カ月ぶりの低水準となった。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は５２．０だった。

英国経済の中核を担うサービス企業が顧客に請求する価格は、４カ月ぶりの速いペースで上昇した。イラン戦争に起因するエネルギー価格上昇でコスト圧力も強まった。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルは、調査結果を踏まえると第３・四半期の経済成長率は約０．１％で、第２・四半期の０．４％を下回ると指摘した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルのチーフビジネスエコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は「９月は、期待外れに鈍い経済成長とインフレ圧力の強まりという懸念すべき組み合わせとなっている。企業景況感の低迷と高コストが引き続き雇用を抑制している」と述べた。

「調査の価格指数の上昇は、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）がタカ派姿勢を維持する可能性を示唆する。一方で、企業活動の伸びが懸念されるほど力強さを欠くことは、借り入れコスト上昇が経済にもたらすリスクを浮き彫りにしている」と語った。

金融市場は、英中銀がヒーリー財務相の予算案発表の翌週に当たる１１月５日に利上げする確率を２２日時点でおよそ６０％織り込んでいる。

一方、製造業ＰＭＩは、国内受注の増加に支えられ、８月の５１．７から５２．０に上昇した。先行きに対する楽観度は７カ月ぶりの高水準となった。

製造業とサービス業の調査を合わせた総合ＰＭＩは５１．７で、８月の５２．５から低下した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 9/23(水) 17:53 ロイター

item.title: 日本株は連休明け上昇へ、AI株高・円安追い風－債券は日銀政策を警戒
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 日本株は5連休明けとなる24日の取引で上昇して始まる見通しだ。世界的なAI関連株の上昇再開に加え、為替の円安進行も追い風となりそうだ。一方、債券市場では金融政策を巡る不透明感を背景に、売り圧力が強まる可能性がある。

シルバーウイーク中に日経平均先物は上昇し、23日の大阪取引所の日経平均先物12月限の夜間取引終値は6万5940円と、18日の日中取引終値から1.3%上昇している。円は1ドル＝158円30銭前後と3週間ぶりの安値圏。18日の日本銀行の利上げ後、当局がレートチェックを実施したと報じられる中で円は一時上昇したものの、その後下げに転じ、長期トレンドを示す200日移動平均線（158円46銭）に接近している。

東京市場では、米国で再び勢いを増すハイテク株高をいったん織り込む展開となりそうだ。メタ・プラットフォームズの新AIエージェント「Muse（ミューズ）」の人気をきっかけにAI関連株への強気な見方が再燃し、ナスダック100指数は今週に入り3%近く上昇しており、22日には最高値を更新した。韓国総合株価指数（KOSPI）も23日、0.9%高となり、SKハイニックスやサムスン電子など半導体関連株が上昇した。これは日本の半導体製造装置株にも買いが波及する可能性がある。

円安も輸出関連株にとって追い風となりそうだ。一方、原油価格は、サウジアラビアによる主要パイプラインの再稼働への期待や、米国とイランの和平協議の進展観測を受けて下落基調が続いていたが、23日はホルムズ海峡での新たな攻撃が材料視され、大幅反発した。原油高によるインフレ懸念から同日の米国株は下落しており、日本株も買い先行後は伸び悩む可能性がある。

バンテージ・グローバル・プライムのマーケットアナリスト、ヘベ・チェン氏は、「世界的なAI株高の再燃やリスクセンチメントの緩やかな改善を背景に、日本株には出遅れを取り戻す余地がある」と指摘。一方、円安は輸出株を短期的に押し上げる可能性があるものの、政府・当局による為替介入への警戒が投資家の慎重姿勢につながると同氏はみる。

item.title: ユーロ圏総合ＰＭＩ、9月は予想外の急上昇 3年超ぶり高水準
item.description: [ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏総合ＰＭＩ、9月は予想外の急上昇　3年超ぶり高水準 9/23 17:49 配信

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は下落予想に反して５３．１に急上昇し、２０２３年４月以来の高水準を記録した。写真は６月、ドイツのベルリンの通り（２０２６年　ロイター／Fabrizio Bensch）

[ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は下落予想に反して５３．１に急上昇し、２０２３年４月以来の高水準を記録した。８月は５２．０だった。ロイターがまとめた予想では５１．７への下落が見込まれていた。ただ、企業は運営コストの急激な上昇に直面している。

ＰＭＩは５０を上回ると、経済活動の拡大を示す。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフ・ビジネス・エコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は「中東で続く紛争に端を発するエネルギー価格の上昇を考慮すれば、９月にインフレ圧力が再び高まっているのは驚くことではない。それだけに、経済成長の回復力が報告されていることは、なおさら心強い」と述べた。

ユーロ圏内貿易を含む輸出のさらなる増加に支えられ、新規受注を示す指数は全体として４年超ぶりの高水準を記録した。

９月はサービス業と製造業の両方が総合ＰＭＩの上昇に寄与した。サービス業ＰＭＩは５１．６から５３．０へと上昇し、ほぼ１年ぶりの高水準となった。予想では５１．５への小幅下落が見込まれていた。

製造業ＰＭＩは５２．７で８月から横ばいとなったが、総合ＰＭＩの構成要素である生産指数は５３．３から５３．４へとわずかに上昇した。

企業は需要の増加に対応するために従業員を増やしたが、エネルギー価格の高騰により、投入コストの急騰に直面した。企業は、その一部を顧客に転嫁することができた。

ウィリアムソン氏は「地政学的な問題や物価上昇という逆風の中でも経済成長が堅調に推移していることは、ＥＣＢが年末までに再び利上げを行う決意を強める要因となるだろう。これにより、利上げは早ければ早いほど良いという論拠がさらに強まり、１０月の利上げが現実味を帯びてくる」と分析した。

キャピタル・エコノミクスのジャック・アレンレイノルズ氏は「９月のユーロ圏総合ＰＭＩの大幅な改善は、７月の公式活動統計が弱かったにもかかわらず、第３・四半期のＧＤＰが拡大するとの当社の見方を裏付ける。産出価格ＰＭＩも上昇したが、賃金への『二次的影響』を示す兆候は依然としてない」と述べた。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は今月、エネルギー価格高騰に起因するインフレを抑制するため、今年２回目となる利上げを実施し、インフレ圧力が長期化する可能性があると警告した。市場では、来年６月末までにさらに３回の利上げが行われると見込まれている。

ＩＮＧのカーステン・ブレゼスキ氏は、「きょうのＰＭＩで、ＥＣＢ内で最もハト派的な政策担当者でさえ、追加利上げの可能性を否定することは難しくなった」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 アングル：欧州の中銀関係者、米国との協調維持に不安　市場介入に懸念 アングル：欧州の猛暑、経済損失は過去最大規模の恐れ　観光の変化で南欧に大打撃 アングル：欧州熱波、マクロ経済面からの市場注目ポイント アングル：欧州、熱波で気候変動への無防備さ露呈　「適応」対策が急務 最終更新: 9/23(水) 19:13 ロイター

item.title: 中国AI株下落、当局のDeepSeekとムーンショット調査の報道受け
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国では23日、AIモデル開発企業の株価が下落した。中国当局がデータセキュリティー上の懸念を巡り、AIスタートアップのDeepSeek（ディープシーク）とムーンショットAIに対する調査を開始したとの報道が材料となった。

米テクノロジー情報サイト「ジ・インフォメーション」の報道を受け、香港市場ではZ.AI（北京智譜華章科技）が一時13.8%下落し、12.4%安で取引を終えた。ミニマックス・グループ（稀宇科技）も4%安となった。インフォメーションによると、調査は、中国企業による米アンソロピックのAIモデル「Claude（クロード）」を介した機密データの処理を同社が指摘したことから始まった。Qwenモデルを開発するアリババグループも、4.4%下落した。

AIの安全性を巡る議論が高まる中、報道を受け、中国のAI企業に対する監視が強化される可能性があるとの投資家の懸念が強まった。トランプ米大統領と中国の習近平国家主席が、近く予定される首脳会談でAI産業を巡る合意を目指すとの観測も強まっている。

ガベカル・キャピタルのポートフォリオマネジャー、レオニード・ミロノフ氏は、投資家は中国政府が業界への監視を強めることを「恐れている」と述べた。また、規制の対象範囲がなお不透明で、中国のAIモデル開発を遅らせるリスクがあることから、投資家心理は悪化しているとの見方を示した。

中国企業は競争力を強化するため、AIモデルの開発を加速しており、ムーンショットAIは「Kimi K3」、アリババは「Qwen3.8-Max」を投入した。規制によって開発ペースが鈍化すれば、こうした進展が停滞する可能性がある。一方、OpenAIやアンソロピックなど米国の競合企業は、価格面での競争力を高めるため、製品の改良を進めている。

独自のAIモデルを持つ他の中国テクノロジー企業も同日に下落し、小米（シャオミ）は約3.8%安、テンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は約2.4%安となった。

item.title: 独総合ＰＭＩ、9月は昨年10月以来の高水準 サービス景況好転
item.description:
Maria Martinez
［ベルリン ２３日 ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが発表した９月のドイツの総合購買担...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独総合ＰＭＩ、9月は昨年10月以来の高水準　サービス景況好転 9/23 17:25 配信

フランクフルトで2023年8月撮影　REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach

Maria Martinez

［ベルリン　２３日　ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが発表した９月のドイツの総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は５３．８と、８月の５１．８から上昇し、２０２５年１０月以来の高水準となった。インフレ圧力が再び高まる中、前月まで５カ月連続で縮小していたサービス業の景況が拡大に転じた。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は、前月から横ばいの５１．８だった。

サービス部門ＰＭＩは８月の４９．７から５２．９に上昇し、７カ月ぶりの高水準となった。製造業ＰＭＩは５３．８と８月の５４．３からに低下したが、引き続き拡大圏を維持した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのエコノミクス担当アソシエートディレクター、フィル・スミス氏は 「９月調査では、回復力を示す兆候がさらに報告された。インフレ圧力が再び高まったにもかかわらず、生産の伸びが加速し、先行きへの期待が安定的に推移し、雇用も２カ月連続で増加した」と述べた。

投入コストは４カ月ぶりの速いペースで上昇し、長期平均を大きく上回った。調査対象企業は、燃料価格の上昇やエネルギーコスト全般の高まりの影響を指摘した。

item.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with drone strikes as Zelenskiy addresses the UN
item.description: Russia pounded Kyiv with drone strikes on Wednesday, hitting railway infrastructure, warehouses and fuel stations as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy warned the UN General Assembly a hard winter lay ahead.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Pavel Polityuk
item.content:encoded: Russia pounded Kyiv with drone strikes on Wednesday, hitting railway infrastructure, warehouses and fuel stations as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy warned the UN General Assembly a hard winter lay ahead. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were killed and 45 were injured, two of them in serious condition. The attack lasted from morning into the evening in one of the heaviest strikes since Russia began hitting Kyiv and nearby areas with faster and high-flying jet drones that are [USN:L8N45D0YY TEXT:"harder to intercept"]. Klitschko said a drone hit a nine-storey non-residential building, as well as a business centre and warehouses. Several explosions were heard and smoke billowed above the centre of the Ukrainian capital and other areas. Zelenskiy said Russia had deployed many drones against the city, with a large number of them jet-powered. "Russia continues to turn civilian and critical infrastructure into targets: pharmaceutical facilities, gas stations, railways, communications infrastructure, and shopping malls," he said on X. In eastern Ukraine, on the frontline of the 4-1/2-year-old war, a Russian aerial bomb attack killed five people and injured six in the village of Oleksandrivka, Regional Governor Vadym Filashkin said. He said seven people were trapped beneath rubble. The village is near Kramatorsk, one of Ukraine's "fortress cities" that Russia is seeking to capture. Zelenskiy, who discussed the prospects for a settlement with US President Donald Trump on Tuesday, [USN:L1N45F0LJ TEXT:"told"] the UN General Assembly that Ukraine would strike back and make the coming winter deeply painful for Russia if the two sides cannot agree a truce on energy attacks before the cold sets in. He said it was important to keep up sanctions pressure on Moscow, including on [USN:L8N45E127 TEXT:"Russian oligarchs"]. In his meeting with Trump, Zelenskiy discussed a [USN:L8N45E0JN TEXT:"potential bilateral ceasefire"] on energy-related targets and asked for increased supplies of US Patriot air defence missiles to defend against an expected Russian winter campaign against Ukraine's electricity infrastructure. No agreements were reached, he said. Zelenskiy said he was ready for "any format" of an energy ceasefire with Moscow, as long as Russia halted its own attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure. On Wednesday, the Kremlin said the grounds for future peace talks with Ukraine [USN:R4N45101G TEXT:"were still not in place"]. After talks between Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York, a Russian Foreign Ministry statement said Moscow "reaffirmed its unconditional commitment to achieving the objectives of its special military operation," as Russia describes its war in Ukraine. PETROL STATIONS HIT "This is the view from the windows of the EU Delegation (in Kyiv) today. Buildings nearby are burning," Katarina Mathernova, the EU ambassador to Ukraine, said in a social media post. The attacks largely targeted the neighbourhood near the main railway station, which Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said had not been damaged. Ukrzaliznytsia's head Oleksandr Pertsovskyi said rail infrastructure came under attack. One worker had been injured. Ukrainian oil company Ukrnafta said Russia hit one of its petrol stations in the capital, the sixth such facility attacked in recent weeks. In total, two petrol stations came under attack, authorities said. Reuters TV footage showed one of the heavily damaged stations on a busy highway.

item.title: ＯＥＣＤ、26年世界成長予測2.9％に引き上げ ＡＩ投資が下支え
item.description:
Leigh Thomas
[パリ ２３日 ロイター] - 経済協力開発機構（ＯＥＣＤ）は２３日発表した経済見通しで、今...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＯＥＣＤ、26年世界成長予測2.9％に引き上げ　ＡＩ投資が下支え 9/23 17:08 配信

パリのＯＥＣＤ本部。3月撮影　REUTERS/Abdul Saboor

Leigh Thomas

[パリ ２３日 ロイター] - 経済協力開発機構（ＯＥＣＤ）は２３日発表した経済見通しで、今年の世界経済は人工知能（ＡＩ）主導の投資を背景に、予想より若干よく持ちこたえているとの見方を示した。ただ、エネルギーショックの影響が根強くなっており、来年の見通しの重しになっていると指摘した。

ＯＥＣＤは２０２６年の世界経済成長率が２．９％と、前年の３．４％から減速すると予測。６月時点の見通し（２．８％）からは小幅に上方修正した。

２７年にかけては、中東紛争によるコモディティー（商品）価格ショックが景気の勢いを損ない、世界の成長率は３．０％への回復にとどまると予想。６月時点の３．１％から下方修正した。

ＯＥＣＤは、データセンターや半導体などＡＩインフラへの旺盛な投資が今年の底堅さを支える柱になっていると指摘。米国の成長を押し上げるとともに、日本や韓国のテクノロジー輸出を伸ばしているとした。

一方で、エネルギー市場の動揺、強力なエルニーニョ現象に関連した異常気象、国債利回りの急上昇、期待外れのＡＩ投資収益などの潜在的要因により、世界経済の見通しは特に不透明感が強いと警告。

これらのリスクが現実となった場合、２７年の世界成長率を合計０．７％ポイント押し下げ、世界のインフレ率を１．１％ポイント押し上げる可能性があると試算した。

ＯＥＣＤのベースライン見通しでは、２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）の２６年インフレ率は４．１％と、６月時点の４．０％から上方修正された。２７年の見通しも６月時点の３．１％から３．６％に引き上げた。物価圧力が広範に及んだり成長が鈍化したりすれば、中央銀行が金利調整を迫られる可能性があるとした。

米国の成長率見通しは２６年が２．２％、２７年が２．１％と見込み、いずれも６月時点から上方修正した。ＡＩ関連の大規模投資が個人消費の減速を相殺するとみている。米国のインフレ率は２６年に３．６％に達し、２７年には２．６％に鈍化すると予測。関税とエネルギー価格の上昇が家計の購買力と企業コストの重しになるとした。

中国の成長率は２６年に４．５％、２７年に４．２％へと減速すると予想し、いずれも６月時点から据え置いた。中国政府による過剰生産能力抑制策が投資に重しとなるほか、消費はインフレ率の緩やかな上昇に直面するとした。

ユーロ圏の成長率は２６年、２７年ともに１．０％を維持する見通し。新たな防衛支出計画が景気を下支えする前に、エネルギー価格と金利の上昇が経済活動を圧迫する見込みだ。

日本の成長率は２６年が０．８％、２７年が０．７％と予測。政策金利の上昇とエネルギー輸入コストの増大が、堅調な設備投資を相殺するとした。労働市場の逼迫と力強い賃金上昇を反映し、インフレ率は２６年の１．８％から２７年には２．６％に加速すると見込んだ。

カナダの２６年成長率見通しは６月時点の１．２％から０．９％に下方修正し、２７年見通しも１．７％から１．３％に引き下げた。米国がカナダからの輸出品に新たな関税を課したことを踏まえた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず コラム：ＡＩで相互依存強める新興企業と巨大ＩＴ コラム：ＡＩ企業の膨らむコスト負担、高品質データで争奪戦 最終更新: 9/23(水) 17:08 ロイター

item.title: UK media regulator investigates Pornhub over age checks
item.description: Britain's media regulator Ofcom said on Wednesday it had opened an investigation into whether adult content platform Pornhub has complied with its legal duties to prevent children from seeing pornography.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's media regulator Ofcom said on Wednesday it had opened an investigation into whether adult content platform Pornhub has complied with its legal duties to prevent children from seeing pornography. Under Britain's Online Safety Act, platforms are required to put in place [USN:L8N3TS0XJ TEXT:"age checks"] to prevent under-18s accessing pornographic content. Aylo, the service provider of Pornhub, said in May that Pornhub would rely on iPhone maker Apple's age-verification process to verify that users are over 18. Ofcom said it was "concerned that Aylo may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing before implementing its new age assurance process". "Our investigation will not make a determination on how Apple operates its age checks," Ofcom said in a statement. Alex Kekesi, Aylo's vice president brand and community, said in a statement that Aylo would fully cooperate with Ofcom and that the investigation would show Apple's "device-level age-verification update ... offers one of the strongest and hardest to circumvent protections currently available". Ofcom has the power to fine a business up to £18 million ($23.93 million) or 10% of its qualifying worldwide revenue, or block non-compliant sites. It has already [USN:S8N3XT0DE TEXT:"levied fines"] on adult content platforms totalling more than £1 million over age check failures. ($1 = 0.7521 pounds)

item.title: UK's Pollen Street says exploring options, in talks about possible sale
item.description: Pollen Street said on Wednesday it is exploring strategic options, including a take-private transaction and had begun preliminary talks with a limited number of parties about making a possible offer for the private capital firm.
item.dc:creator: Amy-Jo Crowley, Anousha Sakoui
item.content:encoded: Pollen Street (POLNP.L) said on Wednesday it is exploring strategic options, including a take-private transaction and had begun preliminary talks with a limited number of parties about making a possible offer for the private capital firm. London-listed Pollen Street issued a statement after Reuters reported it was working on options with an adviser as it seeks to gain asset management scale. Pollen Street's shares rose as much as 16.6% to 950p, their highest level since January. Pollen Street, which has £8.4 billion ($11.22 billion) of assets under management across private equity and private credit strategies, did not name the parties it was speaking to. Reuters reported that potential buyers include mid-sized private equity firms as well as existing shareholder Wafra, which bought a minority stake in the business in 2020 through its investment platform Capital Constellation. Wafra declined to comment. Consolidation pressure is building across the asset management sector as mid-sized firms increasingly seek scale to compete for investor capital and absorb rising regulatory and operating costs. US asset manager Nuveen earlier this year [USN:L1N3Z80BE TEXT:"bought"] Britain's Schroders (SDR.L) in a £9.9 billion deal. At Tuesday's close, shares in Pollen Street were down around 12% for the year but the rally on Wednesday brought the year-to-date return to 1.1%. Formed from the combination in 2022 of Honeycomb Investment Trust and its longstanding manager, Pollen Street Capital, the company's investments include stakes in financial services providers such as insurer Markerstudy, UK challenger bank Shawbrook (SHAW.L) and Dutch digital lender bunq. ($1 = 0.7485 pounds)

Economic activity regains momentum in September after slump, survey shows

Indian economy proved more resilient than expected to a war-led energy shock, expanding 7.8% last quarter as household consumption & business investment-powered growth.

Anup Roy

23 September, 2026 01:10 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Market stalls in Mumbai, India. Photographer: Abeer Khan/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

India’s economic activity accelerated in September, regaining momentum after slowing in recent months as manufacturing climbed to seven-month high and services picked up pace, a flash survey by HSBC Holdings Plc showed Wednesday.

The services purchasing managers’ index rose to 55.8 from 54.1 in August, while the manufacturing purchasing managers’ climbed rose to 55.7 from 52.8 last month. That left the composite index at 56.5, compared with 54.3 in August.

The indexes, which provide an early gauge of private-sector activity, are based on preliminary survey responses and may be revised when final PMI figures are released next month. A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while one below that level signals contraction.

Show Full Article

“Output growth ticked higher at both manufacturing and services companies, with goods producers leading the latest upturn. Aggregate new orders also rose at a quicker pace, prompting a solid expansion in jobs,” HSBC said in a statement. With the expansion in place, the composite index “was back above its long-run average,” it said.

Bond yields and rupee, however, stayed unchanged after the reading.

India’s economy proved more resilient than expected to a war-led energy shock, expanding 7.8% last quarter as household consumption and business investment powered growth. India, the world’s third-largest oil importer, remains vulnerable to elevated energy costs and supply disruptions that can weigh on domestic activity.

“Renewed tensions in the Middle East have once again led firms to build buffers to manage the uncertainties,” said Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC.

Brent crude is hovering around $100 a barrel. However, the government hasn’t raised pump prices since May, insulating the economy from volatile energy prices for now.

Still, price pressures are building. Figures last week showed India’s inflation accelerated in August, moving closer to the top of the central bank’s 2%-6% target range and potentially narrowing the scope for policymakers to remain on hold for long.

Most economists expect the Reserve Bank to raise interest rates on Oct. 7. The central bank has stayed on hold so far this year.

item.content:encoded:

Trump says AI is now ‘super intelligence’. Why the new name matters

Trump wants to replace 'artificial intelligence' with 'super intelligence'. But the term already has a specific meaning in the tech world.

Raunaq Lekhi

23 September, 2026 01:06 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

US President Donald Trump speaks during the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, US, on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026. The theme of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly is "Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all." | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: US President Donald Trump wants to replace the term “artificial intelligence” with “super intelligence”, saying the word “artificial” makes the technology sound fake.

Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, Trump said US government documents would henceforth use “super intelligence” or “SI” instead of artificial intelligence, and suggested other countries to follow suit.

The proposed name, however, is unlikely to change how researchers or the industry understand the technology. In fact, “super intelligence” already has a specific meaning in discussions about the future of AI.

Show Full Article

What does ‘super intelligence’ actually mean? Artificial intelligence is a broad term for computer systems capable of performing tasks associated with human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognising patterns, generating content and solving problems.

“Super intelligence” means something much more specific.

The term is generally used to describe a hypothetical form of AI whose intellectual abilities surpass those of humans across a wide range of areas. It is associated with discussions about AI systems that could potentially reason, learn and solve problems at a level beyond human capability.

That is different from simply giving today’s AI systems a new name.

Researchers have therefore questioned Trump’s use of “super intelligence” to describe existing AI. Experts cited by the BBC said the term is generally reserved for a much more advanced stage of AI, which does not currently exist.

In other words, “super intelligence” is not simply a more accurate synonym for artificial intelligence. It describes a possible future development of the technology.

Read Here: Xi unlikely to take along any CEOs to US summit with Trump

Why does Trump want to rename AI? Trump’s argument is largely about the word “artificial”. He has said it makes intelligence “sound fake”, while arguing that the technology is real and increasingly capable.

The proposed change also fits into his broader approach to AI. Last week, Trump announced plans for an “AI Force” and said he would name an “AI czar” to oversee the industry. He has also pushed back against calls for tighter controls on AI, arguing that the US cannot afford to slow development while competing with China.

At the UN, Trump said the US would not “stifle the growth” of AI, which he described as a technology that could become bigger than the Industrial Revolution. He also dismissed warnings about AI posing an existential threat to humanity as a “hoax”.

His administration’s proposed terminology, however, does not change what AI is.

What other names were considered? Trump had floated several alternatives on his Truth Social platform before settling on “super intelligence”.

Among the names discussed were “superior intelligence”, “extreme intelligence” and “supreme intelligence”. He later used polls on Truth Social to ask followers to weigh in, with “super intelligence” emerging as his preferred choice.

The terminology has already begun appearing among some people in Trump’s orbit, even as its adoption by the wider technology industry remains uncertain.

The proposed change has also drawn a degree of scepticism outside the US. Canadian AI minister Evan Solomon, when asked about the new name, joked that Canadians were “not enthusiastic” about renaming things, in an apparent reference to Trump’s earlier attempts to rename geographical features.

Will AI actually become ‘SI’? For now, there is little indication that the technology industry is preparing to abandon the term AI.

The phrase “artificial intelligence” has been used for decades and covers a vast range of systems, from recommendation algorithms and chatbots to increasingly capable generative AI models.

“Super intelligence”, meanwhile, remains largely a theoretical concept. Using it for existing systems could therefore blur the distinction between what current AI can do and what researchers believe future systems could potentially achieve.

Whether “SI” becomes part of everyday technology language will depend not only on US government documents but also on whether researchers, companies, and the public begin using it. For now, the industry continues to call it AI.

item.title: Rivian recalls about 100,700 vehicles over rearview camera display issue
item.description: Electric vehicle maker Rivian Automotive said on Wednesday it is recalling about 100,700 vehicles, representing a majority of its vehicles produced to date, over a software issue that can obstruct the rearview camera display.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Electric vehicle maker Rivian Automotive (RIVN.O) said on Wednesday it is recalling about 100,700 vehicles, representing a majority of its vehicles produced to date, over a software issue that can obstruct the rearview camera display. Here are some more details: The recall covers certain 2022-2026 R1T pickup trucks, 2022-2027 R1S SUVs and 2027 R2 models, Rivian said. The issue is a non-compliance matter involving US and Canadian rear-visibility safety standards. In an emailed statement, the EV maker told Reuters that, in rare instances when stability control is off, "a safety prompt asking to re-enable stability control may overlap the rearview camera view when shifting into reverse until the vehicle moves." More than 95% of the affected vehicles have already received a software fix, the company said, adding that all vehicles produced after August 10 already include the updated software.

item.description:
Nancy Lapid
[２２日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックと医療情報プラットフォームの...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE-アンソロピック、医療ＡＩ普及へ提携　中低所得国に提供 9/23 14:10 配信

写真はアンソロピックのロゴ。２０２６年６月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Nancy Lapid

[２２日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックと医療情報プラットフォームのオープンエビデンスは２２日、ＡＩを活用した臨床意思決定支援ツールを中低所得国の医師に提供するため提携すると発表した。

オープンエビデンスは査読済みの医学研究や治療ガイドラインを基に医師の質問に回答するサービス。米国と欧州の臨床医は無料で利用できる。

新たな取り組みでは、医学文献や専門家の知見、継続的医学教育へのアクセスが限られ患者ケアに支障が出かねない数十の中低所得国で医療従事者に特化版を無償で提供する。

オープンエビデンスが示したリストによると、この取り組みはウガンダ、アンゴラ、スーダン、ハイチ、モンゴルなど約１００カ国で展開する。

両社によると、アンソロピックの技術がバックエンドの基盤を提供し、オープンエビデンスが医療インフラを踏まえて地域ごとにシステムを最適化する。

提携に関する金銭面の条件は明らかにしていない。

ロイターは先週、アンソロピックがＡＩ技術を応用した医薬品開発の本格化に向け、生物学の研究を行うための研究所を設立したと報じた。

item.title: トランプ氏が習氏を「熱烈」歓迎へ、AI巡る米中対立隠す－24日に会談
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は中国の習近平国家主席を国賓としてワシントンに迎える。世界1、2位の経済大国が長年対立してきた問題で打開が期待されるというより、盛大な儀礼に重点を置いた習氏受け入れとなりそうだ。

トランプ氏は米東部時間23日午後6時（日本時間24日午前7時）、習氏と妻で元軍所属の歌手、彭麗媛氏をアンドルーズ統合基地で歓迎する式典に参加する。米国の大統領が中国国家主席を米国の空港の駐機場で出迎えるのは、極めて異例だ。

24日には貿易や台湾など難しい問題を巡り首脳会談が行われ、現在のトランプ政権で2回目となる国賓を迎えての夕食会も開かれる。米中首脳は25日に別れのあいさつを交わす。

習氏のワシントン訪問は2015年以来。米中双方とも、大きな進展への期待や対立の激化懸念を抑えている。20日にニューヨークで行われた2国間協議は前向きだったと評価されたが、11月に期限を迎える関税休戦の延長では合意に至らなかった。

ワシントンの戦略国際問題研究所（CSIS）に所属し、アジアで勤務経験のある元米外交官エドガード・ケーガン氏は、「今回の訪米そのものがメッセージだ」と指摘。「ホワイトハウス、中国のいずれからも習氏訪米の主要目標を示すシグナルが驚くほど出ていない。両国の関係を管理することが非常に大きな目的だという位置付けだと思う」と述べた。

会談を円滑に進めたい意向を示すかのように、トランプ氏は国連総会での22日の演説で、中国を名指ししたのは1回だけだった。高市早苗首相との日米首脳会談では、習氏の訪米について協議した。

米国は熱烈な歓迎ぶりで友好ムードを演出するが、水面下では亀裂が残っており、中国によるレアアース（希土類）支配からの脱却を急いでいる。ベッセント米財務長官はAIを巡り、「中国が勝てば、その先に明日はない」と警告している。

中国側は、米国による台湾への140億ドル（約2兆2000億円）規模の武器供与計画を阻止することに重点を置いている。習氏が総書記として率いる中国共産党は、台湾を統治したことはないが、台湾を自国領土の一部だと主張している。

item.title: Countries still way behind on UN biodiversity targets, research shows
item.description: Governments are set to fall well short of meeting a major UN target to protect and conserve biodiversity in at least 30% of the world's land and seas by 2030, research published on Wednesday showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Governments are set to fall well short of meeting a major UN target to protect and conserve biodiversity in at least 30% of the world's land and seas by 2030, research published on Wednesday showed. As part of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework [USN:L1N33A21M TEXT:"agreed in late 2022"], nearly 200 countries signed on to the "30 by 30" goal and pledged to mobilise at least $200 billion a year to reverse decades of biodiversity loss. But while another 1.3 million sq km of land and 6 million sq km of marine areas have come under formal protection since the agreement went into effect, total coverage is still only 20% and 10% respectively, according to research by several environmental groups led by the US-based Campaign for Nature and Together for the Ocean. The findings are in line with an official progress report due to be submitted to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity conference in Yerevan, Armenia, next month. A draft released in July warned that none of the 23 goals in the agreement would be reached by 2030 "unless collective implementation accelerates rapidly". "Progress is being made clearly, but it is uneven, and it is clearly also not at the pace and scale required to achieve the Framework's 23 targets by 2030," Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the UNCBD, said at a briefing this month. The Wednesday report said around 26% of terrestrial and inland water areas would be protected if all existing government pledges were fulfilled by 2030, but only 12% of marine ecosystems would be covered. The annual funding shortfall is approximately $75 billion to $150 billion, with spending on marine protection standing at just $1.8 billion, well below the $16 billion required, it said. Even if the "30x30" targets were achieved, more efforts were needed to ensure that ecosystems were genuinely protected, it said, noting that of the 10% of the ocean currently covered by protection plans, only 3.5% was considered "effectively" protected. "There's a significant gap between protection on paper and protection in practice. A line on a map does not mean protection in the water," said Pauli Merriman, senior director for oceans at WWF International. (This story has been corrected to change the figure to 12%, not 13%, in paragraph 7, and to add the name of the NGO in paragraph 3.)

item.title: Jim Ratcliffe: Billionaire Tax Exile Is Making One Valid Point About Britain
item.description: Billionaire Jim Ratcliffe suggests Manchester United Plc is an example of how to run Britain better. And the response from many has been: Who’s he to tell the UK what to do? Ratcliffe is a tax exile with a fortune derived from fossil fuels and some ugly views on immigration. Nor are Man Utd fans a happy bunch. But ignore all that and he has a simple point worth heeding. Whether in business or government, sometimes you have to cut costs.

item.title: 千葉県と神奈川県での死者9人に、ENEOSでは油が海上流出－台風25号
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 千葉県と神奈川県は23日、台風25号による死者を新たにそれぞれ1人確認したと発表した。両県での死者数は計9人になった。行方不明者は計4人おり、住宅にも多くの被害が出た。

発表によると、千葉では6人、神奈川では3人の死亡が確認された。消防庁によると、宮崎県でも1人が死亡したという。千葉・神奈川では30以上の住宅が全半壊した他、床上浸水なども相次いだ。千葉では国道などが冠水し、多くの主要道が通行止めとなった。

国土交通省の発表によると、ENEOSホールディングス傘下のENEOSで21日、根岸製油所（横浜市磯子区）から油が海上に流出した。ENEOSが対応を行っており、その後の流出はないとしている。

16日に発生した台風25号は19日に小笠原諸島に接近し、21日には関東地方に接近した。東京都大島町に一時、レベル5の土砂災害特別警報が発表されたほか、関東地方などにも土砂災害や大雨の警報が出された。

item.title: ソフトバンクG大型ジャンク債、提示条件が改善－高利回りに強い需要
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ソフトバンクグループは、過去最大級となるジャンク債（投資不適格級債）の発行に向けて条件調整を進めている。孫正義氏が掲げる大規模なAI投資の資金を確保するため、同社として過去最高水準の利回りを提示している。

ドル建てとユーロ建てを合わせた発行額は110億ドル（約1兆7400億円）超となり、ブルームバーグの集計によると、ソフトバンクGはジャンク債発行体として世界最大となる見通しだ。引き合いは強く、一部年限では発行条件レンジが当初想定より改善した。一方で、調達コストはなお過去の起債時をおおむね上回る水準となっている。23日に注文の受け付けを締め切る見通しだ。

今回の起債は、AI開発が急速に進む一方で、技術のリスクや規制の必要性を巡る警戒も強まる中、債券投資家がAI投資の資金調達をどう評価するかを占う試金石とみられている。ソフトバンクGは今年、ChatGPTを手掛けるOpenAIへの650億ドル近い投資や、AI分野での追加のM&Aを賄うため、債券市場で積極的に資金を調達してきた。

アジア時間23日午後遅くの時点で、100億ドルのドル建て部分に対する注文は300億ドルを超えたと、事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

強い需要を受け、一部の短めの年限では、提示利回りを当初想定していた水準から引き下げる余地が生じたという。関係者はいずれも、非公開情報だとして匿名を条件に話した。

10億ドルの3.5年債は利回り8.625%となる見通し。45億ドルの5.5年債は9.25－9.375%、45億ドルの7.5年債は9.75－9.875%の水準で条件調整が進められているという。

これらの水準で条件が決まれば、同年限のソフトバンクGのドル建て債として過去最高の利回りとなる見通しだ。ユーロ建て債でも過去最高水準の利回りが見込まれている。4年債は当初の約7.5%から7.125%に引き下げられ、6年債も当初の8.25－8.5%から8%に引き下げられた。

item.title: ソフトバンクG、ジャンク債大型発行で過去最高の利回り提示－関係者
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ソフトバンクグループは、ジャンク（投資不適格）級社債市場で過去最大級となる見通しの高利回り債の発行に乗り出した。AIへの大規模投資に必要な資金を集めようと、過去最高の利回りを提示している。

世界有数のAI投資家であるソフトバンクGは、複数の年限および通貨から成る社債のマーケティングを開始。発行条件を巡る協議も進めている。非公開協議だとして匿名を条件に事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

同社はドル建て債100億ドル（約1兆5800億円）とユーロ建て債10億ユーロ（約1800億円）を含む今回の起債で、110億ドルを超える相当額の調達を目指している。

この社債発行は、「ChatGPT」を開発した米OpenAIへの約650億ドルに迫る投資コミットメントや、AI分野でのさらなる企業の合併・買収（M&A）に必要な資金を確保することが目的。ソフトバンクGは今年に入り起債を活発化させ、借り入れを原資とするAI投資の中心的存在となった。

AIテクノロジーへの期待は世界の投資家を引き付ける一方、業界を巡る安全性への懸念も強まっている。

関係者によると、ソフトバンクGは10億ドルの期間3.5年の社債について8.75%－8.875%、45億ドルの5.5年債に9.375%－9.5%、45億ドルの7.5年債に9.75%－9.875%の利回りを投資家に提示している。ブルームバーグがまとめたデータによると、ソフトバンクGが発行するドル建て債として、それぞれの年限で利回りはいずれも過去最高の水準となる。

アジア時間の23日午後遅くの時点で、ドル建て部分に対する注文は300億ドルを超えたと、事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

ユーロ建てについては、4年物が7.5%前後、6年物が8.25%－8.5%の利回りが提示されている。4年債利回りは過去最高かそれに近い水準で、6年債は過去最高となる。

ソフトバンクGだけが資金調達のため市場を積極的に活用しているわけではない。ゴールドマン・サックス・グループのクレジットストラテジストらがまとめた最近のリポートによると、2026年の世界AI関連債発行額はすでに5750億ドルを超えている。

item.title: US stocks fall as 10-year Treasury yield hits highest since 2007
item.description: US shares fell and benchmark 10-year Treasury yields climbed to their highest level since 2007 on Wednesday, after data showed US business activity racing to a more-than-five-year high in September, fueled by a surge in new orders.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: US shares fell and benchmark 10-year Treasury yields climbed to their highest level since 2007 on Wednesday, after data showed US business activity racing to a more-than-five-year high in September, fueled by a surge in new orders. S&P Global said on Wednesday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month, the [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"highest level"] since July 2021. "They're painting a picture of the economy not just being resilient, but overheating, and in that sense, robust economic growth is no longer balanced, it's adding to inflationary pressures,” said Will Compernolle, macro strategist at FHN Financial. Yields have climbed to multi-year highs as traders price in the likelihood of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, with inflation remaining stubbornly above the central bank's 2% annual target. Interest rate-sensitive 2-year Treasury yields rose 11.4 basis points to 4.891%, after rising as high as 4.947%, the highest since May 2024. The benchmark 10-year yield jumped 13.89 basis points to 5.106%, the highest since 2007 and its biggest one-day increase since April 2025. Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a 66% chance of an October rate hike, up from 53% earlier in the day. Adding to the hawkish tone, Fed Governor Michael Barr said that the central bank took an important step last week to "recalibrate" short-term borrowing costs to bring down inflation, and signaled that [USN:S0N4490DT TEXT:"further rate hikes"] will likely be needed. A break through key technical levels amplified the rise in rates, analysts said. "It looks like for now the technical boundaries that had kept a lid on yields for the last few weeks are just broken, and once this momentum starts it can make traders very hesitant to step in front of it,” Compernolle said. The US Treasury Department also drew very weak demand for a $70 billion 5-year note auction amid the bond market selloff, with the notes selling at the highest yield at an auction since 2007. Stocks slid as yields climbed. Higher rates can weigh on equities both by raising the cost of financing corporate investment and by luring buyers back into the bond market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 0.68% and the S&P 500 (.SPX) dropped 0.75%. The Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) was down 1.13%, a sharp reversal after hitting a record high on Tuesday. The pan-European STOXX 600 index (.STOXX) slid 0.44% and an MSCI index of global stocks (.MIWD00000PUS) fell 0.73%, snapping four consecutive days of gains. GEOPOLITICS IN FOCUS Sentiment was further dampened by comments from Iranian leaders on Wednesday, underscoring that the US and Iran [USN:L1N45F09P TEXT:"remain far apart"] on reaching a peace deal. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that diplomacy must continue even as the two sides remain divided on how to end the war, after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never bow to US pressure. President Donald Trump, addressing the same forum on Tuesday, threatened to "annihilate" Iran but also said his envoys had [USN:L8N45E0CI TEXT:"held productive talks"] with mediators seeking to end the conflict. "We've been through a series of starts and stops like this," said Cole Smead, CEO and portfolio manager at Smead Capital Management. "We're in a pretty momentum-dominated market. I don't think most people feel comfortable stepping in the way of headlines." US crude rose 2.3% to $92.60 a barrel and Brent rose to $103.50 per barrel, up 4.28% on the day. Investors are also looking ahead to a [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"summit"] between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, where tensions over trade, technology and Tehran are expected to play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony. DOLLAR GAINS The prospect of higher rates helped to boost the dollar to multi-week highs versus the euro, sterling and the Canadian dollar. The euro dropped 0.55% to $1.1384 and had reached $1.1367, the lowest since July 28. The dollar was 0.61% firmer against the yen at 158.33 , with speculators wary of drawing more Japanese intervention on any push past 160.00. Spot gold fell 1.64% to $4,283.40 an ounce.
